Although the mechanisms of inducting autoimmunity by some of the infectious agents have been investigated, there is not yet enough research on streptococcal infections.MATERIAL/

A cross sectional study of 38 patients fulfilling the classification criteria for SLE. The patients visited a rheumatology outpatient clinic in Switzerland between January 2002 and December 2004. The last assessment during this period was used for the study. The assessment included, besides demographic data, the measurement of disease activity using the BILAG index, the measurement of disease damage using the SLICC/ACR damage index (SDI (slicc/acr damage index)), as well as the patient's self assessed health status using the patient's questionnaire Medical Outcome Survey Short Form 36 (SF-36).

Sulfasalazine is a widely used anti-inflammatory agent in the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease and several rheumatological disorders. Although as many as 20% of treated patients may experience reversible, dose-dependent side effects, less frequent but potentially severe, systemic reactions have also been reported.

Celiac disease (CD (celiac disease)) is believed to be a permanent intolerance to gluten. A number of patients, however, discontinue the gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)) without developing symptoms or signs. The aim of our study was to investigate whether CD (celiac disease) patients are capable of developing tolerance to gluten.
results.reference: Granulomatous myelotoxicity and enteritis developed in a 21 year old female within 3 weeks of initiating sulfasalazine for rheumatoid arthritis. Following a short course of corticosteroids, the patient had resolution of her cholestatic hepatitis, rash, eosinophilia, and gastrointestinal symptoms with no residual manifestations at 7 months follow-up. Although severe reactions to sulfasalazine are rare and unpredictable, practicing physicians should be aware of unusual clinical presentations of toxicity when prescribing sulfasalazine.

results.question: Is Chaalia/Pan Masala harmful for health?
rewritten: Is the consumption of Chaalia and Pan Masala associated with adverse health effects or increased risk of systemic diseases?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that a high percentage of children using Chaalia and Pan Masala consider these substances harmful to health (96% for Chaalia and 60% for Pan Masala). Additionally, knowledge about established harmful effects was reported as variable but generally high among users. This suggests that Chaalia and Pan Masala are recognized as harmful substances by the studied population.

yes
contexts: To determine the practices and knowledge of harmful effects regarding use of Chaalia and Pan Masala in three schools of Mahmoodabad and Chanesar Goth, Jamshed Town, Karachi, Pakistan.

A total of 370 students were interviewed over a period of six weeks, of which 205 (55.4%) were boys. The ages of the students were between 10 and 15 years. Thirty one percent of the fathers and 62% of the mothers were uneducated. The frequency of use of any brand of Chaalia was found to be 94% and that of Pan Masala was 73.8%. Eighty five percent of them were regular users. A large majority (88%) procured the substances themselves from near their homes. Ninety five percent of the children had friends with the same habits. Eighty four percent were using the substances in full knowledge of their families. Chaalia was considered harmful for health by 96% and Pan Masala by 60%. Good taste was cited as a reason for continuing the habit by 88.5% of the children and use by friends by 57%. Knowledge about established harmful effects was variable. Knowledge about harmful effects was high in both "daily" and "less than daily users".

To achieve the objective a cross-sectional design was used in three government schools of Mahmoodabad and Chanesar Goth, Jamshed Town, Karachi. Students of either gender drawn from these schools fulfilling the inclusion and exclusion criteria were interviewed using a pre-coded structured questionnaire. Along with demographic data, questions regarding frequency of Chaalia and Pan Masala use, practices of this habit in friends and family and place of procurement of these substances, were inquired. Knowledge was assessed about harmful effects and its source of information. In addition, practices in relation to that knowledge were assessed.

A severe systemic reaction to sulfasalazine developed in a 21-year old female with rheumatoid arthritis characterized by eosinophilia, granulomatous enteritis and myelotoxicity, cholestatic hepatitis, and seizures. The clinical course and management of this patient are presented as well as a review of the incidence and outcome of severe systemic reactions to sulfasalazine.

Automated, tailored prompts highlighting familial risk for heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and breast, colorectal, or ovarian cancer were implemented during 2011 to 2012. Medical records of a cohort of community-based primary care patients, aged 35 to 65 years, who previously participated in our Family Healthware study and had a moderate or strong familial risk for any of the 6 diseases were subsequently reviewed. The main outcome measures were PCP (primary care physician) response to the prompts, adding family history risk to problem summary lists, and patient screening status for each disease.
results.reference: The frequency of habits of Chaalia and Pan Masala chewing, by school children in lower socio-economic areas is extremely high. The probable reasons for this high frequency are taste, the widespread use of these substances by family members and friends, low cost and easy availability.

results.question: Does multi-modal cervical physical therapy improve tinnitus in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus?
rewritten: Does multi-modal cervical physical therapy improve tinnitus symptoms in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus associated with cervical spine dysfunction?
results.answer:
The study described shows that multimodal cervical physical therapy significantly decreased tinnitus severity (TFI scores) and neck complaints (NBQ scores) in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus. Over half of the patients experienced substantial improvement immediately after treatment, supporting the effectiveness of this therapy for tinnitus in this patient group.

yes
contexts: Tinnitus can be related to many different aetiologies such as hearing loss or a noise trauma, but it can also be related to the somatosensory system of the cervical spine, called cervicogenic somatic tinnitus (CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus)). Case studies suggest a positive effect of cervical spine treatment on tinnitus complaints in patients with CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus), but no experimental studies are available.
To investigate the effect of a multimodal cervical physical therapy treatment on tinnitus complaints in patients with CST (cervicogenic somatic tinnitus).

Patients with a combination of severe subjective tinnitus (Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI): 25-90 points) and neck complaints (Neck Bournemouth Questionnaire (NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)) > 14 points).
All patients received cervical physical therapy for 6 weeks (12 sessions). Patients were randomized in an immediate-start therapy group (n = 19) and a 6-week delayed-start therapy group (n = 19).

In all patients (n = 38) TFI and NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)-scores decreased significantly after treatment (p = 0.04 and p < 0.001). NBQ (neck bournemouth questionnaire)-scores remained significantly lower after follow-up (p = 0.001). Immediately after treatment, 53% (n = 38) experienced substantial improvement of tinnitus. This effect was maintained in 24% of patients after follow-up at six weeks.
results.reference: Cervical physical therapy can have a positive effect on subjective tinnitus complaints in patients with a combination of tinnitus and neck complaints. Larger studies, using more responsive outcome measures, are however necessary to prove this effect.

results.question: Detailed analysis of sputum and systemic inflammation in asthma phenotypes: are paucigranulocytic asthmatics really non-inflammatory?
rewritten: Is paucigranulocytic asthma truly a non-inflammatory phenotype based on detailed analysis of sputum biomarkers and systemic inflammatory markers in different asthma phenotypes?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that all asthma phenotypes, including paucigranulocytic asthma, show increased sputum eosinophils and elevated blood leukocyte counts compared to healthy subjects. Additionally, paucigranulocytic asthmatics have increased absolute blood eosinophils, suggesting systemic inflammation despite the paucity of granulocytes in sputum. Therefore, paucigranulocytic asthmatics are not truly non-inflammatory.

no
contexts: The technique of induced sputum has allowed to subdivide asthma patients into inflammatory phenotypes according to their level of granulocyte airway infiltration. There are very few studies which looked at detailed sputum and blood cell counts in a large cohort of asthmatics divided into inflammatory phenotypes. The purpose of this study was to analyze sputum cell counts, blood leukocytes and systemic inflammatory markers in these phenotypes, and investigate how those groups compared with healthy subjects.

The total non-squamous cell count per gram of sputum was greater in mixed granulocytic and neutrophilic phenotypes as compared to eosinophilic, paucigranulocytic asthma and healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Sputum eosinophils (in absolute values and percentages) were increased in all asthma phenotypes including paucigranulocytic asthma, compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Eosinophilic asthma showed higher absolute sputum neutrophil and lymphocyte counts than healthy subjects (p < 0.005), while neutrophilic asthmatics had a particularly low number of sputum macrophages and epithelial cells. All asthma phenotypes showed an increased blood leukocyte count compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005), with paucigranulocytic asthmatics having also increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Neutrophilic asthma had raised CRP (C reactive protein) and fibrinogen while eosinophilic asthma only showed raised fibrinogen compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005).

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study on 833 asthmatics recruited from the University Asthma Clinic of Liege and compared them with 194 healthy subjects. Asthmatics were classified into inflammatory phenotypes.

We studied 100 asthma patients who were divided into the following four groups: patients with obstruction who were either ICS-naive (group I) or were treated with ICSs (group II (group i) or were treated with icss)); and nonobstructed patients who were either ICS-naive (group III) or were treated with ICSs (group IV). PD (perception of dyspnea) on the visual analog scale (VAS (visual analog scale)) was assessed during a methacholine-induced FEV(1) decrease and specifically was quantified as the VAS (visual analog scale) slope and score at an FEV(1) decrease of 5 to 20%. BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness) was assessed in terms of the provocative concentration of methacholine causing a 20% fall in FEV(1) (PC(20)). Eosinophil counts in induced sputum samples also were performed. Regression analysis, univariate analysis of variance, and factor analysis were applied for statistical evaluation.

Racial differences in asthma care are not fully explained by socioeconomic status, care access, and insurance status. Appropriate care requires accurate physician estimates of severity. It is unknown if accuracy of physician estimates differs between black and white patients, and how this relates to asthma care disparities.
results.reference: This study demonstrates that a significant eosinophilic inflammation is present across all categories of asthma, and that paucigranulocytic asthma may be seen as a low grade inflammatory disease.

results.question: Is HIV/STD control in Jamaica making a difference?
rewritten: Is the implementation of HIV and sexually transmitted disease control programs in Jamaica effective in reducing infection rates?
results.answer:
The data from Jamaica show that while HIV prevalence remains relatively low in the general population and has only marginally increased in AIDS incidence, there have been significant improvements in condom use and reductions in syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases. These behavioral changes and declines in other STDs suggest that the HIV/STD control program is having a positive impact on the epidemic.

yes
contexts: To assess the impact of the comprehensive HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/STD (sexually transmitted disease) Control Program established in Jamaica since the late 1980s on the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic.

AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) case reports, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) testing of blood donors, antenatal clinic attenders (ANC (antenatal clinic attenders)), food service workers, sexually transmitted disease (STD (sexually transmitted disease)) clinic attenders, female prostitutes, homosexuals and other groups were used to monitor the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic. Primary and secondary syphilis and cases of congenital syphilis were also monitored. National knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP (knowledge, attitude and practice)) surveys were conducted in 1988, 1989, 1992, 1994 and 1996.

The annual AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) incidence rate in Jamaica increased only marginally in the past three years from 18.5 per 100000 population to 21.4 in 1997. HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence in the general population groups tested has been about 1% or less. Among those at high risk, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence rates have risen to 6.3% (95% confidence interval 5.0-8.0) in STD (sexually transmitted disease) clinic attenders, around 10% and 21% in female prostitutes in Kingston and Montego Bay respectively and approximately 30% among homosexuals. Syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases have declined. The proportion of men aged 15-49 years reporting sex with a non-regular partner declined from 35% in 1994 to 26% in 1996 (P<0.001). Women ever having used condoms increased from 51% in 1988 to 62.5% in 1992 and 73% in 1994 and 1996 (P<0.001), while condom use with a non-regular partner increased from 37% in 1992 to 73% in 1996 (P= 0.006). Condom use among men was high over the period: around 81% had ever used condoms and 77% used them with non-regular partners. Gay men, inner-city adults and adolescents aged 12-14 years all reported increases in condom use while condom sales and distribution increased from around 2 million in 1985 to 10 million in 1995.

Adoption and implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care leads to reductions in central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection)) rates in the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit). The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center.

The number of new diagnoses of HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) infection is rising in the northwestern hemisphere and it is becoming increasingly important to understand the mechanisms behind this trend.
results.reference: HIV/STD control measures appear to have slowed the HIV/AIDS epidemic in Jamaica, however a significant minority of persons continue to have unprotected sex in high risk situations.

results.question: Is Panton-Valentine leucocidin associated with the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia in the UK?
rewritten: Is Panton-Valentine leukocidin associated with the pathogenesis and clinical outcomes of Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (bacteraemia) in patients in the United Kingdom?
results.answer:
The data show that only a very small proportion (1.6%) of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia isolates in the UK and Ireland were PVL-positive, and these isolates were methicillin-susceptible and genetically diverse. This low prevalence and lack of PVL in methicillin-resistant strains suggest that PVL is not a major factor in the pathogenesis of S. aureus bacteraemia in this setting.

no
contexts: The morbidity and mortality associated with Panton-Valentine leucocidin (PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin))-positive Staphylococcus aureus suggest that this toxin is a key marker of disease severity. Nevertheless, the importance of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) in the pathogenesis of primary bacteraemia caused by S. aureus is uncertain. We have determined the prevalence of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-encoding genes among isolates of S. aureus from bacteraemic patients.

Consecutive bacteraemia isolates of S. aureus (n=244) from patients hospitalized in 25 centres in the UK and Ireland during 2005 were screened for PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) and mecA genes. PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates were characterized by toxin gene profiling, PFGE, spa-typing and MIC determinations for a range of antimicrobials.

Four out of 244 isolates (1.6%) were PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive and susceptible to oxacillin [methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA)]. Eighty-eight out of 244 (36%) were oxacillin-resistant (methicillin-resistant S. aureus), but none was PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive. The four patients (two males: 30 and 33 years; two females: 62 and 80 years) had infection foci of: skin and soft tissue, unknown, indwelling line, and surgical site, and were located at one centre in Wales, one in England and two in Ireland. One of four PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates was resistant to penicillin and fusidic acid, the remainder were susceptible to all antibiotics tested. Genotypic analyses showed that the four isolates represented three distinct strains; the two isolates from Ireland were related.

Adoption and implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care leads to reductions in central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection)) rates in the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit). The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center.

Adoption of standardized care practices, including bundles and checklists, was associated with a significant reduction of the CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection) rate to zero for>370 consecutive days in our NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) in 2012. Overall, our CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection) rates decreased from 4.1 per 1000 line days in 2009 (13 infections; 3163 line days) to 0.94 in 2013 (2 infections; 2115 line days), which represents a 77% reduction over a 5-year period. In the first quarter of 2013, there was a brief increase in CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection) rate to 3.3 per 1000 line days; after a series of interventions, the CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection) rate was maintained at zero for>600 days. Ongoing training, surveillance, and vigilance with catheter insertion and maintenance practices and improved documentation were identified as key drivers for success.
results.reference: We found that 1.6% of S. aureus (all MSSA) from bacteraemic patients were PVL-positive. This low incidence suggests that PVL-positive S. aureus are of no particular significance as causative agents of S. aureus bacteraemia.

results.question: Are even impaired fasting blood glucose levels preoperatively associated with increased mortality after CABG surgery?
rewritten: Are mildly elevated preoperative fasting blood glucose levels associated with increased postoperative mortality in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery?
results.answer:
The first abstract states that impaired fasting glucose below the diabetes threshold is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions, and the study goal was to determine if preoperative fasting blood glucose is associated with increased mortality after CABG. However, none of the other abstracts provide direct results or conclusions about the association between impaired fasting glucose and mortality after CABG. Therefore, while the initial aim suggests a possible association, the provided abstracts do not confirm this specifically for CABG surgery.

maybe
contexts: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG (impaired fasting glucose)) below the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)) is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions. The study goal was to determine whether pre-operative fasting blood glucose (fB-glu) is associated with an increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).

221 patients underwent CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) in our hospital from 2004 to 2007. 14 patients with preoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) and 4 patients with concomitant valve surgery were excluded from this study. Patients were divided into two groups to examine the influence of statins: those with preoperative statin therapy (Statin group, n = 77) and those without it (Non-statin group, n = 126). In addition, patients were divided into two groups to determine the independent predictors for postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation): those with postoperative AF (AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 54) and those without it (Non-AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 149). Patient data were collected and analyzed retrospectively.

The overall incidence of postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was 26%. Postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was significantly lower in the Statin group compared with the Non-statin group (16% versus 33%, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that independent predictors of AF (atrial fibrillation) development after CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) were preoperative statin therapy (odds ratio [OR]0.327, 95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)] 0.107 to 0.998, p = 0.05) and age (OR 1.058, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.004 to 1.116, p = 0.035).

The anesthetical-surgical procedure presented a mortality rate of 3.125% (1:32) and a morbidity rate of 6.25% (2:32). It was evidenced an initial mean blood glucose = 199.4 mg/dl and the end = 326.1 mg/dl. In spite of extended fasting (minimum of 2 hours for the absolute fasting and maximum of 8.5 hours for liquids, and 20.5 hours for solids) all animals presented at the end of the surgical procedure any gastric content and a blood glucose increase. Those with fasting for liquids and solids when compared to the quantity of solid gastric content, presented a moderate negative degree of correlation.

The case records of patients consecutively undergoing CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery) were reviewed. Patients were stratified retrospectively into high- or low-risk groups according to risk factors for significant carotid stenosis and perioperative stroke: peripheral vascular disease (PVD (peripheral vascular disease)), carotid bruit, diabetes mellitus, age>70 years and/or history of cerebrovascular disease. Prevalence of carotid stenosis detected by ultrasonography, surgical management and perioperative stroke rates were determined in each group.
results.reference: The elevated risk of death after CABG surgery known previously to be associated with CDM seems also to be shared by a group of similar size that includes patients with IFG and undiagnosed DM.

results.question: Does positron emission tomography change management in primary rectal cancer?
rewritten: Does positron emission tomography imaging influence clinical management and treatment decisions in patients with primary rectal adenocarcinoma?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that positron emission tomography (PET) scanning changed the management in 17% of patients with primary rectal cancer, including cancellation of surgery and changes in radiotherapy fields. Additionally, PET altered the overall tumor stage in 39% of patients, and follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of these PET-induced management changes. Therefore, PET does influence management decisions in primary rectal cancer.

yes
contexts: The influence of positron emission tomography in the management of recurrent rectal cancer is well established but its role in primary rectal cancer remains uncertain. This study therefore prospectively assesses the impact of position emission tomography scanning on the management of primary rectal cancer.

Forty-six patients with advanced primary rectal cancer referred for consideration of adjuvant preoperative therapy underwent position emission tomography scanning. The referring physicians prospectively recorded each patient's stage following conventional imaging and the proposed treatment plan prior to position emission tomography scanning. This was then compared with subsequent stage and actual management implemented, and the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced changes was noted by subsequent clinical follow-up.

Compared with computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), positron emission tomography (PET (positron emission tomography)) may have additional value in the assessment of primary and recurrent cervical cancer. However, the degree of tumour uptake of (18)F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D: -glucose (FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)) uptake is sometimes influenced by diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)). Therefore, we conducted this prospective study to compare the diagnostic ability of FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) in patients with cervical cancer complicated by DM (diabetes mellitus) and those without DM (diabetes mellitus).

The surgical management of 36 of 46 patients (78 percent) was unchanged as a result of position emission tomography, even though position emission tomography upstaged disease in 3 of 36 cases (8 percent) and downstaged disease in 5 of 36 cases (14 percent). In 8 of 46 cases (17 percent), management was altered because of the position emission tomography scan findings, including 6 cases (13 percent) in which surgery was cancelled and 2 other cases (4 percent) in which the radiotherapy field was changed. Where available, follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced management change in each case. Two patients had a change in therapy independent of the position emission tomography scan due to clinical circumstances. Overall tumor stage was changed following position emission tomography in 18 of 46 patients (39 percent).

From February 2001 to January 2003, 219 patients (75 with primary and 144 with recurrent cervical cancer) were eligible for analysis. Sixteen had hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), 12 had euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and 191 were in the non-DM (diabetes mellitus) group. The diagnostic power of PET (positron emission tomography) in the hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and non-DM (diabetes mellitus) groups did not differ significantly with regard to the identification of either metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve), 0.967/0.947/0.925, P>0.05) or primary tumours/local recurrence (AUC (area under the curve), 0.950/0.938/0.979, P>0.05). Considering all DM (diabetes mellitus) patients, PET (positron emission tomography) showed a significantly higher detection power than MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)/CT (computed tomography) scans in respect of metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve)=0.956 vs 0.824, P=0.012).
results.reference: Position emission tomography scanning appears to accurately change the stage or appropriately alter the therapy of almost a third of patients with advanced primary rectal cancer. In view of this, we suggest that position emission tomography scanning be considered part of standard workup for such patients, particularly if neoadjuvant chemoradiation is being considered as part of primary management.

results.question: Can you deliver accurate tidal volume by manual resuscitator?
rewritten: Can accurate tidal volume be delivered using a manual resuscitator bag-valve-mask device during mechanical ventilation?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that achieving accurate tidal volume delivery with manual resuscitators is challenging, as tidal volumes vary by user technique, physical characteristics, and device size. However, one study showed that only 1.5% of breaths with a pediatric BVM were below recommended tidal volume, suggesting that accurate delivery is possible but not guaranteed. Overall, the evidence supports that accurate tidal volume can be delivered with manual resuscitators, though variability exists.

yes
contexts: We enrolled 50 providers from a large, busy, urban fire-based EMS (emergency medical services) agency with 14.96 (SD = 9.92) mean years of experience. Only 1.5% of all breaths delivered with the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) during the ventilation scenarios were below the recommended tidal volume. A greater percentage of breaths delivered in the recommended range occurred when the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) was used (17.5% vs 5.1%, p<0.001). Median volumes for each scenario were 570.5mL, 664.0mL, 663.0mL for the pediatric BMV and 796.0mL, 994.5mL, 981.5mL for the adult BVM (bag-valve-mask). In all three categories of airway devices, the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) provided lower median tidal volumes (p<0.001).

Using a patient simulator of a head and thorax that was able to record respiratory rate, tidal volume, peak pressure, and minute volume via a laptop computer, participants were asked to ventilate the simulator during six 1-minute ventilation tests. The first scenario was BVM (bag-valve-mask) ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway in place ventilating with both an adult- and pediatric-sized BVM (bag-valve-mask), the second scenario had a supraglottic airway and both bags, and the third scenario had an endotracheal tube and both bags. Participants were enrolled in convenience manner while they were on-duty and the research staff was able to travel to their stations. Prior to enrolling, participants were not given any additional training on ventilation skills.

One of the problems with manual resuscitators is the difficulty in achieving accurate volume delivery. The volume delivered to the patient varies by the physical characteristics of the person and method. This study was designed to compare tidal volumes delivered by the squeezing method, physical characteristics and education and practice levels.

An instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) was designed. Laypersons were handed a bag containing a LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®), a bag mask valve device (BMV (bag mask valve device)), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed. Time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated.

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.
results.reference: The tidal volume delivered by a manual resuscitator shows large variations. There were significant differences in the volume delivered by compression methods, but physical characteristics are not a predictor of tidal volume delivery. The manual resuscitator is not a suitable device for accurate ventilation.

results.question: Can increases in the cigarette tax rate be linked to cigarette retail prices?
rewritten: Is there an association between increases in cigarette excise tax rates and changes in cigarette retail prices?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that in China, despite an increase in the cigarette excise tax in 2009, the retail prices of cigarettes did not increase because the State Tobacco Monopoly Administration used its authority to keep prices stable. This suggests that increases in the cigarette tax rate do not necessarily lead to higher retail prices, at least in the context described.

no
contexts: The 2009 excise tax increase on cigarettes in China has not translated into higher retail prices because the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) used its policy authority to ensure that retail cigarette prices did not change. The government tax increase is being collected at both the producer and wholesale levels. As a result, the 2009 excise tax increase in China has resulted in higher tax revenue for the government and lower profits for the tobacco industry, with no increase in the retail price of cigarettes for consumers.
To explain China's cigarette pricing mechanism and the role of the Chinese State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration)) on cigarette pricing and taxation.

Published government tobacco tax documentation and statistics published by the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) are used to analyse the interrelations among industry profits, taxes and retail price of cigarettes in China.

Household survey data were abstracted from serial surveys in 27 countries. Average annual changes (AAC (annual changes)) between the most recent and penultimate survey were calculated for under-five mortality rates and for 22 variables in the domains of clinical, outreach, and family- and community-based services. For all 27 countries and a subset of 19 African countries, we conducted principal component analysis to reduce the variables into a few components in each domain and applied linear regression to assess the correlation between changes in the principal components and changes in under-five mortality rates after controlling for multiple potential confounding factors.

An index of smoking susceptibility was created using measures of cigarette use and future intention to smoke. A zero-order correlation for parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing and smoking susceptibility showed a strong association (r = -.36, p<.001). A hierarchical logistic regression yielded odds ratios (ORs (odds ratios)) for being susceptible to or having tried smoking for three levels of parental R-rated movie restriction. Results show that compared to full restriction, respondents with partial or no restriction were more likely to be susceptible to smoking (partial restriction: OR = 2.1, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.5-2.8; no restriction: OR = 3.3, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 2.3-4.6), when controlling for demographic factors, and family and friend smoking. Analyses using a measure of smoking prevalence as the dependent variable yielded similar results (partial restriction: OR = 1.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.0-2.2; no restriction: OR = 2.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.7-3.7).
results.reference: Numerous studies have found that taxation is one of the most effective policy instruments for tobacco control. However, these findings come from countries that have market economies where market forces determine prices and influence how cigarette taxes are passed to the consumers in retail prices. China's tobacco industry is not a market economy; therefore, non-market forces and the current Chinese tobacco monopoly system determine cigarette prices. The result is that tax increases do not necessarily get passed on to the retail price.

results.question: Vertical lines in distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM): a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children?
rewritten: Are vertical lines in the distal esophageal mucosa a definitive endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in pediatric patients?
results.answer:
The presence of vertical lines in the esophageal mucosa (VLEM) was observed as the only mucosal abnormality in a group of children, and most of these children had eosinophilic esophagitis confirmed by histology. The strong association between VLEM and moderate to severe eosinophilic esophagitis supports that VLEM is a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children.

yes
contexts: We observed an endoscopic abnormally in a group of children with histological esophagitis. We termed this finding "vertical lines in esophageal mucosa" (VLEM). We examined the relationship between the presence of VLEM and significant histologic changes in esophageal mucosal biopsies.

The esophageal mucosa had a normal appearance on 160 endoscopic studies (Group 1) and VLEM were the only mucosal abnormalities in 41 endoscopies (Group 2). Histology was normal in 92 of 160 biopsies (57.5%) from Group 1, and 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) from Group 2. Most patients in Group 2 had eosinophilic esophagitis (34 of 41, 83%, specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.5, p>0.001) which was of moderate to severe intensity (31 of 34, 91.2%, specificity 0.88, sensitivity 0.73, p<0.001).

Primary eosinophilic esophagitis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus, evokes recurrent dysphagia. Endoscopy is often unremarkable, and no consensus exists regarding management of resultant dysphagia. The response of a series of patients with primary eosinophilic esophagitis to dilation is reported together with a description of a possibly pathognomonic sign: fragile esophageal mucosa, for which the term "crêpe-paper" mucosa is introduced.

Between January 1, 1992, and August 31, 1994, the senior author (JFF) performed 255 esophageal biopsies. The procedure reports, available endoscopic photographs, and histology reports were reviewed to establish the endoscopic and histologic appearance of the esophageal mucosa. Intraepithelial cells were counted in a blind review of 42 randomly selected biopsies.

Mean mucosal thickness in patients with IHPS (infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis) approximated mean muscle thickness, with a ratio of 0.89. In infants with IHPS (infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis), the pyloric mucosa constitutes approximately one third of the cross-sectional diameter of the pyloric mass and fills and obstructs the pyloric canal.
results.reference: Histology usually demonstrated moderate to severe inflammation when VLEM were present. VLEM may be a highly specific endoscopic feature of esophagitis in children.

results.question: Does hypoglycaemia increase the risk of cardiovascular events?
rewritten: Does hypoglycemia increase the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure in patients with diabetes mellitus?
results.answer:
The provided abstract [5] shows that severe hypoglycaemia is associated with a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular events, including cardiovascular death, arrhythmic death, and mortality. Non-severe hypoglycaemia, however, was not associated with these outcomes. Therefore, severe hypoglycaemia does increase the risk of cardiovascular events.

yes
contexts: Several studies have shown associations between hyperglycemia and risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD (cardiovascular disease)) and mortality, yet glucose-lowering treatment does little to mitigate this risk. We examined whether associations between hyperglycemia and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk were explained by underlying insulin resistance.
Metabolic syndrome (MetS (metabolic syndrome)) is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events. We evaluated heart dimensions in hypertensive patients with MetS (metabolic syndrome).

In 60 middle-aged individuals without diabetes we studied the associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour post oral glucose tolerance test plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity as well as body fat percentage with CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk. Insulin sensitivity was measured as the glucose infusion rate during a euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp, body fat percentage was measured by dual X-ray absorptiometry, and CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk was estimated using the Framingham risk score. Associations of fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity and body fat percentage with the Framingham risk score were assessed in linear regression models.

It has recently been shown that non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C) may be a better predictor of cardiovascular risk than low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C). Based on known ethic differences in lipid parameters and cardiovascular risk prediction, we sought to study the predictability of attaining non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C target and long-term major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event)) in Thai patients after acute myocardial infarction (AMI (acute myocardial infarction)) compared to attaining LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C target.

A total of 12 537 participants with dysglycaemia and high CV (cardiovascular)-risk were randomized to basal insulin glargine titrated to a fasting glucose of ≤ 5.3 mmol/L (95 mg/dL) or standard glycaemic care. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was defined as symptoms confirmed by glucose ≤ 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycaemia as a requirement for assistance or glucose ≤ 36 mg/dL. Outcomes were: (i) the composite of CV (cardiovascular) death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke; (ii) mortality; (iii) CV (cardiovascular) mortality; and (iv) arrhythmic death. Hazards were estimated before and after adjustment for a hypoglycaemia propensity score. During a median of 6.2 years (IQR: 5.8-6.7), non-severe hypoglycaemic episodes occurred in 41.7 and 14.4% glargine and standard group participants, respectively, while severe episodes occurred in 5.7 and 1.8%, respectively. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was not associated with any outcome following adjustment. Conversely, severe hypoglycaemia was associated with a greater risk for the primary outcome (HR: 1.58; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.24-2.02, P<0.001), mortality (HR: 1.74; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.39-2.19, P<0.001), CV (cardiovascular) death (HR: 1.71; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.27-2.30, P<0.001) and arrhythmic death (HR: 1.77; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.17-2.67, P = 0.007). Similar findings were noted for severe nocturnal hypoglycaemia for the primary outcome and mortality. The severe hypoglycaemia hazard for all four outcomes was higher with standard care than with insulin glargine.
results.reference: Severe hypoglycaemia is associated with an increased risk for CV outcomes in people at high CV risk and dysglycaemia. results.answer:

Therefore, the evidence suggests that the radiographic transition zone does not accurately correlate with the level of aganglionosis on the specimen.

results.reference: Correlation between level of radiographic transition zone on contrast enema and length of aganglionosis remains low. Systematic preoperative biopsy by coelioscopy or ombilical incision is mandatory.

results.question: Is dexamethasone an effective alternative to oral prednisone in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations?
rewritten: Is dexamethasone an effective alternative to oral prednisone for the management of acute asthma exacerbations in pediatric patients?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that multiple pediatric clinical trials found dexamethasone to be not inferior to prednisone in treating mild to moderate asthma exacerbations. Meta-analysis showed similar outcomes in symptom resolution and physician revisits, with some studies suggesting additional benefits of dexamethasone such as better compliance and less vomiting. Therefore, dexamethasone can be considered an effective alternative to oral prednisone in this context.

yes
contexts: A short course of systemic corticosteroids is an important therapy in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations. Although a 5-day course of oral prednisone or prednisolone has become the most commonly used regimen, dexamethasone has also been used for a shorter duration (1-2 days) with potential for improvement in compliance and palatability. We reviewed the literature to determine if there is sufficient evidence that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations in the inpatient setting.

Six completed pediatric clinical trials met the inclusion criteria. All of the pediatric trials found that prednisone is not superior to dexamethasone in treating mild to moderate asthma exacerbations. Meta-analysis demonstrated homogeneity between the dexamethasone and prednisone groups when examining symptomatic return to baseline and unplanned physician revisits after the initial emergency department encounter. Some studies found potential additional benefits of dexamethasone, including improved compliance and less vomiting.

To investigate if fetal gender (1) affects the risk of having an emergency department (ED (emergency department)) visit for asthma; and (2) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had at least one visit to the ED (emergency department) for asthma during pregnancy.

results.reference: The current literature suggests that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative to prednisone in the treatment of mild to moderate acute asthma exacerbations in children, with the added benefits of improved compliance, palatability, and cost. results.question: Mammographic screening in Sami speaking municipalities and a control group. Are early outcome measures influenced by ethnicity?
rewritten: Does mammographic screening in Sami-speaking municipalities compared to a control population influence early breast cancer detection outcomes based on ethnic differences?
results.answer:
The attendance rate for mammographic screening was slightly higher in the Sami population (78%) compared to the non-Sami population (75%), and recall rates were significantly lower in the Sami group (2.4% vs. 3.3%). However, the rate of invasive screen-detected cancer was not significantly different, and the percentage of all breast cancers detected in the screening program was lower in the Sami group but not statistically significant. These findings suggest some differences in early outcome measures related to ethnicity.

contexts: Female citizens of Sami (the indigenous people of Norway) municipalities in northern Norway have a low risk of breast cancer. The objective of this study was to describe the attendance rate and outcome of the Norwegian Breast Cancer Screening Program (NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program)) in the Sami-speaking municipalities and a control group.

The NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) targets women aged 50-69 years. Rates and percentages were compared using chi-square test with a p-value<0.05 as statistical significant.

The attendance rate in the NBCSP (norwegian breast cancer screening program) was 78% in the Sami and 75% in the non-Sami population (p<0.01). The recall rates were 2.4 and 3.3% in the Sami and non-Sami population, respectively (p<0.01). The rate of invasive screen detected cancer was not significantly lower in the Sami group (p=0.14). results.question: Do Electrochemiluminescence Assays Improve Prediction of Time to Type 1 Diabetes in Autoantibody-Positive TrialNet Subjects?
rewritten: Do Electrochemiluminescence Immunoassays Enhance the Prediction Accuracy of Progression Time to Type 1 Diabetes in Autoantibody-Positive Individuals Enrolled in the TrialNet Natural History Study?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assays, specifically ECL-IAA and ECL-GADA, are significantly associated with progression to type 1 diabetes in autoantibody-positive TrialNet subjects. Adding ECL positivity to existing risk models improved prediction accuracy, with a higher risk of progression observed in ECL-positive individuals. Therefore, ECL assays do improve prediction of time to type 1 diabetes in this population.

contexts: To explore whether electrochemiluminescence (ECL (electrochemiluminescence)) assays can help improve prediction of time to type 1 diabetes in the TrialNet autoantibody-positive population.

Subjects who were ECL (electrochemiluminescence) positive had a risk of progression to diabetes within 6 years of 58% compared with 5% for the ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-negative subjects (P<0.0001). The model with positivity for ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-GADA and/or ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-IAA (insulin autoantibody) was the best, and factors that remained significantly associated with time to diabetes were area under the curve (AUC (area under the curve)) C-peptide, fasting C-peptide, AUC (area under the curve) glucose, number of positive autoantibodies by RIAs (radioimmunoassays), and ECL (electrochemiluminescence) positivity. Adding ECL (electrochemiluminescence) to the Diabetes Prevention Trial risk score (DPTRS (diabetes prevention trial risk score)) improved the receiver operating characteristic curves with AUC (area under the curve) of 0.83 (P<0.0001).

TrialNet subjects who were positive for one or more autoantibodies (microinsulin autoantibody, GAD65 autoantibody [GADA], IA-2A, and ZnT8A) with available ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-insulin autoantibody (IAA (insulin autoantibody)) and ECL (electrochemiluminescence)-GADA data at their initial visit were analyzed; after a median follow-up of 24 months, 177 of these 1,287 subjects developed diabetes.

Participants were 7 individuals with T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and 10 controls. There were no diabetic complications and HbA1c (hemoglobin A1c) was 8.7 ± 2.6 mmol/mol for T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and 5.3 ± 0.4 mmol/mol for control groups. Since insulin therapy might have an atherogenic effect, we studied the relationship between cumulative insulin dose and atherosclerosis in type 1 diabetes. results.reference: ECL assays improved the ability to predict time to diabetes in these autoantibody-positive relatives at risk for developing diabetes. These findings might be helpful in the design and eligibility criteria for prevention trials in the future.

results.question: Assessment of appropriate antimicrobial prescribing: do experts agree?
rewritten: Assessment of appropriate antimicrobial prescribing practices: is there consensus among infectious disease experts and clinical pharmacologists?
results.answer:
The context indicates that infectious disease specialists' assessments of antimicrobial appropriateness were compared to a reference standard based on modal expert opinion, and interrater and intrarater agreements were analyzed. This suggests that there is a measurable level of agreement among experts, although the exact degree of agreement is not specified here. Therefore, experts do show agreement in assessing appropriate antimicrobial prescribing.

yes
contexts: Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.

Twenty-four doctors specialized in infectious diseases or clinical microbiology (16 specialists and 8 residents) from five hospitals were asked to assess the appropriateness of antimicrobial agents prescribed for a broad spectrum of indications in 56 paper cases. They were instructed how to handle guideline applicability and deviations. We created a reference standard of antimicrobial appropriateness using the modal assessment of 16 specialists. We calculated criterion validity and interrater and intrarater overall and specific agreement with an index expert (senior infectious disease physician) and analysed the influence of doctor characteristics on validity.

To observe if medical providers alter their prescribing patterns of three relatively expensive categories of medications provided as samples by manufacturers (focus medications) when they receive additional education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower cost alternatives (counter samples) that are made available to dispense.

In a population-based cohort study using register data, we analysed the prescribing of new drugs by Danish general practitioners. Angiotensin-II antagonists, triptans, selective cyclo-oxygenase-2 antagonists and esomeprazol were used in the assessment. As indicators of new drug uptake, we used adoption time, cumulative incidence, preference proportion, incidence rate and prescription cost and volume. For each measure, we ranked the general practices. Ranks were pair-wise plotted, and Pearson's correlation coefficient ( r) was calculated. Next, we analysed the correlation between ranks across different drug classes.

By the conclusion of the study, all remaining 17 practices had adopted PHQ-9 as a routine part of depression care in their practice. On the basis of responses from 17 psychiatrists from those practices, PHQ-9 scores influenced clinical decision making for 93% of 6,096 patient contacts. With the additional information gained from the PHQ-9 score, one or more treatment changes occurred during 40% of these clinical contacts. Changing the dosage of antidepressant medication and adding another medication were the most common treatment changes recorded by psychiatrists, followed by starting or increasing psychotherapy and by switching or initiating antidepressants. In 3% of the patient contacts, using the PHQ-9 led to additional suicide risk assessment.
results.reference: Doctors specialized in infectious diseases and clinical microbiology assess the appropriateness of antimicrobials prescribed for a broad spectrum of indications with acceptable agreement and validity, regardless of their experience or hospital of employment. However, there is room for improvement, which merits attention in multidisciplinary discussions and education.

results.question: Cycloplegic autorefraction in young adults: is it mandatory?
rewritten: Is cycloplegic autorefraction necessary for accurate refractive error assessment in young adults?

This suggests that cycloplegic autorefraction provides more accurate refractive error assessment in this age group, especially for hypermetropes, indicating its importance for precise correction.

100 patients (age 8 - 90 years, median 60.5 years) with various eye disorders, among them 39 with amblyopia due to strabismus, and 13 healthy volunteers were tested. results.question: Does screening or surveillance for primary hepatocellular carcinoma with ultrasonography improve the prognosis of patients?
rewritten: Does screening or surveillance for primary hepatocellular carcinoma using abdominal ultrasonography improve clinical outcomes and overall prognosis in patients at risk?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that screening and surveillance for primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are associated with significantly better prognostic outcomes, including improved survival times and favorable tumor morphology or staging. contexts: The purpose of this paper is to evaluate the efficacy of ultrasonographic screening for primary hepatocellular carcinoma.

Patients with primary lung cancer who underwent radical surgery between 2010 and 2014 were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical, pathologic, and prognosis data were obtained and analyzed.

results.question: Department of Transportation vs self-reported data on motor vehicle collisions and driving convictions for stroke survivors: do they agree?
rewritten: Do Department of Transportation records and self-reported data on motor vehicle collisions and driving convictions show concordance in stroke survivors?
results.answer:
The study found only moderate agreement between Ministry of Transportation records and self-reports of collisions and convictions among stroke survivors, with kappa coefficients of 0.52 and 0.47 respectively. results.question: Neoadjuvant Imatinib in Locally Advanced Gastrointestinal stromal Tumours, Will Kit Mutation Analysis Be a Pathfinder?

results.answer:

results.question: Does lung ischemia and reperfusion have an impact on coronary flow?

results.answer:
