The study outcome, regular treatment of daily pain, examined whether patients received any analgesic, other than those not recommended by AMDA (american medical directors association), at least twice a day for each day of documented daily pain (i.e., 7 days before date of last MDS).
results.reference: We found evidence that pain can be a significant clinical problem in psychiatric patients which seems to be underestimated in psychiatry. The investigated patients in general adult psychiatry are characterized by specific risk factors different from clinical subpopulations of other disciplines.

results.question: Does concomitant anterior/apical repair during midurethral sling improve the overactive bladder component of mixed incontinence?
rewritten: Does concomitant anterior and apical pelvic organ prolapse repair performed during midurethral sling surgery improve the overactive bladder symptoms in women with mixed urinary incontinence?
results.answer:
The study found that both groups—those undergoing midurethral sling (MUS) alone and those undergoing MUS with concomitant anterior/apical (AA) prolapse repair—showed significant improvement in overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms postoperatively. However, there was no significant difference in the degree of improvement between the two cohorts, indicating that adding AA repair does not provide additional benefit to the OAB component of mixed urinary incontinence.

no
contexts: Midurethral sling (MUS (midurethral sling)) can improve overactive bladder (OAB (overactive bladder)) symptoms. It is unclear if anterior/apical prolapse (AA (apical prolapse)) repair provides additional benefit. We hypothesized that women with mixed urinary incontinence (MUI (mixed urinary incontinence)) experience greater improvement in the OAB (overactive bladder) component of their symptoms after concomitant MUS (midurethral sling) and AA (apical prolapse) repair compared with MUS (midurethral sling) alone.

This is a retrospective cohort study of women with bothersome MUI (defined by objective stress test and validated questionnaire) undergoing MUS (midurethral sling) alone ("MUS (midurethral sling)-only") or concomitant MUS (midurethral sling) and AA (apical prolapse) repair ("MUS (midurethral sling) + AA (apical prolapse)"). Our primary outcome was the Overactive Bladder Questionnaire Symptom Severity (OAB (overactive bladder)-q SS) change score 6 weeks after surgery.

Of 151 women, 67 (44 %) underwent MUS (midurethral sling)-only and 84 (56 %) underwent MUS (midurethral sling) + AA (apical prolapse). The MUS (midurethral sling)-only cohort was younger and had less severe baseline prolapse (p < 0.05 for both). Postoperative complications (predominantly UTI) occurred in 35 (23 %) patients and were similar between cohorts. For all subjects mean OAB (overactive bladder)-q SS scores significantly improved postoperatively (p < 0.05). Our primary outcome, OAB (overactive bladder)-q SS change score, showed no significant differences between cohorts (30 ± 26 MUS (midurethral sling)-only vs 25 ± 25 MUS (midurethral sling) + AA (apical prolapse), p = 0.20), indicating similar improvements in OAB (overactive bladder) symptoms. Multivariate linear regression analysis revealed no difference in OAB (overactive bladder)-q SS change score between cohorts; however, OAB (overactive bladder)-q SS change scores were lower for women with a postoperative complication (β = -19, 95 % CI (confidence interval) -31 to -6; p < 0.01).
To compare the accuracy achieved by a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP (urology nurse practitioner)) and consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumours during flexible cystoscopy.

Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM (intraoperative neuromonitoring)) aims to control nerve-sparing total mesorectal excision (TME (total mesorectal excision)) for rectal cancer in order to improve patients' functional outcome. This study was designed to compare the urogenital and anorectal functional outcome of TME (total mesorectal excision) with and without IONM (intraoperative neuromonitoring) of innervation to the bladder and the internal anal sphincter.
results.reference: In women with bothersome MUI, concomitant AA repair does not result in additional improvement in OAB symptoms over MUS alone. Patients with postoperative complications exhibit less improvement in OAB symptoms.

results.question: Does the use of atypical antipsychotics as adjunctive therapy in depression result in cost savings?
rewritten: Does adjunctive treatment with atypical antipsychotics in major depressive disorder lead to healthcare cost savings?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that atypical antipsychotics (AAPs) used as second-line agents in depression result in higher mean adjusted pharmacy costs and higher mean adjusted total mental health-related costs compared to other treatments. There was no difference in total healthcare costs or inpatient and emergency department visits, suggesting no overall cost savings with AAP use.

no
contexts: To estimate healthcare costs and utilization of AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) compared to other second-line agents.

Several atypical antipsychotics (AAPs (atypical antipsychotics)) are used as second-line agents for treatment resistant depression. AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) can be expensive compared to other treatment options and can cause several side effects.

A total of 3910 members received second-line treatment. Treatment groups were AAPs (n = 2211), augmentation agents other than AAPs (n = 1008), and antidepressant switching (n = 691). AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) resulted in higher mean adjusted pharmacy costs and higher mean adjusted total mental health-related costs. Mean adjusted total healthcare costs and number of inpatient and ED (emergency department) visits were not different among treatments.

This study examined Dutch patients with an initial treatment episode in 2009 or 2010 in specialized mental health settings for depressive disorder (N = 85,754). Follow-up data about treatment episodes were available up until 2013. The data set included demographic (age, gender), and clinical factors (comorbidity with other DSM-IV Axis; scores on the 'Global Assessment of Functioning'). Cox regression analyses were used to assess whether duration of treatment and relapse into mental health care were related.

All currently available atypical antipsychotics have, at clinically relevant doses: i) high serotonin (5-HT)2 occupancy; ii) greater 5-HT2 than dopamine (D)2 occupancy; and iii) a higher incidence of extrapyramidal side effects when their D2 occupancy exceeds 80%. A review of pharmacologic and behavioral data suggested that amoxapine should also conform to this profile; therefore, we undertook a positron-emission tomography (PET (positron-emission tomography)) study of its 5-HT2 and D2 occupancy.
results.reference: The results show no evidence that AAPs used as second-line treatment for depression results in overall cost savings or lower inpatient and ED visits compared to other treatment strategies.

results.question: Can patients be anticoagulated after intracerebral hemorrhage?
rewritten: Is anticoagulation therapy safe and effective for patients following intracerebral hemorrhage?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that anticoagulation after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is generally not preferred, especially for patients with prior lobar ICH, as withholding anticoagulation improves quality-adjusted life expectancy. However, for patients with prior deep hemispheric ICH, anticoagulation might be considered if the risk of thromboembolic stroke is particularly high. Thus, anticoagulation can be used selectively depending on the type of ICH and individual risk factors.

maybe
contexts: For patients with prior lobar ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage), withholding anticoagulation therapy was strongly preferred, improving quality-adjusted life expectancy by 1.9 QALYs (quality-adjusted life years). For patients with prior deep hemispheric ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage), withholding anticoagulation resulted in a smaller gain of 0.3 QALYs (quality-adjusted life years). In sensitivity analyses for patients with deep ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage), anticoagulation could be preferred if the risk of thromboembolic stroke is particularly high.

Warfarin increases both the likelihood and the mortality of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage)), particularly in patients with a history of prior ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage). In light of this consideration, should a patient with both a history of ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage) and a clear indication for anticoagulation such as nonvalvular atrial fibrillation be anticoagulated? In the absence of data from a clinical trial, we used a decision-analysis model to compare the expected values of 2 treatment strategies-warfarin and no anticoagulation-for such patients.

One-hundred-fourteen trauma patients were initiated on therapeutic anticoagulation. The most common indication for anticoagulation was deep venous thrombosis (46%). Twenty-four patients (21%) had at least 1 anticoagulation complication. The most common complication was a sudden drop in hemoglobin concentration requiring blood transfusion (11 patients). Five patients died (4%), 3 of whom had significant hemorrhage attributed to anticoagulation. Bivariate followed by logistic regression analysis identified chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (OR = 9.2, 95%CI (confidence interval) = 1.5-54.7), UH (unfractionated heparin) use (OR = 3.8, 95%CI (confidence interval) = 1.1-13.0), and lower initial platelet count (OR = 1.004, 95%CI (confidence interval) = 1.000-1.008) as being associated with complications. Patients receiving UH (unfractionated heparin) vs. FH (fractionated heparin) differed in several characteristics including laboratory values and anticoagulation indications.

We used a Markov state transition decision model stratified by location of hemorrhage (lobar or deep hemispheric). Effectiveness was measured in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs (quality-adjusted life years)). Data sources included English language literature identified through MEDLINE searches and bibliographies from selected articles, along with empirical data from our own institution. The base case focused on a 69-year-old man with a history of ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage) and newly diagnosed nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.

Trauma patients who require therapeutic anticoagulation pose a difficult treatment problem. The purpose of this study was to determine: (1) the incidence of complications using therapeutic anticoagulation in trauma patients, and (2) if any patient factors are associated with these complications.
results.reference: Survivors of lobar ICH with atrial fibrillation should not be offered long-term anticoagulation. Similarly, most patients with deep hemispheric ICH and atrial fibrillation should not receive anticoagulant therapy. However, patients with deep hemispheric ICH at particularly high risk for thromboembolic stroke or low risk of ICH recurrence might benefit from long-term anticoagulation.

results.question: Diagnostic and therapeutic ureteroscopy: is dilatation of ureteral meatus always necessary?
rewritten: Is dilatation of the ureteral orifice always necessary during diagnostic and therapeutic ureteroscopy for ureteral pathologies?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a study comparing ureteroscopy performed with and without ureteral meatus dilatation, assessing feasibility and safety. Since the study includes a group undergoing ureteroscopy without dilatation and evaluates outcomes such as complications and success rates, it implies that dilatation is not always necessary for diagnostic or therapeutic ureteroscopy.

no
contexts: To assess the feasibility and safety of diagnostic or therapeutic semirigid ureteroscopy without ureteral meatus dilatation.

A comparative, retrospective study was conducted of patients undergoing ureteroscopy from January 2000 to May 2008. For data analysis purposes, the population was divided into two groups based on whether ureteroscopy had been performed with (Group 1) or without (Group 2) ureteral meatus dilatation. Variables recorded included age, sex, type of procedure, surgical diagnosis, passive or active dilatation, number of stones, stone location, stone diameter, peroperative and postoperative complications, internal urinary diversion after the procedure, therapeutic success rate, operating time, and hospital stay duration. A 8-9.8 Fr Wolf semirigid ureteroscope was used. Descriptive statistics of the population and cohorts were performed, providing medians, quartiles, and limit values for non-normally distributed interval variables, and absolute and relative frequencies for categorical variables. Shapiro-Wilk's, Mann-Whitney's U, Chi-square, and Fisher's exact tests were used for statistical analysis. A value of p 2 alpha<or = 0.005 was considered statistically significant. Arcus Quickstat Biomedical 1.0 software was used.

A series of 188 patients with 208 ureteral stones were treated with semirigid ureteroscopy and holmium:YAG laser lithotripsy from January 2003 to December 2005. Of the stones, 116 were lower ureteral, 37 middle ureteral, and 55 upper ureteral.
To study the efficiency and safety of holmium:YAG laser lithotripsy for ureteral stones.

The success rate was 92.7% at the time of ureteroscopy and 96.7% at 3 months. The failures were secondary to retropulsion of the stones (3.3%). There were no perforations and one stricture. Stenting was done in 90% of patients.
results.reference: In selected cases, ureteroscopy may be performed without ureteral meatus dilatation with success and morbidity rates similar to when the procedure is performed with meatal dilatation.

results.question: Does managed care enable more low income persons to identify a usual source of care?
rewritten: Does enrollment in managed care programs increase the likelihood of low-income individuals having a usual source of primary healthcare?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that high managed care penetration is associated with a lower likelihood of uninsured low-income persons having a usual source of care and a usual physician. Managed care has only marginal effects on privately insured and Medicaid beneficiaries, suggesting it does not significantly enable more low-income persons to identify a usual source of care.

no
contexts: (1) To examine the effects of managed care on the likelihood of low-income persons having a usual source of care and a usual physician, and; (2) To examine the association between usual source of care and access.

High managed care penetration in the community is associated with a lower likelihood of having a usual source of care for uninsured persons (54.8% vs. 62.2% in low penetration areas) as well as a lower likelihood of having a usual physician (60% vs. 72.8%). Managed care has only marginal effects on the likelihood of having a usual source of care for privately insured and Medicaid beneficiaries. Having a usual physician substantially reduces unmet medical needs for the insured but less so for the uninsured.
Usual source of care, usual physician, managed care enrollment, managed care penetration.
By requiring or encouraging enrollees to obtain a usual source of care, managed care programs hope to improve access to care without incurring higher costs.

It is uncertain whether the inverse equity hypothesis-the idea that new health interventions are initially primarily accessed by the rich, but that inequalities narrow with diffusion to the poor-holds true for cancer screening in low and middle income countries (LMICs (low and middle income countries)).This study examines the relationship between overall coverage and economic inequalities in coverage of cancer screening in four middle-income countries.
results.reference: Having a usual physician can be an effective tool in improving access to care for low-income populations, although it is most effective when combined with insurance coverage. However, the effectiveness of managed care in linking more low-income persons to a medical home is uncertain, and may have unintended consequences for uninsured persons.

results.question: Knee extensor strength, dynamic stability, and functional ambulation: are they related in Parkinson's disease?
rewritten: Is there a correlation between knee extensor muscle strength, dynamic postural stability, and functional ambulation capacity in patients with Parkinson's disease?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that knee extensor strength positively correlates with dynamic postural stability and that dynamic postural stability positively correlates with functional ambulation in patients with Parkinson's disease. Additionally, knee extensor strength negatively correlates with disease severity, suggesting these factors are interrelated in this population.

yes
contexts: To evaluate the relationship between knee extensor strength, postural stability, functional ambulation, and disease severity in Parkinson's disease (PD (parkinson's disease)).

Knee extensor strength positively correlated with dynamic postural stability and negatively correlated with disease severity. Further, dynamic postural stability was negatively correlated to disease severity and positively correlated with functional ambulation in this cohort of patients with PD (P<.05). The results also suggest that the Functional Reach Test may be a valuable assessment tool to examine postural stability in PD (parkinson's disease).

Participants were evaluated on their isokinetic knee extensor strength. Additionally, participants completed an assessment of their postural stability (Functional Reach Test for static stability and a dynamic postural stability assessment as measured by the center of pressure-center of mass moment arm during gait initiation). Participants also underwent an evaluation of their functional ambulation as measured by a 6-minute walk test. Lastly, participants were evaluated by a neurologist specially trained in movement disorders to assess neurologic status and disease severity using the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale and the Hoehn and Yahr disability score.
Patients (N=44) with idiopathic PD (parkinson's disease).

Six human cadaver knees were tested before implantation, after implantation with a bicruciate-retaining unicompartmental knee prosthesis, and after implantation with a posterior cruciate-retaining tricompartmental knee prosthesis. The unicompartmental prosthesis was initially implanted, and it was then revised to a total condylar knee replacement. The knee kinematics were measured with use of an electromagnetic tracking device while the knee was put through dynamic simulated stair-climbing under peak flexion moments of approximately 40 N-m. Quadriceps tension was also measured for all three conditions.
results.reference: These findings suggest a malleable relationship between knee extensor strength, dynamic stability, and disease severity in PD. Although strength is only one piece of the puzzle in the functional outcome of PD, these findings may assist clinicians in designing appropriate interventions aimed at increasing function and decreasing fall risk in PD.

results.question: Is distance to provider a barrier to care for medicaid patients with breast, colorectal, or lung cancer?
rewritten: Is geographic distance to healthcare providers a barrier to accessing medical care for Medicaid beneficiaries diagnosed with breast cancer, colorectal cancer, or lung cancer?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that greater travel burden, measured by driving distance or time, is associated with later stage at diagnosis for breast cancer patients and longer time-to-treatment for colorectal cancer patients on Medicaid. This suggests that distance to provider acts as a barrier to timely care for these cancer patients. Although lung cancer is mentioned in the patient cohort, specific findings related to lung cancer are not detailed, but the overall evidence supports distance as a barrier for at least breast and colorectal cancer patients.

yes
contexts: Distance to provider might be an important barrier to timely diagnosis and treatment for cancer patients who qualify for Medicaid coverage. Whether driving time or driving distance is a better indicator of travel burden is also of interest.

Driving distances and times from patient residence to primary care provider were calculated for 3,917 breast, colorectal (CRC (colorectal)) and lung cancer Medicaid patients in Washington State from 1997 to 2003 using MapQuest.com. We fitted regression models of stage at diagnosis and time-to-treatment (number of days between diagnosis and surgery) to test the hypothesis that travel burden is associated with timely diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

Later stage at diagnosis for breast cancer Medicaid patients is associated with travel burden (OR = 1.488 per 100 driving miles, P= .037 and OR = 1.270 per driving hour, P= .016). Time-to-treatment after diagnosis of CRC (colorectal) is also associated with travel burden (14.57 days per 100 driving miles, P= .002 and 5.86 days per driving hour, P= .018).

Automated, tailored prompts highlighting familial risk for heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and breast, colorectal, or ovarian cancer were implemented during 2011 to 2012. Medical records of a cohort of community-based primary care patients, aged 35 to 65 years, who previously participated in our Family Healthware study and had a moderate or strong familial risk for any of the 6 diseases were subsequently reviewed. The main outcome measures were PCP (primary care physician) response to the prompts, adding family history risk to problem summary lists, and patient screening status for each disease.

Treatment delays in breast cancer are generally thought to affect prognosis but the impact on survival remains unclear. Indicators for breast cancer care include time to primary treatment. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether time to primary treatment (TPT (to primary treatment)) in breast cancer impacts survival.
results.reference: Although travel burden is associated with timely diagnosis and treatment for some types of cancer, we did not find evidence that driving time was, in general, better at predicting timeliness of cancer diagnosis and treatment than driving distance. More intensive efforts at early detection of breast cancer and early treatment of CRC for Medicaid patients who live in remote areas may be needed.

results.question: Can folic acid protect against congenital heart defects in Down syndrome?
rewritten: Does folic acid supplementation reduce the risk of congenital heart defects in individuals with Down syndrome?
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts specifically investigated whether first-trimester folic acid use protects against heart anomalies in children with Down syndrome. The results showed no protective effect of folic acid on heart anomalies overall or on specific types of defects associated with Down syndrome. Therefore, the evidence does not support folic acid as protective against congenital heart defects in Down syndrome.

no
contexts: Several studies have suggested a protective effect of folic acid (FA (folic acid)) on congenital heart anomalies. Down syndrome (DS (down syndrome)) infants are known to have a high frequency of heart anomalies. Not all children with DS (down syndrome) suffer from heart anomalies, which raises the question whether maternal factors might affect the risk of these anomalies. Our objectives were to investigate whether first-trimester FA (folic acid) use protects against heart anomalies among DS (down syndrome) children.

Women with liveborn DS (down syndrome) children participating in the Slone Epidemiology Center Birth Defects Study between 1976 and 1997 were included. We performed case-control analyses using DS (down syndrome), with heart anomalies as cases and DS (down syndrome), without heart anomalies as controls. Subanalyses were performed for defects that have been associated with FA (folic acid) in non-DS (down syndrome) populations (conotruncal, ventricular septal [VSD]) and for those that are associated with DS (ostium secundum type atrial septal defects [ASD (autism spectrum disorder)]and endocardial cushion defects [ECD]). Exposure was defined as the use of any FA (folic acid)-containing product for an average of at least 4 days per week during the first 12 weeks of pregnancy, whereas no exposure was defined as no use of FA (folic acid) in these 12 weeks.
Fetuses with CHD (congenital heart defects) in the Paris registry of congenital malformations and cohort of children with CHD (Epicard).

Of the 223 cases, 110 (49%) were exposed versus 84 (46%) of the 184 controls. After adjustment for possible confounders, no protective effect of FA (folic acid) was found on heart anomalies overall (OR 0.95, 95% CI (confidence interval): 0.61-1.47) nor separately for conotruncal defects, VSDs, ASDs, or ECDs.

It is postulated that some aspects of methotrexate toxicity may be related to its action as an anti-folate. Folic acid (FA (folic acid)) is often given as an adjunct to methotrexate therapy, but there is no conclusive proof that it decreases the toxicity of methotrexate and there is a theoretical risk that it may decrease the efficacy of methotrexate.
results.reference: Our study does not show a protective effect of FA on heart anomalies among infants with DS.

results.question: Are there mental health differences between francophone and non-francophone populations in manitoba?
rewritten: Are there differences in the prevalence and types of mental health disorders between Francophone and non-Francophone populations in Manitoba, Canada?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that outside urban areas, Francophones in Manitoba have lower rates of diagnosed substance use disorder and suicide/suicide attempts compared to non-Francophones, but no differences were found in rates of mood disorders, anxiety disorders, dementia, or any mental disorders after adjusting for confounders. However, Francophones were less likely to report good mental health subjectively. This suggests some mental health differences exist between the groups.

yes
contexts: Francophones may experience poorer health due to social status, cultural differences in lifestyle and attitudes, and language barriers to health care. Our study sought to compare mental health indicators between Francophones and non-Francophones living in the province of Manitoba.

Outside urban areas, Francophones had lower rates of diagnosed substance use disorder (rate ratio [RR (relative risk)] = 0.80; 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.68 to 0.95) and of suicide and suicide attempts (RR (relative risk) = 0.59; 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.43 to 0.79), compared with non-Francophones, but no differences were found between the groups across the province in rates of diagnosed mood disorders, anxiety disorders, dementia, or any mental disorders after adjusting for age, sex, and geographic area. When surveyed, Francophones were less likely than non-Francophones to report that their mental health was excellent, very good, or good (66.9%, compared with 74.2%).

Two populations were used: one from administrative datasets housed at the Manitoba Centre for Health Policy and the other from representative survey samples. The administrative datasets contained data from physician billings, hospitalizations, prescription drug use, education, and social services use, and surveys included indicators on language variables and on self-rated health.

Four hundred and forty-three women, aged 42-52 years, enrolled in the Study of Women's Health Across the Nation in Pittsburgh and participated in the Mental Health Study. Psychiatric interviews obtained information on lifetime psychiatric disorders at baseline and on occurrences of MDD (major depressive disorder) episodes annually. Psychosocial and health-related data were collected annually. Cox multivariable analyses were conducted separately for women with and without a MDD (major depressive disorder) history at baseline.

The point prevalence of pain was about 50%, the 6-month prevalence 75.5% and the 12-month prevalence 76.5%. The patients' most frequent complaints were low back pain, headache and shoulder and neck pain. Patients with affective disorders most frequently had pain complaints, followed by those with neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders and those with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizotypic and delusional disorders. Almost 10% of all patients reported pain continuing at least 3 months in the past year. Impairment and unfitness for work were related to specific psychiatric diagnosis. Statistically significant risk factors for pain were depression (OR=6.05) and the number of past admissions to psychiatric hospitals (OR=3.609).
results.reference: The discrepancy in how Francophones view their mental health and their rates of diagnosed mental disorders may be related to health seeking behaviours in the Francophone population. Community and government agencies should try to improve the mental health of this population through mental health promotion and by addressing language and cultural barriers to health services.

results.question: Does type 1 diabetes mellitus affect Achilles tendon response to a 10 km run?
rewritten: Does type 1 diabetes mellitus alter the biomechanical and histopathological response of the Achilles tendon following a 10-kilometer running exercise?
results.answer:
The study comparing Achilles tendon load-response in participants with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and controls found no difference in baseline tendon structure or response to load after a 10 km run. Neither group showed a tendon response over the 4 days post-exercise, indicating that T1DM does not affect Achilles tendon response to this exercise.

no
contexts: Achilles tendon structure deteriorates 2-days after maximal loading in elite athletes. The load-response behaviour of tendons may be altered in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus)) as hyperglycaemia accelerates collagen cross-linking. This study compared Achilles tendon load-response in participants with T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and controls.

Participants were 7 individuals with T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and 10 controls. All regularly ran distances greater than 5 km and VISA-A scores indicated good tendon function (T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) = 94 ± 11, control = 94 ± 10). There were no diabetic complications and HbA1c (hemoglobin A1c) was 8.7 ± 2.6 mmol/mol for T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and 5.3 ± 0.4 mmol/mol for control groups. Baseline tendon structure was similar in T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) and control groups - UTC (ultrasound tissue characterisation) echo-types (I-IV) and anterior-posterior thickness were all p > 0.05. No response to load was seen in either T1DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) or control group over the 4-days post exercise.

Achilles tendon structure was quantified at day-0, day-2 and day-4 after a 10 km run. Ultrasound tissue characterisation (UTC (ultrasound tissue characterisation)) measures tendon structural integrity by classifying pixels as echo-type I, II, III or IV. Echo-type I has the most aligned collagen fibrils and IV has the least.

Since insulin therapy might have an atherogenic effect, we studied the relationship between cumulative insulin dose and atherosclerosis in type 1 diabetes. We have focused on patients with type 1 diabetes instead of type 2 diabetes to minimise the effect of insulin resistance as a potential confounder.

Impaired fasting glucose (IFG (impaired fasting glucose)) below the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)) is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions. The study goal was to determine whether pre-operative fasting blood glucose (fB-glu) is associated with an increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).
results.reference: Active individuals with T1DM do not have a heightened Achilles tendon response to load, which suggests no increased risk of tendon injury. We cannot extrapolate these findings to sedentary individuals with T1DM.

results.question: Fragility of the esophageal mucosa: a pathognomonic endoscopic sign of primary eosinophilic esophagitis?
rewritten: Is fragility of the esophageal mucosa a pathognomonic endoscopic sign of primary eosinophilic esophagitis?
results.answer:
The first abstract describes "fragile esophageal mucosa" as a possibly pathognomonic sign of primary eosinophilic esophagitis, introducing the term "crêpe-paper" mucosa specifically in this context. This suggests that mucosal fragility observed endoscopically is characteristic and potentially diagnostic of the disease. No other abstracts contradict this finding.

yes
contexts: Primary eosinophilic esophagitis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus, evokes recurrent dysphagia. Endoscopy is often unremarkable, and no consensus exists regarding management of resultant dysphagia. The response of a series of patients with primary eosinophilic esophagitis to dilation is reported together with a description of a possibly pathognomonic sign: fragile esophageal mucosa, for which the term "crêpe-paper" mucosa is introduced.

The esophageal mucosa had a normal appearance on 160 endoscopic studies (Group 1) and VLEM were the only mucosal abnormalities in 41 endoscopies (Group 2). Histology was normal in 92 of 160 biopsies (57.5%) from Group 1, and 1 of 41 biopsies (2.4%) from Group 2. Most patients in Group 2 had eosinophilic esophagitis (34 of 41, 83%, specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.5, p>0.001) which was of moderate to severe intensity (31 of 34, 91.2%, specificity 0.88, sensitivity 0.73, p<0.001).

We observed an endoscopic abnormally in a group of children with histological esophagitis. We termed this finding "vertical lines in esophageal mucosa" (VLEM). We examined the relationship between the presence of VLEM and significant histologic changes in esophageal mucosal biopsies.
Five men underwent endoscopy because of dysphagia confirmed (clinically, endoscopically, and histologically) to be caused by primary eosinophilic esophagitis and were treated by bouginage.

Between January 1, 1992, and August 31, 1994, the senior author (JFF) performed 255 esophageal biopsies. The procedure reports, available endoscopic photographs, and histology reports were reviewed to establish the endoscopic and histologic appearance of the esophageal mucosa. Intraepithelial cells were counted in a blind review of 42 randomly selected biopsies.
results.reference: Primary eosinophilic esophagitis is characterized by fragile esophageal mucosa that readily tears in response to minor trauma during otherwise uneventful diagnostic endoscopy. This "crêpe-paper" sign may alert endoscopists to the presence of the disease when other mucosal alterations are lacking. Dilation is effective for patients with symptoms with minimal morbidity, despite development of disquieting lesions in response to the procedure.

results.question: Does cup-cage reconstruction with oversized cups provide initial stability in THA for osteoporotic acetabular fractures?
rewritten: Does cup-cage reconstruction using oversized acetabular cups provide initial biomechanical stability in total hip arthroplasty for patients with osteoporotic acetabular fractures?
results.answer:
The study reports that immediate THA using an oversized acetabular component with a cup-cage construct was performed in elderly patients with osteoporotic acetabular fractures. At 1 year, most components showed migration within acceptable limits for primary THA, indicating initial stability, although some components exceeded these limits. Overall, the contact surface and migration data suggest that cup-cage reconstruction with oversized cups can provide initial stability in this context.

yes
contexts: This study measured acetabular component stability and the initial surface contact achieved between the acetabular component and unfractured region of the pelvis after THA (total hip arthroplasty) using an oversized acetabular component and cup-cage reconstruction.

The incidence of acetabular fractures in osteoporotic patients is increasing. Immediate total hip arthroplasty (THA (total hip arthroplasty)) has potential advantages, but achieving acetabular component stability is challenging and, at early followup, reported revision rates for loosening are high.QUESTIONS/

Between November 2011 and November 2013, we treated 40 acute acetabular fractures in patients older than 70 years of age. Of these, 12 (30%) underwent immediate THA (total hip arthroplasty) using an oversized acetabular component with screws inserted only into the ilium and a cup-cage construct. Postoperatively all patients were mobilized without weightbearing restrictions. Indications for immediate THA (total hip arthroplasty) after acetabular fractures were displaced articular comminution deemed unreducible. Eleven of the 12 were prospectively studied to evaluate the initial stability of the reconstructions using radiostereometric analysis. One of the patients died of a pulmonary embolism after surgery, and the remaining 10 (median age, 81 years; range, 72-86 years) were studied. Of these, five were analyzed at 1 year and five were analyzed at 2 years. Acetabular component migration was defined as acceptable if less than the limits for primary THA (total hip arthroplasty) that predict later loosening (1.76 mm of proximal migration and 2.53° of sagittal rotation). The contact surface between the acetabular component and ilium in direct continuity with the sacroiliac joint, and the ischium and pubis in direct continuity with the symphysis pubis, was measured on postoperative CT scans.

To determine the relationship between injury severity surrogates and other patient factors with the development and severity of heterotopic ossification (HO (heterotopic ossification)) following open reduction internal fixation of acetabular fractures treated with a posterior approach.

At 1 year the median proximal migration was 0.83 mm (range, 0.09-5.13 mm) and sagittal rotation was 1.3° (range, 0.1°-7.4°). Three of the 10 components had migration above the suggested limits for primary THA (total hip arthroplasty) at 1 year postoperatively. The contact surface achieved at surgery between the acetabular component and pelvis ranged from 11 to 17 cm(2) (15%-27% of each component).
results.reference: The majority of acetabular components in this cohort were stable despite the small contact surface achieved between the component and pelvic bone. Three of 10 migrated in excess of the limits that predict later loosening in primary THA but it remains to be seen whether these limits apply to this selected group of frail osteoporotic patients. We continue to use this technique routinely to treat patients with the same indications, but since the analysis of these data we have added screw fixation of the acetabular component to the ischial tuberosity and the superior pubic ramus.

results.question: Pulmonary valve replacement in adults late after repair of tetralogy of fallot: are we operating too late?
rewritten: Is pulmonary valve replacement performed in adult patients late after surgical repair of tetralogy of Fallot associated with delayed intervention and adverse clinical outcomes?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that chronic pulmonary regurgitation after TOF repair leads to right ventricular dilation and increased risk of sudden cardiac death, suggesting that delayed intervention may allow for progressive RV dysfunction. The study measuring RV volumes and function before and after pulmonary valve replacement implies that timing of surgery is a critical issue, supporting the concern that surgery might be performed too late to prevent adverse remodeling.

yes
contexts: We studied 25 consecutive adult patients who underwent PVR (pulmonary valve replacement) for significant PR (pulmonary regurgitation) late after repair of TOF (tetralogy of fallot). Radionuclide angiography was performed in all at a mean of 8.2 months (+/- 8 months) before PVR (pulmonary valve replacement) and repeated at a mean of 28.0 months (+/- 22.8 months) after the operation. Right ventricular (RV (right ventricular)) end-systolic volume (RVESV (rv) end-systolic volume)), RV (right ventricular) end-diastolic volume (RVEDV (rv end-diastolic volume)) and RV (right ventricular) ejection fraction (RVEF (rv ejection fraction)) were measured.

Chronic pulmonary regurgitation (PR (pulmonary regurgitation)) following repair of tetralogy of Fallot (TOF (tetralogy of fallot)) leads to RV (right ventricular) dilation and an increased incidence of sudden cardiac death in adult patients.

The purpose of this study is to evaluate right ventricular (RV (right ventricular)) volume and function after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR (pulmonary valve replacement)) and to address the issue of optimal surgical timing in these patients.

Hospital mortality was 2.3% for MV (mitral valve) repair and 12.5% for MV (mitral valve) replacement (p = 0.03). Actuarial survival at 2.5 years was 92 ± 3.2% for MV (mitral valve) repair and 73 ± 7.9% for MV (mitral valve) replacement (p = 0.02). At a mean follow-up of 2.3 years (median, 1.6 years), in the MV (mitral valve) repair group LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction) significantly increased (from 0.308 ± 0.077 to 0.382 ± 0.095, p<0.0001) and LV (left ventricular) dimensions significantly decreased (p = 0.0001). On the other hand, in the MV (mitral valve) replacement group LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction) did not significantly change (from 0.336 ± 0.076 to 0.31 ± 0.11, p = 0.56) and the reduction of LV (left ventricular) dimensions was not significant. Mitral valve replacement was identified as the only predictor of hospital (odds ratio, 6; 95% confidence interval, 1.1 to 31; p = 0.03) and overall mortality (hazard ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval, 1.1 to 8.9; p = 0.02).

One-hundred and thirty-two patients with severe functional MR (mitral regurgitation) and systolic dysfunction (mean ejection fraction 0.32 ± 0.078) underwent mitral surgery in the same time frame. The decision to replace rather than repair the MV (mitral valve) was taken when 1 or more echocardiographic predictors of repair failure were identified at the preoperative echocardiogram. Eighty-five patients (64.4%) received MV (mitral valve) repair and 47 patients (35.6%) received MV (mitral valve) replacement. Preoperative characteristics were comparable between the 2 groups. Only ejection fraction was significantly lower in the MV (mitral valve) repair group (0.308 ± 0.077 vs 0.336 ± 0.076, p = 0.04).
results.reference: Right ventricular recovery following PVR for chronic significant pulmonary regurgitation after repair of TOF may be compromised in the adult population. In order to maintain adequate RV contractility, pulmonary valve implant in these patients should be considered before RV function deteriorates.

results.question: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis: a premalignant condition?
rewritten: Is xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis a premalignant condition associated with an increased risk of gallbladder carcinoma?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that p53 mutation and PCNA expression, markers associated with malignancy, are significantly lower in Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis (XGC) compared to gallbladder carcinoma (GBC). Additionally, the beta-catenin expression pattern in XGC resembles that of chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladders rather than GBC. These findings suggest that XGC does not exhibit molecular features typical of a premalignant condition.

no
contexts: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis (XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis)) is an uncommon variant of chronic cholecystitis, characterized by marked thickening of the gallbladder wall and dense local adhesions. It often mimics a gallbladder carcinoma (GBC (gallbladder carcinoma)), and may coexist with GBC (gallbladder carcinoma), leading to a diagnostic dilemma. Furthermore, the premalignant nature of this entity is not known. This study was undertaken to assess the p53, PCNA and beta-catenin expression in XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis) in comparison to GBC (gallbladder carcinoma) and chronic inflammation.

p53 mutation was positive in 52% of GBC (gallbladder carcinoma) cases and 3% of XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis), but was not expressed in chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladders. p53 expression was lower in XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis) than in GBC (P<0.0001). PCNA expression was seen in 65% of GBC (gallbladder carcinoma) cases and 11% of XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis), but not in chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladders. PCNA expression was higher in GBC (gallbladder carcinoma) than XGC (P=0.0001), but there was no significant difference between the XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis), chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladder groups. Beta-catenin expression was positive in the GBC (gallbladder carcinoma), XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis), chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladder groups. But the expression pattern in XGC (xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis), chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladders was homogenously membranous, whereas in GBC (gallbladder carcinoma) the membranous expression pattern was altered to cytoplasmic and nuclear.

Sections from paraffin-embedded blocks of surgically resected specimens of GBC (69 cases), XGC (65), chronic cholecystitis (18) and control gallbladder (10) were stained with the monoclonal antibodies to p53 and PCNA, and a polyclonal antibody to beta-catenin. p53 expression was scored as the percentage of nuclei stained. PCNA expression was scored as the product of the percentage of nuclei stained and the intensity of the staining (1-3). A cut-off value of 80 for this score was taken as a positive result. Beta-catenin expression was scored as type of expression-membranous, cytoplasmic or nuclear staining.
We tested the hypothesis that the treatment of patients with acute cholecystitis (AC (acute cholecystitis)) would be improved under the care of laparoscopic specialists.
The purpose of this study is to examine whether or not well differentiated (w-d) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC (hepatocellular carcinoma)) is indeed clinically early cancer.
results.reference: The expression of p53, PCNA and beta-catenin in XGC was significantly different from GBC and similar to chronic cholecystitis, thus indicating the inflammatory nature of XGC and may not support a premalignant nature of the lesion.

results.question: Does TDP-43 type confer a distinct pattern of atrophy in frontotemporal lobar degeneration?
rewritten: Does transactive response DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) pathological subtype confer a distinct neuroanatomical atrophy pattern in frontotemporal lobar degeneration?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that different TDP-43 types in frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) are associated with distinct patterns of brain atrophy on MRI. Specifically, type 1 shows frontotemporal and parietal atrophy, type 2 shows predominantly anterior temporal lobe atrophy, and type 3 shows predominantly posterior frontal atrophy, supporting the idea that TDP-43 type confers distinct atrophy patterns.

yes
contexts: To determine whether TDP-43 type is associated with distinct patterns of brain atrophy on MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) in subjects with pathologically confirmed frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)).

In this case-control study, we identified all subjects with a pathologic diagnosis of FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) with TDP-43 immunoreactive inclusions (FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP) and at least one volumetric head MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) scan (n = 42). In each case we applied published criteria for subclassification of FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP into FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP types 1-3. Voxel-based morphometry was used to compare subjects with each of the different FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP types to age- and gender-matched normal controls (n = 30). We also assessed different pathologic and genetic variants within, and across, the different types.

Twenty-two subjects were classified as FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP type 1, 9 as type 2, and 11 as type 3. We identified different patterns of atrophy across the types with type 1 showing frontotemporal and parietal atrophy, type 2 predominantly anterior temporal lobe atrophy, and type 3 predominantly posterior frontal atrophy. Within the FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP type 1 group, those with a progranulin mutation had significantly more lateral temporal lobe atrophy than those without. All type 2 subjects were diagnosed with semantic dementia. Subjects with a pathologic diagnosis of FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) with motor neuron degeneration had a similar pattern of atrophy, regardless of whether they were type 1 or type 3.

To investigate whether the presence of hippocampal atrophy (HCA (hippocampal atrophy)) on MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) in Alzheimer's disease (AD (alzheimer's disease)) leads to a more rapid decline in cognitive function. To investigate whether cognitively unimpaired controls and depressed subjects with HCA (hippocampal atrophy) are at higher risk than those without HCA (hippocampal atrophy) of developing dementia.
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) was collected for genotyping from 73 term newborns suffering from TTN and 55 healthy controls from a Caucasian cohort.
results.reference: Although there are different patterns of atrophy across the different FTLD-TDP types, it appears that genetic and pathologic factors may also affect the patterns of atrophy.

results.question: Is oncoplastic surgery a contraindication for accelerated partial breast radiation using the interstitial multicatheter brachytherapy method?
rewritten: Is oncoplastic breast surgery a contraindication for accelerated partial breast irradiation using interstitial multicatheter brachytherapy in early-stage breast cancer patients?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts include a retrospective analysis of 136 breasts treated with breast-conserving oncoplastic surgery followed by adjuvant accelerated partial breast irradiation (APBI) using doses consistent with brachytherapy methods. This indicates that oncoplastic surgery was performed prior to APBI without being a contraindication. Therefore, oncoplastic surgery does not appear to be a contraindication for accelerated partial breast radiation using interstitial multicatheter brachytherapy.

no
contexts: To evaluate accelerated partial breast irradiation (APBI (accelerated partial breast irradiation)) in patients after oncoplastic surgery for early breast cancer.

A retrospective analysis of 136 breasts of 134 patients, who received breast-conserving oncoplastic surgery for low-risk breast cancer between 2002 and 2010 in the Universities of Vienna and Luebeck followed by adjuvant APBI (accelerated partial breast irradiation) applying total doses of pulse dose rate of 50.4 Gy or high-dose rate (HDR (high-dose rate)) of 32 Gy over 4 days. Target volume definition was performed by the use of surgical-free margin data, related to intraoperatively fixed clip positions, pre- and postoperative imaging, and palpation.

Immediate breast reconstruction (IBR (immediate breast reconstruction)) provides psychological benefit to many early breast cancer patients however concerns persist regarding its potential impact on chemotherapy delivery. We investigated the association between IBR (immediate breast reconstruction), complications and adjuvant chemotherapy delivery.

Clinically positive axillary nodes are widely considered a contraindication to sentinel lymph node (SLN (sentinel lymph node)) biopsy in breast cancer, yet no data support this mandate. In fact, data from the era of axillary lymph node dissection (ALND (axillary lymph node dissection)) suggest that clinical examination of the axilla is falsely positive in as many as 30% of cases. Here we report the results of SLN (sentinel lymph node) biopsy in a selected group of breast cancer patients with palpable axillary nodes classified as either moderately or highly suspicious for metastasis.

Comparisons were made between 107 patients who received IBR (immediate breast reconstruction) and 113 who received mastectomy alone. Those receiving IBR (immediate breast reconstruction) were on average younger, with lower body mass index (BMI (body mass index)) and better prognoses. Overall complication rates were comparable (mastectomy alone: 45.1% versus IBR (immediate breast reconstruction): 35.5%, p = 0.2). There was more return to surgery in the IBR (immediate breast reconstruction) group with 11.5% of tissue expanders requiring removal, whilst more seromas occurred in the mastectomy group. There was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy.
results.reference: These preliminary results suggest the feasibility of multicatheter APBI after oncoplastic breast-conserving surgery in selected low-risk breast cancer patients; however, special attention to target volume definition is needed. Further prospective investigations with long follow-up are needed to define the real value of the procedure.

results.question: Diagnostic characteristics of child bipolar I disorder: does the "Treatment of Early Age Mania (team)" sample generalize?
rewritten: Do the diagnostic characteristics of pediatric bipolar I disorder observed in the Treatment of Early Age Mania (TEAM) study sample generalize to broader clinical populations?
results.answer:
The context indicates that the TEAM sample and the Phenomenology sample were similar in age and demographics, but the TEAM sample had significantly more severe symptoms such as ultradian rapid cycling, psychosis, and suicidality. This suggests that while the TEAM sample shares some characteristics with other child bipolar I disorder populations, it may represent a more severe subset, limiting full generalizability.

no
contexts: Subjects (N = 247) were outpatients who participated in either the National Institute of Mental Health-funded Phenomenology and Course of Pediatric Bipolar Disorders study or the Treatment of Early Age Mania (TEAM (treatment of early age mania)) study. Both studies required that subjects have current DSM-IV bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed phase) and a Children's Global Assessment Scale (CGAS (children's global assessment scale)) score<or=60. All subjects had elation and/or grandiosity. Subjects in the Phenomenology study were obtained from 1995 to 1998 by consecutive new case ascertainment from designated pediatric and psychiatric facilities. Subjects in the TEAM (treatment of early age mania) RCT (randomized controlled trial) were recruited from media and community sources between March 2003 and March 2005. Assessment instruments included the Washington University in St. Louis Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia, given separately to parents about their children and to children about themselves, and the CGAS (children's global assessment scale). Logistic regression was used for comparisons.

The TEAM (treatment of early age mania) and Phenomenology groups were similar in age (10.4 [SD = 2.3], 10.9 [SD = 2.3]years, respectively) and other demography. Both had long current episode duration (4.8 [SD = 2.4], 3.2 [SD = 2.3]years) and low lifetime use of any mood stabilizer (23.6%, 35.0%). Many mania symptoms and ultradian rapid cycling, psychosis, and suicidality were significantly more prevalent in the RCT (randomized controlled trial) sample.

To examine the representativeness of a randomized controlled trial (RCT (randomized controlled trial)) sample versus one obtained by consecutive new case ascertainment, for subjects with child bipolar I disorder.

Probands were 83 participants in an ongoing controlled study of PEA-BP (blood pressure). The PEA-BP (blood pressure) phenotype was defined by DSM-IV mania with at least one of the cardinal symptoms of mania (elation and/or grandiosity) to avoid diagnosing mania only by symptoms that overlapped with those for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD (attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder)). Comprehensive assessment of the probands included separate Washington University in St. Louis Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (WASH-U-KSADS) interviews of parents about their children and of children about themselves. Hypersexuality and uninhibited people-seeking were assessed from the corresponding WASH-U-KSADS items. Microsatellite genotyping of the AVPR1A (arginine vasopressin v1a receptor) repeats was conducted using fluorescently labeled primers and detected by laser-induced fluorescence. Alleles were determined with the assistance of semi-automated allele-calling software. There were 32 complete, biological trios (28 informative families) for the GATA repeat and 34 complete, biological trios (30 informative families) for the complex repeat. Data were analyzed using case-control and family-based association methods.

Participants with major affective disorders in the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH (national institute of mental health)) Collaborative Depression Study (CDS (collaborative depression study)) were followed prospectively for up to 25 years. A total of 909 participants meeting prospective diagnostic criteria for major depressive and bipolar disorders were followed through 4204 mood cycles. Suicidal behavior was defined as suicide attempts or completions. Mixed-effects, grouped-time survival analysis assessed risk of suicidal behavior and differential effects of risk factors for suicidal behavior by polarity. In addition to polarity, the main effects of age, gender, hopelessness, married status, prior suicide attempts and active substance abuse were modeled, with mood cycle as the unit of analysis.
results.reference: Generalization of the RCT sample was supported, because only 7.8% of Phenomenology subjects did not fit the RCT criteria. Nevertheless, because the RCT subjects were more severely ill, it is unclear if treatment findings from the RCT will be applicable to children with less severe mania.

results.question: Estimation of basal metabolic rate in Chinese: are the current prediction equations applicable?
rewritten: Are the existing basal metabolic rate prediction equations valid and accurate for estimating basal metabolic rate in the Chinese population?
results.answer:
The study developed a new BMR prediction equation specifically for Chinese adults and found that it had higher accuracy compared to commonly used existing equations such as Harris-Benedict, Henry, and Mifflin. This suggests that current prediction equations may not be fully applicable to the Chinese population, especially across a wide BMI range, and a tailored equation improves estimation accuracy.

no
contexts: Measurement of basal metabolic rate (BMR (basal metabolic rate)) is suggested as a tool to estimate energy requirements. Therefore, BMR (basal metabolic rate) prediction equations have been developed in multiple populations because indirect calorimetry is not always feasible. However, there is a paucity of data on BMR (basal metabolic rate) measured in overweight and obese adults living in Asia and equations developed for this group of interest. The aim of this study was to develop a new BMR (basal metabolic rate) prediction equation for Chinese adults applicable for a large BMI (body mass index) range and compare it with commonly used prediction equations.

Subjects were 121 men and 111 women (age: 21-67 years, BMI (body mass index): 16-41 kg/m(2)). Height, weight, and BMR (basal metabolic rate) were measured. Continuous open-circuit indirect calorimetry using a ventilated hood system for 30 min was used to measure BMR (basal metabolic rate). A regression equation was derived using stepwise regression and accuracy was compared to 6 existing equations (Harris-Benedict, Henry, Liu, Yang, Owen and Mifflin). Additionally, the newly derived equation was cross-validated in a separate group of 70 Chinese subjects (26 men and 44 women, age: 21-69 years, BMI (body mass index): 17-39 kg/m(2)).

The high prevalence of obesity in African American (AA (american)) women may result, in part, from a lower resting metabolic rate (RMR (resting metabolic rate)) than non-AA (american) women. If true, AA (american) women should require fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight. Our objective was to determine in the setting of a controlled feeding study, if AA (american) women required fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight.

The equation developed from our data was: BMR (kJ/d) = 52.6 x weight (kg) + 828 x gender + 1960 (women = 0, men = 1; R(2) = 0.81). The accuracy rate (within 10 % accurate) was 78 % which compared well to Owen (70 %), Henry (67 %), Mifflin (67 %), Liu (58 %), Harris-Benedict (45 %) and Yang (37 %) for the whole range of BMI (body mass index). For a BMI (body mass index) greater than 23, the Singapore equation reached an accuracy rate of 76 %. Cross-validation proved an accuracy rate of 80 %.

Elevated resting heart rate (RHR (resting heart rate)) is a neglected marker in cardiovascular risk factor studies of sub-Saharan African populations. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of elevated RHR (resting heart rate) and other risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD (cardiovascular disease)) and to investigate any associations between RHR (resting heart rate) and these risk factors in a rural population in Ghana.
results.reference: To date, the newly developed Singapore equation is the most accurate BMR prediction equation in Chinese and is applicable for use in a large BMI range including those overweight and obese.

results.question: Does rugby headgear prevent concussion?
rewritten: Does the use of protective rugby headgear reduce the incidence and severity of sports-related concussions in rugby players?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts discuss attitudes toward protective headgear and concussion incidence in sports but do not specifically address whether rugby headgear prevents concussion. The data show that players believe headgear can prevent concussion, but coaches are less convinced, and actual usage is low. There is no direct evidence presented about the effectiveness of rugby headgear in preventing concussion.

no
contexts: To examine the attitudes of players and coaches to the use of protective headgear, particularly with respect to the prevention of concussion.

Although the players tended to believe that the headgear could prevent concussion (62%), the coaches were less convinced (33%). Despite the players' belief that headgear offers protection against concussion, only a minority reported wearing headgear (27%) and few (24%) felt that its use should be made mandatory. Common reasons for not wearing headgear were "its use is not mandatory", "it is uncomfortable", and "it costs too much".

A total of 150 patients were enrolled. The majority (67%) of concussions were sports related. Among sports-related concussions, soccer (30%), football (11%), lacrosse (8%), and basketball (8%) injuries were most common. More than one third (39%) reported return to play (RTP (return to play)) on the day of the injury. Physician follow-up was equivalent for sport and nonsport concussions (2 weeks, 58%; 4 weeks, 64%). Sports-related concussion patients were more likely to follow up with a trainer (2 weeks, 25% vs. 10%, p = 0.06; 4 weeks, 29% vs. 8%, p<0.01). Of the patients who did RTP (return to play) or normal activities at 2 weeks (44%), more than one third (35%) were symptomatic, and most (58%) did not receive medical clearance. Of the patients who had returned to activities at 4 weeks (64%), less than one quarter (23%) were symptomatic, and most (54%) received medical clearance.

A questionnaire designed to assess attitudes to headgear was administered to 63 players from four different Canadian teams, each representing a different level of play (high school, university, community club, national). In addition, coaches from all four levels were questioned about team policies and their personal opinions about the use of headgear to prevent concussion.

Concussions are commonly diagnosed in pediatric patients presenting to the emergency department (ED (emergency department)). The primary objective of this study was to evaluate compliance with ED (emergency department) discharge instructions for concussion management.
results.reference: Although most players in the study believe that rugby headgear may prevent concussion, only a minority reported wearing it. Coaches tended to be less convinced than the players that rugby headgear can prevent concussion.

results.question: Spinal subdural hematoma: a sequela of a ruptured intracranial aneurysm?
rewritten: Is spinal subdural hematoma a potential complication or sequela of ruptured intracranial cerebral aneurysm?
results.answer:
The provided case report describes a spinal subdural hematoma occurring after a subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm, noting that such a case had never been reported before. This indicates that spinal subdural hematoma can indeed be a sequela of a ruptured intracranial aneurysm, at least in rare instances.

yes
contexts: A case of spinal subdural hematoma (SSDH (spinal subdural hematoma)) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH (subarachnoid hemorrhage)) because of a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm is described. Such a case has never been reported.

A 52-year-old woman underwent a craniotomy for a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm. A computed tomography scan showed that SAH (subarachnoid hemorrhage) existed predominantly in the posterior fossa and subdural hematoma beneath the cerebellar tentorium. Intrathecal administration of urokinase, IV administration of fasudil hydrochloride, and continuous cerebrospinal fluid (CSF (cerebrospinal fluid)) evacuation via cisternal drainage were performed as prophylactic treatments for vasospasm. On the sixth postoperative day, the patient complained of severe lower back and buttock pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a subdural hematoma in the lumbosacral region. Although the mass effect was extensive, the patient showed no neurologic symptoms other than the sciatica. She was treated conservatively. The hematoma dissolved gradually and had diminished completely 15 weeks later. Her pain gradually subsided, and she was discharged 7 weeks later without any neurologic deficit.

The rate of aortic aneurysm rupture correlates with the aneurysm's diameter, and a higher rate of rupture is observed in patients with larger aneurysms. According to the literature, contradictory results concerning the relationship between atmospheric pressure and aneurysm size have been reported.AIM: In this paper, we assessed the influence of changes in atmospheric pressure on abdominal aneurysm ruptures in relationship to the aneurysm's size.

The records of 223 patients with ruptured abdominal aneurysms were evaluated. All of the patients had been admitted to the department in the period 1997-2007 from the Silesia region. The atmospheric pressures on the day of the rupture and on the days both before the rupture and between the rupture events were compared. The size of the aneurysm was also considered in the analysis.

There were no statistically significant differences in pressure between the days of rupture and the remainder of the days within an analysed period. The highest frequency of the admission of patients with a ruptured aortic aneurysm was observed during periods of winter and spring, when the highest mean values of atmospheric pressure were observed; however, this observation was not statistically confirmed. A statistically non-significant trend towards the higher rupture of large aneurysms (>7 cm) was observed in the cases where the pressure increased between the day before the rupture and the day of the rupture. This trend was particularly pronounced in patients suffering from hypertension (p = 0.1).
results.reference: Although the exact mechanism of SSDH in this case is unclear, we speculate that this SSDH was a hematoma that migrated from the intracranial subdural space. Low CSF pressure because of continuous drainage and intrathecal thrombolytic therapy may have played an important role in the migration of the hematoma through the spinal canal. It is important to recognize the SSDH as a possible complication of the SAH accompanied with intracranial subdural hematoma.

results.question: Can shape analysis differentiate free-floating internal carotid artery thrombus from atherosclerotic plaque in patients evaluated with CTA for stroke or transient ischemic attack?
rewritten: Can morphological shape analysis differentiate free-floating thrombus from atherosclerotic plaque in the internal carotid artery of patients undergoing computed tomography angiography for acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1]-[3] demonstrates that quantitative shape analysis of lesions on CTA can differentiate free-floating intraluminal thrombus (FFT) from atherosclerotic plaque with good sensitivity (87.5%) and specificity (71.4%), supported by an area under the ROC curve of 0.85. This indicates that shape analysis is a useful tool for distinguishing FFT from plaque in patients evaluated for stroke or transient ischemic attack.

yes
contexts: Patients presenting with transient ischemic attack or stroke may have symptom-related lesions on acute computed tomography angiography (CTA (computed tomography angiography)) such as free-floating intraluminal thrombus (FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)). It is difficult to distinguish FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) from carotid plaque, but the distinction is critical as management differs. By contouring the shape of these vascular lesions ("virtual endarterectomy"), advanced morphometric analysis can be performed. The objective of our study is to determine whether quantitative shape analysis can accurately differentiate FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) from atherosclerotic plaque.

We collected 23 consecutive cases of suspected carotid FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) seen on CTA (13 men, 65 ± 10 years; 10 women, 65.5 ± 8.8 years). True-positive FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) cases (FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)+) were defined as filling defects resolving with anticoagulant therapy versus false-positives (FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)-), which remained unchanged. Lesion volumes were extracted from CTA (computed tomography angiography) images and quantitative shape descriptors were computed. The five most discriminative features were used to construct receiver operator characteristic (ROC (receiver operator characteristic)) curves and to generate three machine-learning classifiers. Average classification accuracy was determined by cross-validation.

Follow-up imaging confirmed sixteen FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)+ and seven FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)- cases. Five shape descriptors delineated FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)+ from FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)- cases. The logistic regression model produced from combining all five shape features demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.5% and a specificity of 71.4% with an area under the ROC (receiver operator characteristic) curve = 0.85 ± 0.09. Average accuracy for each classifier ranged from 65.2%-76.4%.

Extracranial internal carotid artery stenosis is a risk factor for perioperative stroke in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery (CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery)). Although selective and non-selective methods of preoperative carotid screening have been advocated, it remains unclear if this screening is clinically relevant.AIM: To test whether selective carotid screening is as effective as non-selective screening in detecting significant carotid disease.

The case records of patients consecutively undergoing CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery) were reviewed. Patients were stratified retrospectively into high- or low-risk groups according to risk factors for significant carotid stenosis and perioperative stroke: peripheral vascular disease (PVD (peripheral vascular disease)), carotid bruit, diabetes mellitus, age>70 years and/or history of cerebrovascular disease. Prevalence of carotid stenosis detected by ultrasonography, surgical management and perioperative stroke rates were determined in each group.
results.reference: We identified five quantitative shape descriptors of carotid FFT. This shape "signature" shows potential for supplementing conventional lesion characterization in cases of suspected FFT.

results.question: Dementia and aphasia in motor neuron disease: an underrecognised association?
rewritten: Is there an underrecognized association between dementia and aphasia in patients with motor neuron disease?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that patients with motor neuron disease (MND) can exhibit cognitive dysfunction and language deficits, with some cases showing frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) and semantic dementia, which are associated with dementia and aphasia. This suggests that dementia and aphasia in MND are present but may be underrecognized in clinical settings.

yes
contexts: To determine the prevalence and nature of global cognitive dysfunction and language deficits in an unselected population based cohort of patients with motor neuron disease (MND (motor neuron disease)).

A battery of neuropsychological and language tests was administered to patients presenting consecutively over a 3 year period to a regional neurology service with a new diagnosis of sporadic motor neuron disease.

Twenty-two subjects were classified as FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP type 1, 9 as type 2, and 11 as type 3. We identified different patterns of atrophy across the types with type 1 showing frontotemporal and parietal atrophy, type 2 predominantly anterior temporal lobe atrophy, and type 3 predominantly posterior frontal atrophy. Within the FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration)-TDP type 1 group, those with a progranulin mutation had significantly more lateral temporal lobe atrophy than those without. All type 2 subjects were diagnosed with semantic dementia. Subjects with a pathologic diagnosis of FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) with motor neuron degeneration had a similar pattern of atrophy, regardless of whether they were type 1 or type 3.

To investigate whether the presence of hippocampal atrophy (HCA (hippocampal atrophy)) on MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) in Alzheimer's disease (AD (alzheimer's disease)) leads to a more rapid decline in cognitive function. To investigate whether cognitively unimpaired controls and depressed subjects with HCA (hippocampal atrophy) are at higher risk than those without HCA (hippocampal atrophy) of developing dementia.
No significant differences in rate of cognitive decline, mortality or progression to dementia were found between subjects with or without HCA (hippocampal atrophy).
results.reference: The prevalence of cognitive impairment in MND in this population based study of an unselected cohort was higher than has been previously reported. Language deficits, especially anomia, may be relatively frequent in the MND population. Aphasia in MND may be masked by dysarthria and missed if not specifically examined.

results.question: Does solid culture for tuberculosis influence clinical decision making in India?
rewritten: Does the use of solid culture methods for Mycobacterium tuberculosis detection influence clinical decision-making and treatment outcomes in tuberculosis patients in India?
results.answer:
The data show that a majority of culture-positive patients started treatment before culture results were available, and only a small number initiated or modified treatment based on culture or DST results. This suggests that while culture results are obtained, they have limited impact on changing clinical decisions in this setting.

no
contexts: In a retrospective review of 150 culture-positive and 150 culture-negative consecutively sampled tuberculosis (TB (tuberculosis)) suspects, treatment decisions were analysed at presentation, after the availability of culture detection results and after the availability of drug susceptibility testing (DST (drug susceptibility testing)) culture results.
To investigate the impact of solid culture on Löwenstein-Jensen medium on clinical decision making.

A total of 124 (82.7%) culture-positive patients and 35 (23.3%) culture-negative patients started anti-tuberculosis treatment prior to receiving their culture results; 101 patients (33.7%) returned for their results; two (1.3%) initiated treatment based on positive culture and no culture-negative patients discontinued treatment. DST (drug susceptibility testing) was performed on 119 (79.3%) positive cultures: 30 (25.2%) showed any resistance, eight (6.7%) showed multidrug resistance and one (0.84%) showed extensively drug-resistant TB (tuberculosis). Twenty-eight patients (23.5%) returned for their DST (drug susceptibility testing) results. Based on DST (drug susceptibility testing), treatment was modified in four patients (3.4%).

To determine whether the OraQuick® HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA) in sputum is a valid tool for HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) surveillance among TB (tuberculosis) patients.

A cross sectional study was carried out on sputa of patients diagnosed with tuberculosis. Sputa were tested for antibodies to HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) using OraQuick® HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA). The results were compared with results of serum ELISA.
results.reference: Using solid culture, 150 cultures need to be tested for one treatment modification and 30 for DST. The cost of the widespread application of culture will need to be balanced against its impact on treatment decisions in India.

results.question: Diffusion-weighted echo-planar MR imaging of primary parotid gland tumors: is a prediction of different histologic subtypes possible?
rewritten: Can diffusion-weighted echo-planar magnetic resonance imaging accurately differentiate histologic subtypes of primary parotid gland tumors?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that diffusion-weighted echo-planar MR imaging (epiDWI) can differentiate certain histologic subtypes of primary parotid gland tumors based on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values, such as distinguishing pleomorphic adenomas from other entities and differentiating Warthin tumors from some other tumor types. However, some malignant tumors like mucoepidermoid carcinomas and acinic cell carcinomas were not distinguishable from Warthin tumors using this method.
