Patients were divided into three groups (remission, failure and relapse) depending on the late outcome of their treatment as determined at the time of analysis, i.e. 88 months (median) years after surgery. Remission is defined as biochemical reversal of hypercortisolism with re-emergence of diurnal circadian rhythm, resolution of clinical features and adequate suppression on low-dose dexamethasone testing. Failure is defined as the absence of any of these features. Relapse is defined as the re-emergence of Cushing's disease more than one year after operation. Clinical features such as weight, sex, hypertension, associated endocrine disorders and smoking, biochemical studies including preoperative and postoperative serum cortisol, urine free cortisol, serum ACTH, radiological, histological and surgical findings were assessed in relation to these three groups to determine whether any factors could reliably predict failure or relapse after treatment.

A retrospective analysis of a contemporary series of patients with pituitary apoplexy was performed to ascertain whether the histopathological features influence the clinical presentation or the outcome.

To examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality)) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR (biochemical recurrence)). Prostate-specific antigen (PSA (prostate-specific antigen)), grade, and stage are the classic triad used to predict BCR (biochemical recurrence) after radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)). Multiple nomograms use these to predict risk of BCR (biochemical recurrence). A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR (biochemical recurrence). However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM (prostate cancer-specific mortality).

A retrospective analysis was performed in 59 patients treated for pituitary apoplexy at the University of Virginia Health System, Charlottesville, Virginia, or Groote Schuur Hospital, University of Cape Town, South Africa. The patients were divided into two groups according to the histological features of their disease: one group with infarction alone, comprising 22 patients; and the other with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage, comprising 37 patients. The presenting symptoms, clinical features, endocrinological status, and outcome were compared between the two groups.
results.reference: Transsphenoidal pituitary surgery is a safe method of treatment in patients with Cushing's disease. Operative findings, radiological and histological findings, together with early postoperative serum cortisol and urine free cortisol estimates may identify failures in treatment. Alternative treatment might then be required for these patients. Because of the risk of late relapse, patients require life-long follow-up.

results.question: Can bedside assessment reliably exclude aspiration following acute stroke?
rewritten: Can bedside clinical assessment reliably exclude aspiration pneumonia in patients following acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke?
results.answer:
The bedside assessment by a speech and language therapist showed a sensitivity of 47% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 85% for detecting aspiration, indicating it misses a significant number of aspiration cases. Even with optimized elements (weak voluntary cough and altered consciousness), sensitivity was 75% and NPV 91%, which still does not reliably exclude aspiration. Therefore, bedside assessment cannot reliably exclude aspiration following acute stroke.

no
contexts: To investigate the ability of a bedside swallowing assessment to reliably exclude aspiration following acute stroke.

94 patients underwent videofluoroscopy; 20 (21%) were seen to be aspirating, although this was not detected at the bedside in 10. In 18 (22%) of the patients the speech and language therapist considered the swallow to be unsafe. In the medical assessment, 39 patients (41%) had an unsafe swallow. Bedside assessment by a speech and language therapist gave a sensitivity of 47%, a specificity of 86%, positive predictive value (PPV (positive predictive value)) of 50% and a negative predictive value (NPV (negative predictive value)) of 85% for the presence of aspiration. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify the optimum elements of the bedside assessments for predicting the presence of aspiration. A weak voluntary cough and any alteration in conscious level gave a sensitivity of 75%, specificity of 72%, PPV (positive predictive value) of 41% and NPV (negative predictive value) of 91% for aspiration.

Patients presenting with transient ischemic attack or stroke may have symptom-related lesions on acute computed tomography angiography (CTA (computed tomography angiography)) such as free-floating intraluminal thrombus (FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus)). It is difficult to distinguish FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) from carotid plaque, but the distinction is critical as management differs. By contouring the shape of these vascular lesions ("virtual endarterectomy"), advanced morphometric analysis can be performed. The objective of our study is to determine whether quantitative shape analysis can accurately differentiate FFT (free-floating intraluminal thrombus) from atherosclerotic plaque.

We examined the placebo arm of the NINDS t-PA stroke trial to test the hypothesis that the total volume of cerebral infarction in patients with right hemisphere strokes would be greater than the volume of cerebral infarction in patients with left hemisphere strokes who have similar NIHSS (national institutes of health stroke scale) scores. The volume of stroke was determined by computerized image analysis of CT films and CT images stored on computer tape and optical disks. Cube-root transformation of lesion volume was performed for each CT. Transformed lesion volume was analyzed in a logistic regression model to predict volume of stroke by NIHSS (national institutes of health stroke scale) score for each hemisphere. Spearman rank correlation was used to determine the relation between the NIHSS (national institutes of health stroke scale) score and lesion volume.

The case records of patients consecutively undergoing CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery) were reviewed. Patients were stratified retrospectively into high- or low-risk groups according to risk factors for significant carotid stenosis and perioperative stroke: peripheral vascular disease (PVD (peripheral vascular disease)), carotid bruit, diabetes mellitus, age>70 years and/or history of cerebrovascular disease. Prevalence of carotid stenosis detected by ultrasonography, surgical management and perioperative stroke rates were determined in each group.
results.reference: Bedside assessment of swallowing lacks the necessary sensitivity to be used as a screening instrument in acute stroke, but there are concerns about the use of videofluoroscopy as a gold standard. The relative importance of aspiration and bedside assessment in predicting complications and outcome needs to be studied.

results.question: Are UK radiologists satisfied with the training and support received in suspected child abuse?
rewritten: Are radiologists in the United Kingdom satisfied with the adequacy of training and professional support provided for the diagnosis and management of suspected non-accidental injury in pediatric patients?
results.answer:
The abstract indicates that only 61% of departments had a named radiologist for skeletal surveys in suspected child abuse, with 25% of initial reports done by non-paediatric radiologists and 15% lacking ready access to paediatric radiology opinion. Additionally, 61% thought the service could be improved, and 73% would never consider providing expert evidence even with training. This suggests dissatisfaction with the current training and support.

no
contexts: Sixty-one percent of departments had a named radiologist to report their skeletal surveys, 16% assigned surveys to a random radiologist, and 23% referred them elsewhere. Only 52% of departments had a dedicated paediatric radiologist, thus in a significant proportion of departments (25%) initial reports on skeletal surveys for physical abuse were provided by non-paediatric radiologists. Fifteen percent did not have ready access to a paediatric radiology opinion. Sixty-one percent thought that the service could be improved. Expert evidence was provided by 5% of respondents. Seventy-three percent would never consider providing expert evidence, even if given adequate radiology and/or legal training.

A prospective cohort study was conducted from November 2011 to November 2012 in a pediatric ED (emergency department) at a regional Level 1 trauma center, serving 35,000 pediatric patients per year. Subjects were aged 8 years to 17 years and were discharged from the ED (emergency department) with a diagnosis of concussion. Exclusion criteria included recent (past 3 months) diagnosis of head injury, hospital admission, intracranial injury, skull fracture, suspected nonaccidental trauma, or preexisting neurologic condition. Subjects were administered a baseline survey in the ED (emergency department) and were given standardized discharge instructions for concussion by the treating physician. Telephone follow-up surveys were conducted at 2 weeks and 4 weeks after ED (emergency department) visit.

An OSCE test-format (seven stations: Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS (advanced cardiac life support)), Basic Life Support (BLS (basic life support)), Trauma-Management (TM (trauma-management)), Pediatric-Emergencies (PE (pediatric-emergencies)), Acute-Coronary-Syndrome (ACS (acute-coronary-syndrome)), Airway-Management (AM (airway-management)), and Obstetrical-Emergencies (OE (obstetrical-emergencies))) was administered to 207 medical students in their third year of training after they had received didactics in emergency medicine management. Participants were randomly assigned to one of the two simultaneously run tracks: either with SE (n = 110) or with FE (n = 98). Students were asked to rate each OSCE station and to provide their overall OSCE perception by means of a standardized questionnaire. The independent samples t-test was used and effect sizes were calculated (Cohens d).

We reviewed clinical and radiographic information on 259 pediatric type II SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures) that were enrolled in a prospective registry of elbow fractures. The characteristics of the patients who were treated without surgery were compared with those of patients who were treated surgically. Treatment outcomes, as assessed by the final clinical and radiographic alignment, range of motion of the elbow, and complications, were compared between the groups to define clinical and radiographic features that related to success or failure of nonoperative management.

Concussions are commonly diagnosed in pediatric patients presenting to the emergency department (ED (emergency department)). The primary objective of this study was to evaluate compliance with ED (emergency department) discharge instructions for concussion management.
results.reference: The survey shows significant dissatisfaction amongst consultant radiologists with the current service, confirms a low number of paediatric radiologists taking on this work, and suggests the potential to increase numbers of radiology child abuse experts by 27% if given improved training and support. Appropriate service and education strategies should be implemented.

results.question: Artefacts in 24-h pharyngeal and oesophageal pH monitoring: is simplification of pH data analysis feasible?
rewritten: Are artefacts in 24-hour pharyngeal and esophageal pH monitoring significant, and is simplification of pH data analysis feasible in gastroesophageal reflux disease assessment?
results.answer:
The context indicates that artefacts caused by food intake substantially influence raw 24-h pH data, necessitating manual correction. Simplification by leaving out meals aligns well with manually corrected data and reduces false positives, though it carries a small risk (9%-18%) of undetected reflux. However, excluding meals plus a 2-hour postprandial period leads to a high rate of false negatives (21%-50%), suggesting that some simplification is feasible but must be carefully applied.

yes
contexts: Ambulatory 24-h dual-channel pharyngeal and oesophageal pH monitoring is the standard test for measuring gastro-oesophageal and gastropharyngeal reflux. Artefacts caused by the intake of food may result in falsely positive gastropharyngeal reflux, which necessitates a manual review of 24-h pH data. The purpose of the study was to investigate the influence of meals and whether leaving out meals affected the reliability of the test.

Patients referred for otolaryngological complaints, suspected to have been caused by gastro-oesophageal reflux, underwent 24-h dual-channel pH monitoring. The raw unprocessed pH data were corrected by visual inspection of the 24-h tracings (corrected data), by leaving out meals or meals plus a 2-h postprandrial period.

The raw pH data were substantially influenced by artefacts of food intake and pseudoreflux. Data obtained by leaving out meals agreed best with manually corrected data. Many of the falsely positive reflux episodes could be removed, thereby inducing a 9%-18% chance of undetected reflux. When examining the fraction of time supine, manually corrected data and data leaving out meals were fully concordant and detected 79% of patients with gastropharyngeal reflux. However, leaving out meals plus a 2-h postprandrial period resulted in 21%-50% falsely negative tests.

The study group comprised 19 patients (17 female; mean BMI (body mass index) 35.4 kg/m(2)) divided into 2 groups. Group A (n = 10) patients with severe GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) and evidence of residual fundus/neofundus, Hiatal hernia with good results in terms of weight loss. Group B (n = 9) patients with severe GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease), a residual fundus/neofundus, inadequate weight loss or weight regain. Fundectomy was indicated when a residual fundus/neofundus was associated with severe GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) symptoms. The presence of a residual fundus/neofundus was assessed by a barium swallow and/or multislice computed tomography.

Excellent association between acceleration response to VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) and pH>or = 7.20, and between a negative response to VAS (no acceleration or decelerations) and pH<7.20 were found in the first stage of labor, the second stage of labor, and the combination of both stages together (p = 0.0001, OR = 10.6 [3.3-34.0]). It was observed that negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) responses for predicting fetal acidosis (pH<7.20) were comparable between term (>or = 37 weeks) and preterm (<37 weeks,>or = 34 weeks) fetuses. Since the preterm fetuses enrolled in the study were limited in number, it is difficult to draw adequate conclusions. The positive predictive value (PPV (positive predictive value)) of fetal acidosis was 67% in both groups of FHR (fetal heart rate) variable decelerations and late decelerations, but the false negative rate of acceleration VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response for predicting no acidosis was significantly higher in the group of late decelerations (29% vs 8%, p = 0.034). Finally, both a negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response and fetal acidosis (pH<7.20) have equal predictability for neonatal morbidity. The PPV (positive predictive value) of NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) admission by a negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response was two times higher than that of fetal acidosis (PPV (positive predictive value) = 61% vs 29%, p = 0.038).
results.reference: Leaving out the period of intake of meals and beverages from the raw pH data might be the second best test after the time-consuming visual correction with a small chance of undetected gastropharyngeal reflux. For scientific purposes and when in doubt, it remains necessary to review the computer-generated data manually to discover every gastropharyngeal reflux event.

results.question: Can the condition of the cell microenvironment of mediastinal lymph nodes help predict the risk of metastases in non-small cell lung cancer?
rewritten: Can the cellular microenvironment of mediastinal lymph nodes serve as a predictive biomarker for metastatic risk in patients with non-small cell lung cancer?
results.answer:
The study in abstract [1] focuses on analyzing the immune cell microenvironment of regional lymph nodes positive for lung cancer, implying that characteristics of the lymph node microenvironment are being investigated in relation to cancer presence. Abstract [3] further examines immune cell properties in lymph nodes and their relation to cytokeratin-positive cells, which are markers of metastasis. This suggests that the condition of the lymph node microenvironment may provide information relevant to metastasis risk. Therefore, the condition of the cell microenvironment of mediastinal lymph nodes can help predict the risk of metastases in non-small cell lung cancer.

yes
contexts: The aim of this study was to analyze the properties of the immune cell microenvironment of regional lymph nodes (LNs (lymph nodes)) positive for lung cancer.

Mediastinal lymph node dissection is an essential component of lung cancer surgery; however, choosing mediastinal lymph nodes stations to be dissected is subjective. We carried out this research to investigate the need for dissection of station 9 lymph nodes during lung cancer surgery.

Twenty-four patients operated on for stages T1 and T2 of the NSCLC (non small cell lung cancer), were enrolled in the study. Peripheral blood and LN tissue were obtained from different lymph node sites and levels. As a control, LN tissue was taken from patients diagnosed with emphysema or pneumothorax. The cells from randomly chosen LN were tested by multi-color flow cytometry. Separate portions of LN were snap-frozen and examined for the presence of cytokeratin positive cells (CK (cytokeratin positive cells)). Propensity for apoptosis, level of TCR zeta chain expression of T cells and the number and maturation status of dendritic cells were confronted with the presence of CK (cytokeratin positive cells)-positive cells.

A total number of 1397 patients were included in this research. The metastasis rate of station 9 was 3.45%, which was significantly lower than other mediastinal stations. This metastasis rate was significantly correlated with pT stage, the lobe where the tumor was located, metastasis status of intrapulmonary lymph nodes, pTNM stage, and most of the other mediastinal lymph node stations. In males or ground glass opacity (GGO (ground glass opacity)) patients, the metastasis of station 9 nodes was more unlikely to occur, even though there was no statistical significance. The staging results of most patients (99.63%) would not be impaired, even if station 9 nodes were not dissected, and the prognostic analysis showed that the metastasis status of station 9 had no significant influence on survival.

We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) plus radical surgery.
results.reference: The preliminary results of this study suggest that this approach may be helpful as an independent tumor staging factor. It is also worth noting that part of the staging process could also be based on features describing the immune cells in the peripheral blood.

results.question: Are wandering and physically nonaggressive agitation equivalent?
rewritten: Are wandering behavior and physically nonaggressive agitation clinically equivalent in patients with neuropsychiatric disorders?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that wandering and physically nonaggressive agitation (PNA) are related but not identical concepts. Factor analyses showed a one-factor solution for wandering and a two-factor solution for PNA, with significant but not perfect correlations between wandering and PNA factors, suggesting they are overlapping but distinct behaviors.

no
contexts: The authors examined equivalence of wandering and physically nonaggressive agitation (PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation)) as concepts.

Video-tapes for up to twelve 20-minute observations per participant were coded for wandering using an empirically derived taxonomy of ambulation patterns. Separate raters coded the same tapes for six PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation) behaviors on the agitation behavior mapping instrument.

Most participants (73.5%) wandered; all showed PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation) behaviors. Factor analyses yielded an one-factor solution for wandering (explained variance = 43.66%) and a two-factor solution for PNA (explained variance = 53.45%). Overall wandering correlated significantly with PNA (physically nonaggressive agitation) Factor 1 (df =179, r = 0.68, p<0.001) and Factor 2, but at a lower value (df = 179, r = 0.26, p<0.01).

Disorders of consciousness (DOC (disorders of consciousness)) diagnosis relies on the presence or absence of purposeful motor responsiveness, which characterizes the minimally conscious state (MCS (minimally conscious state)) and the unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome)), respectively. Functional neuroimaging studies have raised the question of possible residual conscious awareness also in clinically-defined UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome) patients. The aim of our study was to identify electrophysiological parameters, by means of a transcranial magnetic stimulation approach, which might potentially express the presence of residual networks sustaining fragmentary behavioral patterns, even when no conscious behavior can be observed.

We enrolled 25 severe DOC (disorders of consciousness) patients, following post-anoxic or traumatic brain injury and 20 healthy individuals (HC) as control group. Baseline electrophysiological evaluation evidenced, in comparison to HC, a partial preservation of cortical effective connectivity and excitability in clinically defined MCS (minimally conscious state), whereas these components were absent in clinically defined UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome). Then, we applied an anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (a-tDCS) protocol over the orbitofrontal cortex.
results.reference: Findings depict wandering and PNA as overlapping, but nonequivalent phenomena. Evidence supporting construct validity of wandering was more robust than that for PNA. Results have implications for accuracy in scientific and clinical detection and labeling of wandering and agitation.

results.question: Is size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement an option in modern aortic surgery?
rewritten: Is size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement a viable surgical option in contemporary management of ascending aortic aneurysms?
results.answer:
The retrospective study in abstract [1] describes the use of size-reducing ascending aortoplasty combined with external reinforcement using a non-coated dacron prosthesis to stabilize the aortic wall in patients with ascending aorta aneurysm or ectasia. Abstract [2] also mentions reduction aortoplasty as an optional therapy for enlargement of the ascending aorta, although it notes that clear indications are not yet established. Together, these suggest that size-reducing ascending aortoplasty with external reinforcement is considered an option in aortic surgery.

yes
contexts: In a retrospective study between 1997 and 2005, we investigated 531 patients operated for aneurysm or ectasia of the ascending aorta (diameter: 45-76mm). Of these, in 50 patients, size-reducing ascending aortoplasty was performed. External reinforcement with a non-coated dacron prosthesis was added in order to stabilize the aortic wall.

Enlargement of the ascending aorta is often combined with valvular, coronary, or other cardiac diseases. Reduction aortoplasty can be an optional therapy; however, indications regarding the diameter of aorta, the history of dilatation (poststenosis, bicuspid aortic valve), or the intraoperative management (wall excision, reduction suture, external reinforcement) are not established.

The rate of aortic aneurysm rupture correlates with the aneurysm's diameter, and a higher rate of rupture is observed in patients with larger aneurysms. According to the literature, contradictory results concerning the relationship between atmospheric pressure and aneurysm size have been reported.AIM: In this paper, we assessed the influence of changes in atmospheric pressure on abdominal aneurysm ruptures in relationship to the aneurysm's size.

Between August 2000 and September 2002, 139 patients underwent isolated aortic valve replacement (AVR (aortic valve replacement)) with the Mosaic (n = 67) or Perimount (n = 72) bioprosthesis. Intraoperatively, the internal aortic annulus diameter was measured by insertion of a gauge (Hegar dilator), while prosthesis size was determined by using the original sizers. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed to determine hemodynamic and dimensional data. As the aim of AVR (aortic valve replacement) is to achieve a maximal effective orifice area (EOA (effective orifice area)) within a given aortic annulus, the ratio of EOA (effective orifice area) to patient aortic annulus area was calculated, the latter being based on annulus diameter measured intraoperatively.

The use of a balloon expandable stent valve includes balloon predilatation of the aortic stenosis before valve deployment. The aim of the study was to see whether or not balloon predilatation is necessary in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVI (transcatheter aortic valve implantation)).
results.reference: As demonstrated in this study, size reduction of the ascending aorta using aortoplasty with external reinforcement is a safe procedure with excellent long-term results. It is a therapeutic option in modern aortic surgery in patients with poststenotic dilatation of the aorta without impairment of the sinotubular junction of the aortic valve and root.

results.question: Does depression diagnosis and antidepressant prescribing vary by location?
rewritten: Does the prevalence of major depressive disorder diagnosis and patterns of antidepressant medication prescribing vary by geographic location or region?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts do not contain any information about geographic variation or differences by location in depression diagnosis or antidepressant prescribing. The studies focus on risk factors, symptom assessment tools, and treatment changes but do not address location-based differences.

no
contexts: Women's vulnerability for a first lifetime-onset of major depressive disorder (MDD (major depressive disorder)) during midlife is substantial. It is unclear whether risk factors differ for first lifetime-onset and recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder). Identifying these risk factors can provide more focused depression screening and earlier intervention. This study aims to evaluate whether lifetime psychiatric and health histories, personality traits, menopausal status and factors that vary over time, e.g. symptoms, are independent risk factors for first-onset or recurrent MDD (major depressive disorder) across 13 annual follow-ups.

The three disorder groups had rates of adult MD (major depression) during the period 18-35 years that were significantly (p<.05) higher than that of the group with no disorder. Furthermore, those in the comorbid MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder) group had significantly (p<.05) higher rates of adult MD (major depression) than those in the AUD (alcohol use disorder)-only group, and marginally (p<.10) higher rates of adult MD (major depression) than those in the MD (major depression)-only group. After adjustment for confounding, the difference in rates of adult MD (major depression) between the MD (major depression)-only group and the MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder) group were no longer statistically significant. The factors that explained the associations were gender, childhood behavior problems, and exposure to physical and sexual abuse.

Women without lifetime MDD (major depressive disorder) at baseline had a lower risk of developing MDD (major depressive disorder) during midlife than those with a prior MDD (major depressive disorder) history (28% v. 59%) and their risk profiles differed. Health conditions prior to baseline and during follow-ups perception of functioning (ps<0.05) and vasomotor symptoms (VMS (vasomotor symptoms)) (p = 0.08) were risk factors for first lifetime-onset MDD (major depressive disorder). Being peri- and post-menopausal, psychological symptoms and a prior anxiety disorder were predominant risk factors for MDD (major depressive disorder) recurrence.

By the conclusion of the study, all remaining 17 practices had adopted PHQ-9 as a routine part of depression care in their practice. On the basis of responses from 17 psychiatrists from those practices, PHQ-9 scores influenced clinical decision making for 93% of 6,096 patient contacts. With the additional information gained from the PHQ-9 score, one or more treatment changes occurred during 40% of these clinical contacts. Changing the dosage of antidepressant medication and adding another medication were the most common treatment changes recorded by psychiatrists, followed by starting or increasing psychotherapy and by switching or initiating antidepressants. In 3% of the patient contacts, using the PHQ-9 led to additional suicide risk assessment.

Four hundred and forty-three women, aged 42-52 years, enrolled in the Study of Women's Health Across the Nation in Pittsburgh and participated in the Mental Health Study. Psychiatric interviews obtained information on lifetime psychiatric disorders at baseline and on occurrences of MDD (major depressive disorder) episodes annually. Psychosocial and health-related data were collected annually. Cox multivariable analyses were conducted separately for women with and without a MDD (major depressive disorder) history at baseline.
results.reference: New depression diagnosis and antidepressant use was shown to be less likely in areas of higher own-ethnic density for some, but not all, ethnic groups.

results.question: Can routinely collected ambulance data about assaults contribute to reduction in community violence?
rewritten: Can routinely collected prehospital emergency medical services data on assault-related injuries contribute to the reduction of community violence through epidemiological surveillance and targeted intervention strategies?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that ambulance data and police data on assaults show partial overlap in hotspots, with about half of police hotspots not overlapping with ambulance hotspots, suggesting ambulance data captures additional assault locations unknown to police. This implies that routinely collected ambulance data could provide valuable information to better understand and potentially reduce community violence through improved hotspot identification and interagency data-sharing.

yes
contexts: The 'law of spatiotemporal concentrations of events' introduced major preventative shifts in policing communities. 'Hotspots' are at the forefront of these developments yet somewhat understudied in emergency medicine. Furthermore, little is known about interagency 'data-crossover', despite some developments through the Cardiff Model. Can police-ED (emergency department) interagency data-sharing be used to reduce community-violence using a hotspots methodology?

Spatiotemporal location of calls for services to the police and the ambulance service are equally highly concentrated in a small number of geographical areas, primarily within intra-agency hotspots (33% and 53%, respectively) but across agencies' hotspots as well (25% and 15%, respectively). Datasets are statistically correlated with one another at the 0.57 and 0.34 levels, with 50% overlap when adjusted for the number of hotspots. At least one in every two police hotspots does not have an ambulance hotspot overlapping with it, suggesting half of assault spatiotemporal concentrations are unknown to the police. Data further suggest that more severely injured patients, as estimated by transfer to hospital, tend to be injured in the places with the highest number of police-recorded crimes.

In the prehospital setting, Emergency Medical Services (EMS (emergency medical services)) professionals rely on providing positive pressure ventilation with a bag-valve-mask (BVM (bag-valve-mask)). Multiple emergency medicine and critical care studies have shown that lung-protective ventilation protocols reduce morbidity and mortality. Our primary objective was to determine if a group of EMS (emergency medical services) professionals could provide ventilations with a smaller BVM (bag-valve-mask) that would be sufficient to ventilate patients. Secondary objectives included 1) if the pediatric bag provided volumes similar to lung-protective ventilation in the hospital setting and 2) compare volumes provided to the patient depending on the type of airway (mask, King tube, and intubation).

12-month (2012) descriptive study and analysis of spatiotemporal clusters of police and emergency calls for service using hotspots methodology and assessing the degree of incident overlap. 3775 violent crime incidents and 775 assault incidents analysed using spatiotemporal clustering with k-means++ algorithm and Spearman's rho.

The objective of the current study is to determine to what extent the reduction of Chile's traffic fatalities and injuries during 2000-2012 was related to the police traffic enforcement increment registered after the introduction of its 2005 traffic law reform.
results.reference: A hotspots approach to sharing data circumvents the problem of disclosing person-identifiable data between different agencies. Practically, at least half of ambulance hotspots are unknown to the police; if causal, it suggests that data sharing leads to both reduced community violence by way of prevention (such as through anticipatory patrols or problem-oriented policing), particularly of more severe assaults, and improved efficiency of resource deployment.

results.question: Volume change of uterine myomas during pregnancy: do myomas really grow?
rewritten: Do uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) increase in volume during pregnancy?
results.answer:
The data show that during pregnancy, some uterine myomas decrease in size while others increase. Specifically, between the first and second periods, 44.9% of myomas enlarged with a mean increase of 69%, and between the second and third periods, 25% enlarged with a mean increase of 102%. This indicates that myomas do grow during pregnancy, although not all do.

yes
contexts: To estimate changes in uterine myoma volume during pregnancy.

We analyzed the change in volume of uterine myomas between the first half of pregnancy (up until 19 weeks), third quarter (20-30 weeks), and last quarter (31 weeks to term). The volume of largest uterine myoma was calculated using the formula Volume (mm3)=Pi/6x(length mm)x(width mm)x(height mm).
One hundred-seven patients diagnosed with uterine myomas during pregnancy and who had two or more obstetrical ultrasounds in different periods of pregnancy.

The mean age of the population was 31+/-6 years. Between the first and the second study periods, the percentage of uterine myomas that decreased in size was 55.1% (95% CI (confidence interval): 43-66), with a mean decrease in volume of 35%+/-4%; while the percentage of uterine myomas that enlarged was 44.9% (95% CI (confidence interval): 34-56), with a mean increase in volume of 69%+/-11%. Between the second and the third study periods, 75% (95% CI (confidence interval): 56-87) became smaller, with a mean decrease in volume of 30%+/-3%; while 25% (95% CI (confidence interval): 13-43) enlarged, with a mean increase in volume of 102%+/-62%.

Endometrial CD56+ uNK (uterine natural killer) cells were significantly increased in biopsies obtained during bleeding episodes (P<0.001), compared with HT (hormone therapy) users with no bleeding. The highest level of IL (interleukin)-15 expression was also seen in biopsies taken during bleeding. No clear relationship between killer Ig like receptor genotype and bleeding on HT (hormone therapy) was observed.
results.reference: Contrary to common belief, we found that uterine myomas commonly decrease in volume over the course of pregnancy.

results.question: Is laparoscopic adrenalectomy safe and effective for adrenal masses larger than 7 cm?
rewritten: Is laparoscopic adrenalectomy a safe and effective surgical approach for the treatment of adrenal tumors larger than 7 centimeters in diameter?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that laparoscopic adrenalectomy (LA) is the gold standard for small adrenal masses, but the role for large masses (>7 cm) is not well defined. One study retrospectively evaluated outcomes of LA for lesions larger than 7 cm, implying that the procedure is being performed and studied in this context. Although detailed safety and efficacy results are not provided here, the fact that 18 consecutive cases were performed suggests it is considered feasible and potentially safe and effective.

yes
contexts: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy (LA (laparoscopic adrenalectomy)) has become the gold standard treatment for small (less than 6 cm) adrenal masses. However, the role of LA (laparoscopic adrenalectomy) for large-volume (more than 6 cm) masses has not been well defined. Our aim was to evaluate, retrospectively, the outcome of LA (laparoscopic adrenalectomy) for adrenal lesions larger than 7 cm.
18 consecutive laparoscopic adrenalectomies were performed from 1996 to 2005 on patients with adrenal lesions larger than 7 cm.

Treatment of neonatal testicular torsion has two objectives: salvage of the involved testicle (which is rarely achieved) and preservation of the contralateral gonad. The second goal universally involves contralateral testicular scrotal fixation to prevent the future occurrence of contralateral torsion. However, there is controversy with regards to management of a synchronous contralateral hydrocele. It has been our policy not to address the contralateral hydrocele through an inguinal incision to minimize potential injury to the spermatic cord. Our objective in this study was to determine whether the decision to manage a contralateral hydrocele in cases of neonatal testicular torsion solely through a scrotal approach is safe and effective.

Up to 30 % of patients who have undergone laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy require revision surgery for inadequate weight loss, weight regain, and/or the development of severe upper gastrointestinal symptoms. The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of laparoscopic fundectomy (LF (laparoscopic fundectomy)) in cases of a residual fundus/neofundus development regarding GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) symptoms.

Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG (laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy)) is currently being performed with increasing frequency worldwide. It offers an excellent weight loss and resolution of comorbidities in the short term with a very low incidence of complications. However, the ever present risk of a staple line leak is still a major concern.
results.reference: LA for adrenal masses larger than 7 cm is a safe and feasible technique, offering successful outcome in terms of intraoperative and postoperative morbidity, hospital stay and cosmesis for patients; it seems to replicate open surgical oncological principles demonstrating similar outcomes as survival rate and recurrence rate, when adrenal cortical carcinoma were treated. The main contraindication for this approach is the evidence, radiologically and intraoperatively, of local infiltration of periadrenal tissue.

results.question: Upstream solutions: does the supplemental security income program reduce disability in the elderly?
rewritten: Does enrollment in the Supplemental Security Income program reduce the incidence or severity of disability among elderly adults?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that increases in Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits are associated with reductions in mobility limitations among elderly individuals, suggesting a decrease in disability rates. The findings were consistent across various sensitivity analyses and subgroups, supporting the idea that SSI reduces disability in the elderly.

yes
contexts: Higher benefits are linked to lower disability rates. Among all single elderly individuals, 30 percent have mobility limitations, and an increase of $100 per month in the maximum SSI (supplemental security income) benefit caused the rate of mobility limitations to fall by 0.46 percentage points. The findings were robust to sensitivity analyses. First, analyses limited to those most likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced larger effects, but analyses limited to those least likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced no measurable effect. Second, varying the disability measure did not meaningfully alter the findings. Third, excluding the institutionalized, immigrants, individuals living in states with exceptionally large benefit changes, and individuals living in states with no SSI (supplemental security income) supplements did not change the substantive conclusions. Fourth, Medicaid did not confound the effects. Finally, these results were robust for married individuals.

The robust relationship between socioeconomic factors and health suggests that social and economic policies might substantially affect health, while other evidence suggests that medical care, the main focus of current health policy, may not be the primary determinant of population health. Income support policies are one promising avenue to improve population health. This study examines whether the federal cash transfer program to poor elderly, the Supplemental Security Income (SSI (supplemental security income)) program, affects old-age disability.

This study uses the 1990 and 2000 censuses, employing state and year fixed-effect models, to test whether within-state changes in maximum SSI (supplemental security income) benefits over time lead to changes in disability among people aged sixty-five and older.

An estimated 25.8 million adults aged 40-65 (26.7%) said they would be interested in paying for a public insurance program to cover PAS (personal assistance services) benefits. However, interest in PAS (personal assistance services) insurance varied by age, race, ethnicity, region, income, disability status, and family experience with ADL assistance. Only 1.6 million adults aged 40-65 (1.8%) said they would be willing to pay $100 per month or more for coverage.

To estimate the number of middle-aged adults interested in purchasing PAS (personal assistance services) insurance, the sociodemographic, socioeconomic and disability attributes of this population, and the maximum monthly premium they would be willing to pay for such coverage.
results.reference: Income support policy may be a significant new lever for improving population health, especially that of lower-income persons. Even though the findings are robust, further analyses are needed to confirm their reliability. Future research should examine a variety of different income support policies, as well as whether a broader range of social and economic policies affect health.

results.question: Profiling quality of care: Is there a role for peer review?
rewritten: Is there a role for peer review in profiling and improving the quality of healthcare delivery?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that peer review, specifically physician review, has variable reliability depending on the condition being assessed. For chronic diseases with a well-developed evidence base like diabetes and hypertension, peer review shows higher reliability in profiling quality of care, suggesting a meaningful role. However, for conditions like COPD and acute illnesses, the reliability is low, indicating limitations. Overall, the evidence supports a role for peer review in profiling quality of care, particularly for certain conditions.

yes
contexts: For COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and a collection of acute conditions the reliability of a single physician review was quite low (intra-class correlation = 0.16-0.26) but comparable to most previously published estimates for the use of this method in inpatient settings. However, for diabetes and hypertension the reliability is significantly higher at 0.46. The higher reliability is a result of the reviewers collectively being able to distinguish more differences in the quality of care between patients (p<0.007) and not due to less random noise or individual reviewer bias in the measurement. For these conditions the level of true quality (i.e. the rating of quality of care that would result from the full population of physician reviewers reviewing a record) varied from poor to good across patients.

We sought to develop a more reliable structured implicit chart review instrument for use in assessing the quality of care for chronic disease and to examine if ratings are more reliable for conditions in which the evidence base for practice is more developed.

We conducted a reliability study in a cohort with patient records including both outpatient and inpatient care as the objects of measurement. We developed a structured implicit review instrument to assess the quality of care over one year of treatment. 12 reviewers conducted a total of 496 reviews of 70 patient records selected from 26 VA clinical sites in two regions of the country. Each patient had between one and four conditions specified as having a highly developed evidence base (diabetes and hypertension) or a less developed evidence base (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or a collection of acute conditions). Multilevel analysis that accounts for the nested and cross-classified structure of the data was used to estimate the signal and noise components of the measurement of quality and the reliability of implicit review.

Health care delivery has undertaken a major shift from inpatient management to ambulatory surgical care with increasing emphasis on quality assurance (QA (quality assurance)) processes. Educational opportunities for medical undergraduate programmes are being sought in the day surgery environment. Our study was undertaken to explore ways in which senior medical students can actively contribute to the QA (quality assurance) processes as part of an undergraduate day surgery educational programme.

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.
results.reference: For conditions with a well-developed quality of care evidence base, such as hypertension and diabetes, a single structured implicit review to assess the quality of care over a period of time is moderately reliable. This method could be a reasonable complement or alternative to explicit indicator approaches for assessing and comparing quality of care. Structured implicit review, like explicit quality measures, must be used more cautiously for illnesses for which the evidence base is less well developed, such as COPD and acute, short-course illnesses.

results.question: Eyelid-parotid metastasis: do we screen for coexisting masses?
rewritten: Should patients with eyelid metastasis from parotid gland carcinoma be screened for coexisting metastatic masses?
results.answer:
The case reports and objective summaries indicate that primary tumors in the eyelid can metastasize to the parotid gland and vice versa, suggesting a clinical relationship between these sites. Given this metastatic potential, screening for coexisting masses in both the eyelid and parotid gland would be clinically relevant to identify and differentiate primary tumors from metastases. Therefore, the evidence supports screening for coexisting masses in cases of eyelid-parotid metastasis.

yes
contexts: Two patients with malignant parotid tumours underwent radical parotidectomy and presented subsequently with eyelid lesions. Biopsy showed that both eyelid lesions were histologically similar to the primary parotid tumour. A third patient was noted to have ipsilateral upper eyelid and parotid gland tumours. Histology and immunocytochemistry were used to differentiate the primary tumour and the metastasis.
To report three cases illustrating that it is not unusual for a primary eyelid tumour to metastasise to the parotid gland and vice versa.

In 136 patients, a primary parotid gland tumor was confirmed by histology. Among the observers, a high correlation was calculated (0.98). ADC values of pleomorphic adenomas were significantly higher than those of all other entities, except for myoepithelial adenomas (P = .054). ADC values of Warthin tumors were different from those of myoepithelial adenomas, lipomas, and salivary duct carcinomas (P<.001, 0.013, and .037, respectively). Mucoepidermoid carcinomas, acinic cell carcinomas, and basal cell adenocarcinomas were not differentiable from Warthin tumors (P = .094, .396, and .604, respectively).
Both tumors were in the advanced stages. Metastatic carcinoma of the prostate was discarded due to the form of presentation.

We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) plus radical surgery.
results.reference: These cases illustrate that tumours involving eyelids and parotid glands can present simultaneously or sequentially, and either of these structures could be the focus of primary or metastatic tumour. The important message for oculoplastic and parotid surgeons is to routinely assess both the periocular and parotid area when patients present with a mass in either structure.

results.question: Will CT ordering practices change if we educate residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure?
rewritten: Does educating medical residents about the potential risks of ionizing radiation exposure influence their computed tomography (CT) scan ordering practices?
results.answer:
The study showed that after a radiologist's lecture on radiation exposure, 90% of residents did not change the number of CT scans they ordered, and only 10% decreased their ordering. However, some residents increased the use of alternative imaging modalities like MRI and ultrasound, and a minority changed the types of CT scans ordered. This suggests that while the overall CT ordering volume largely remained the same, some changes in ordering behavior and imaging choices did occur following education.

yes
contexts: The aim of this study was to determine if educating residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure from computed tomographic (CT (computed tomographic)) imaging alters ordering patterns. This study also explored whether referring physicians are interested in radiation education and was an initial effort to address their CT (computed tomographic) ordering behavior.

Two to four months after a radiologist's lecture on the potential effects of radiation exposure related to CT (computed tomographic) scans, urology and orthopedic residents were surveyed regarding the number and types of CT (computed tomographic) scans they ordered, the use of alternative imaging modalities, and whether they used the lecture information to educate patients.

Twenty-one resident lecture attendants completed the survey. The number of CT (computed tomographic) scans ordered after the lecture stayed constant for 90% (19 of 21) and decreased for 10% (two of 21). The types of CT (computed tomographic) scans ordered changed after the lecture for 14% (three of 21). Thirty-three percent (seven of 21) reported increases in alternative imaging after the lecture, including 24% (five of 21) reporting increases in magnetic resonance imaging and 19% (four of 21) reporting increases in ultrasound. Patients directed questions about radiation exposure to 57% (12 of 21); 38% (eight of 21) used the lecture information to educate patients. Referring physicians were interested in the topic, and afterward, other physician groups requested radiation education lectures.
Evaluate the capability of different Computed Tomography scanners to determine urinary stone compositions based on CT attenuation values and to evaluate potential differences between each model.

The surgical management of 36 of 46 patients (78 percent) was unchanged as a result of position emission tomography, even though position emission tomography upstaged disease in 3 of 36 cases (8 percent) and downstaged disease in 5 of 36 cases (14 percent). In 8 of 46 cases (17 percent), management was altered because of the position emission tomography scan findings, including 6 cases (13 percent) in which surgery was cancelled and 2 other cases (4 percent) in which the radiotherapy field was changed. Where available, follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced management change in each case. Two patients had a change in therapy independent of the position emission tomography scan due to clinical circumstances. Overall tumor stage was changed following position emission tomography in 18 of 46 patients (39 percent).
results.reference: Most clinicians did not change their CT scan ordering after receiving education about radiation from a radiologist. Radiation education allowed clinicians to discuss CT benefits and risks with their patients and to choose appropriate CT protocols. Referring physician groups are interested in this topic, and radiologists should be encouraged to give radiation lectures to them.

results.question: Does context matter for the relationship between deprivation and all-cause mortality?
rewritten: Does the socioeconomic and environmental context influence the association between socioeconomic deprivation and all-cause mortality rates?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that while there are spatial patterns of deprivation and mortality (with hotspots and coldspots), the relationship between socio-economic deprivation and all-cause mortality does not vary significantly between regions in Scotland. This suggests that the context, in terms of geographic region within Scotland, does not alter the deprivation-mortality relationship. Therefore, context in this spatial sense does not matter for the relationship between deprivation and all-cause mortality.

no
contexts: The initial exploratory spatial data analysis reveals concentrations of high standardized mortality ratios (SMR (standardized mortality ratios)) and deprivation (hotspots) in the West of Scotland and concentrations of low values (coldspots) for both variables in the rest of the country. The main spatial regression result is that deprivation is the only variable that is highly significantly correlated with all-cause mortality in all models. However, in contrast to the expected spatial heterogeneity in the deprivation-mortality relationship, this relation does not vary between regions in any of the models. This result is robust to a number of specifications, including weighting for population size, controlling for spatial autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity, assuming a non-linear relationship between mortality and socio-economic deprivation, separating the dependent variable into male and female SMRs, and distinguishing between West, North and Southeast regions. The rejection of the hypothesis of spatial heterogeneity in the relationship between socio-economic deprivation and mortality complements prior research on the stability of the deprivation-mortality relationship over time.

A growing body of research emphasizes the importance of contextual factors on health outcomes. Using postcode sector data for Scotland (UK), this study tests the hypothesis of spatial heterogeneity in the relationship between area-level deprivation and mortality to determine if contextual differences in the West vs. the rest of Scotland influence this relationship. Research into health inequalities frequently fails to recognise spatial heterogeneity in the deprivation-health relationship, assuming that global relationships apply uniformly across geographical areas. In this study, exploratory spatial data analysis methods are used to assess local patterns in deprivation and mortality. Spatial regression models are then implemented to examine the relationship between deprivation and mortality more formally.

First, to establish whether a deprivation gradient in all-cause mortality exists for all ethnic groups within New Zealand; second, if such gradients do exist, whether their absolute slopes are the same; and third, if such gradients exist, what impact the unequal deprivation distributions of the different ethnic groups have on the observed ethnic inequalities in life expectancy at birth.

All four ethnic groups exhibit deprivation gradients in all-cause mortality (life expectancy). Maori show the steepest gradients, with slopes approximately 25% steeper than those of Europeans for both males and females. By contrast, gradients among Asian and Pacific peoples are shallower than those of their European counterparts.
In this study we investigated whether the association between measures of fetal growth restriction and intellectual performance was mediated by socioeconomic or familial factors.
results.reference: The homogeneity we found in the deprivation-mortality relationship across the regions of Scotland and the absence of a contextualized effect of region highlights the importance of taking a broader strategic policy that can combat the toxic impacts of socio-economic deprivation on health. Focusing on a few specific places (e.g. 15% of the poorest areas) to concentrate resources might be a good start but the impact of socio-economic deprivation on mortality is not restricted to a few places. A comprehensive strategy that can be sustained over time might be needed to interrupt the linkages between poverty and mortality.

results.question: Does stress increase imitation of drinking behavior?
rewritten: Does psychological stress increase the imitation of alcohol consumption behavior in humans?
results.answer:
The provided studies show that participants consumed more alcohol when confederates drank alcohol regardless of stress condition, and no difference in alcohol consumption was found between stress and no-stress groups. Additionally, no moderating effect of stress on the tendency to imitate drinking behavior was observed.

no
contexts: That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.

With a 2 (confederate's drinking condition: alcohol vs. soda) × 2 (participant's stress condition: stress vs. no stress) experimental design, we tested whether the tendency to imitate other people's drinking was related to participants' induced stress levels. The young male adults (N = 106) were randomly assigned to each of the conditions. In each session, directly after the stress or no-stress period, confederates and participants entered a bar laboratory where we observed their drinking behavior. Prior to entering the session, confederates were instructed to drink alcohol or soda.

Rats given 5 min of alcohol-associated cues responded significantly more on the active lever (26% increase) and consumed more alcohol as verified by increased blood alcohol levels (8.9 mM versus control 7.5 mM). Ten or 15 min of cues did not change alcohol consumption and 5 min in a novel environment decreased response by 66%. After a 10-day break in training, 5 min of alcohol-associated cues still increased alcohol consumption (29% increase) and the cue effect could be dose-dependently blocked by naltrexone (143% decrease at 0.03 mg/kg).

Participants in both stress and no-stress conditions consumed substantially more alcohol when confederates drank alcohol than when they drank soda. There was no difference in alcohol consumed between stress and no-stress conditions. No moderating effect of stress on the tendency to drink along with peers was found.

Alcohol-associated cues elicit craving in human addicts but little is known about craving mechanisms. Current animal models focus on relapse and this may confound the effect of environmental cues. OBJECTIVES. To develop a model to study the effects of environmental cues on alcohol consumption in animals not experiencing withdrawal or relapse.
results.reference: Generally, it appears that among young male adults, imitation of alcohol consumption is a robust phenomenon not dependent on individual stress levels.

results.question: School food policy at Dutch primary schools: room for improvement?
rewritten: Is there potential for improvement in the nutritional quality and implementation of school food policies at primary schools in the Netherlands?
results.answer:
The study indicates that while most Dutch primary schools have a written food policy and principals believe sufficient attention is paid to nutrition, the rules are often not clearly defined. Additionally, there is variation in parental opinions on enforcement, and some parents feel the school should enforce the policy more strongly, suggesting there is room for improvement in both policy clarity and implementation.

yes
contexts: Schools can play an important role in the prevention of obesity, e.g. by providing an environment that stimulates healthy eating habits and by developing a food policy to provide such an environment. The effectiveness of a school food policy is affected by the content of the policy, its implementation and its support by parents, teachers and principals. The aim of this study is to detect opportunities to improve the school food policy and/or implementation at Dutch primary schools. Therefore, this study explores the school food policy and investigates schools' (teachers and principals) and parents' opinion on the school food policy.

Data on the schools' perspective of the food policy was collected from principals and teachers by means of semi-structured interviews. In total 74 principals and 72 teachers from 83 Dutch primary schools were interviewed. Data on parental perceptions about the school food policy were based on a cross-sectional survey among 1,429 parents from the same schools.

Most principals (87.1%) reported that their school had a written food policy; however in most cases the rules were not clearly defined. Most of the principals (87.8%) believed that their school paid sufficient attention to nutrition and health. Teachers and principals felt that parents were primarily responsible to encourage healthy eating habits among children, while 49.8% of the parents believed that it is also a responsibility of the school to foster healthy eating habits among children. Most parents reported that they appreciated the school food policy and comply with the food rules. Parents' opinion on the enforcement of the school food policy varied: 28.1% believed that the school should enforce the policy more strongly, 32.1% was satisfied, and 39.8% had no opinion on this topic.
Four primary care practices affiliated with the University of Nijmegen in the Netherlands.

A multi-site action research was conducted over a 16-month period in 2007-2009 with three Victorian community palliative care services. Using mixed method data collection strategies to assess feasibility, we conducted a baseline audit of staff and clients; analysed relevant documents (client records, policies, procedures and quality improvement strategies) pre-implementation and post-implementation and conducted key informant interviews (n = 9).
results.reference: Dutch primary schools could play a more important role in fostering healthy eating habits among children. The school food policy could be improved by clearly formulating food rules, simplifying supervision of the food rules, and defining how to enforce the food rules. In addition, the school food policy will only influence children's dietary behaviour if both the school and the parents support the policy.

results.question: Is the atopy patch test with house dust mites specific for atopic dermatitis?
rewritten: Is the atopy patch test using house dust mite allergens specific for diagnosing atopic dermatitis?
results.answer:
The atopy patch test (APT) with house dust mites shows a higher positivity rate in atopic dermatitis (AD) patients compared to non-AD subjects, indicating some level of specificity. However, positive responses were also observed in atopic subjects without eczema and in nonatopic individuals, suggesting that the test is not exclusively specific for AD. Therefore, while the APT is more specific for AD, it is not entirely specific.

no
contexts: The aim of this study was to evaluate the response to the APT (atopy patch test) with house dust mites (HDM (house dust mites)) in subjects nonaffected by AD (atopic dermatitis) and to compare the outcomes observed in these cases with those pointed out in AD (atopic dermatitis) patients, evaluating also the differences between two allergen extracts manufactured at different purifications and concentrations.

The atopy patch test (APT (atopy patch test)), namely the patch test with aeroallergens, is regarded as specific for patients with atopic dermatitis (AD (atopic dermatitis)), but small numbers of positive APT (atopy patch test) were reported in the past also in atopic subjects without dermatitis and in healthy persons.

Forty-seven atopic subjects without eczema (AWE (atopic subjects without eczema)), 33 nonatopic (NA (nonatopic)) subjects and 77 adult AD (atopic dermatitis) patients were patch tested with an extract of purified bodies of HDM (house dust mites) at 20% and with another extract of whole bodies of HDM (house dust mites) at 30%, the latter corresponding to 300 microg/g of Der p 1. The reproducibility of APT (atopy patch test) was also tested in 8 AD (atopic dermatitis) patients, in 37 AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) subjects and in 19 NA (nonatopic) subjects.

Positive responses with extract at 20% were observed in 29 (37.7%) AD (atopic dermatitis), in 5 (10.6%) AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) and in 4 (12.1%) NA (nonatopic) subjects. The APT (atopy patch test) with HDM (house dust mites) at 30% was positive in 32 (41.6%) AD (atopic dermatitis), 9 (19.1%) AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) and 4 (12.1%) NA (nonatopic) persons. The rates of positivity and the intensity scores of responses were significantly different between AD (atopic dermatitis) and non-AD (atopic dermatitis) subjects (p<0.01). The reproducibility of the APT (atopy patch test) in the three groups was satisfactory.

Health care providers, which include house staff, nurses, and respiratory care practitioners who provide care to patients with asthma in the primary general medicine clinic or the pulmonary medicine clinic of a university-county hospital in which patients were referred, were surveyed and assigned a performance score regarding the knowledge base of the appropriate use of metered-dose inhalers. Patients who attended the primary care general medicine and pulmonary subspecialty clinic were also assessed as to their proficiency in the use of metered-dose inhalers.
results.reference: These observations lead to conclude that the APT with HDM is positive also in non-AD subjects but it is probably more specific for AD.

results.question: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans: is it a growth disturbance of the secondary physis of the epiphysis?
rewritten: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans: is it a growth disturbance of the secondary ossification center of the epiphyseal cartilage?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) is hypothesized to result from an insult affecting endochondral ossification from the secondary physis of the epiphysis. MRI findings show significant secondary physeal disruption in juvenile OCD cases compared to controls, supporting the idea that juvenile OCD is related to a growth disturbance of the secondary physis.

yes
contexts: The primary physis is responsible for longitudinal bone growth. Similarly, epiphysial growth relies on endochondral ossification from the circumferential secondary physeal [corrected]. injury can result in disruption of normal ossification. The cause of juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (OCD (osteochondritis dissecans)) remains elusive. We hypothesized that juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) results from an insult affecting endochondral ossification from the secondary physis. The purpose of our study was to evaluate the MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) appearance of the distal femoral epiphysis-particularly the secondary physis-of children with juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) and to compare these findings with the MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) findings of unaffected children.

Knee MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) examinations of 30 children (age range, 8 years 8 months to 13 years 4 months) with OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) and 30 matched control patients were evaluated for skeletal maturity; location of the OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) lesion, if present; secondary physeal [corrected] continuity; overlying chondroepiphysial integrity, contour, and width; signal intensity of subchondral bone; and secondary physeal [corrected]conspicuity. Variables were compared using chi-square tests.

All children were skeletally immature. Condylar lesions were medial in 24 knees and lateral in six knees. All were in the middle one third, posterior one third, or middle and posterior thirds in the sagittal plane. The majority of lesions spanned the intercondylar and middle one third of the femoral condyle in the coronal plane (73%). There was a significant difference between secondary physeal [corrected] disruption in juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) condyles compared with unaffected condyles (p<0.001) and control condyles (p<0.001). Compared with unaffected and control condyles, the OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) group showed chondroepiphysial widening (p<0.001) and subchondral bone edema (p<0.001) on MRI (magnetic resonance imaging). Neither chondroepiphysial integrity nor chondroepiphysial contour was significantly different between groups (p = 0.21, p = 0.31, respectively).

The aetiology of osteochondritis dissecans is still unclear. The aim of this prospective pilot study was to analyse whether vitamin D insufficiency, or deficiency, might be a contributing etiological factor in the development of an OCD lesion.

To determine the relationship between injury severity surrogates and other patient factors with the development and severity of heterotopic ossification (HO (heterotopic ossification)) following open reduction internal fixation of acetabular fractures treated with a posterior approach.
results.reference: MRI of children with OCD consistently showed secondary physis disruption, overlying chondroepiphysial widening, and subchondral bone edema. We suggest that disruption of normal endochondral ossification may be associated with juvenile OCD.

results.question: Do preoperative statins reduce atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting?
rewritten: Do preoperative statin therapy reduce the incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation following coronary artery bypass grafting surgery?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that preoperative statin therapy is associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting (16% vs. 33%, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis further supports statins as an independent predictor reducing the risk of postoperative AF (OR 0.327, p = 0.05). Therefore, the evidence supports that preoperative statins reduce atrial fibrillation after CABG.

yes
contexts: Recent studies have demonstrated that statins have pleiotropic effects, including anti-inflammatory effects and atrial fibrillation (AF (atrial fibrillation)) preventive effects. The objective of this study was to assess the efficacy of preoperative statin therapy in preventing AF (atrial fibrillation) after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).

The overall incidence of postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was 26%. Postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was significantly lower in the Statin group compared with the Non-statin group (16% versus 33%, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that independent predictors of AF (atrial fibrillation) development after CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) were preoperative statin therapy (odds ratio [OR]0.327, 95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)] 0.107 to 0.998, p = 0.05) and age (OR 1.058, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.004 to 1.116, p = 0.035).

221 patients underwent CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) in our hospital from 2004 to 2007. 14 patients with preoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) and 4 patients with concomitant valve surgery were excluded from this study. Patients were divided into two groups to examine the influence of statins: those with preoperative statin therapy (Statin group, n = 77) and those without it (Non-statin group, n = 126). In addition, patients were divided into two groups to determine the independent predictors for postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation): those with postoperative AF (AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 54) and those without it (Non-AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 149). Patient data were collected and analyzed retrospectively.

Atrial fibrillation, which occurs in 12% of all major foregut surgeries, can prolong hospital stay and increase morbidity. Minimally invasive techniques in foregut surgery have been suggested to cause less tissue trauma. We examined the factors associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation after foregut surgery at our institution.

Extracranial internal carotid artery stenosis is a risk factor for perioperative stroke in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery (CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery)). Although selective and non-selective methods of preoperative carotid screening have been advocated, it remains unclear if this screening is clinically relevant.AIM: To test whether selective carotid screening is as effective as non-selective screening in detecting significant carotid disease.
results.reference: Our study indicated that preoperative statin therapy seems to reduce AF development after CABG.

results.question: Is there a uniform basal endometrial gene expression profile during the implantation window in women who became pregnant in a subsequent ICSI cycle?
rewritten: Is there a consistent basal endometrial gene expression profile during the implantation window in women who achieved pregnancy following a subsequent intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) cycle?
results.answer:
The study analyzed 43 genes in the endometrium during the window of implantation in women who subsequently became pregnant after ICSI. Only 6 genes showed statistically uniform expression among these women, while the majority exhibited considerable differences in expression levels. This indicates that there is not a uniform basal gene expression profile during the implantation window in these women.

contexts: To understand which genes are really involved in the implantation process, we planned to study the gene basal expression profile during the window of implantation (WOI (window of implantation)) of patients who became pregnant in a subsequent ICSI cycle.

results.question: Clinician assessment for acute chest syndrome in febrile patients with sickle cell disease: is it accurate enough?
rewritten: Is clinician assessment sufficiently accurate for diagnosing acute chest syndrome in febrile patients with sickle cell disease?
results.answer:

Physician sensitivity for predicting ACS was only 39%, and 61% of ACS cases were not clinically suspected before chest radiography. results.question: Improvements in survival of gynaecological cancer in the Anglia region of England: are these an effect of centralisation of care and use of multidisciplinary management?

The context indicates that in 1999, the Department of Health in England introduced guidance for multidisciplinary team management and surgical concentration in specialist hospitals for gynaecological cancer, which was rapidly adopted in the East of England.
