All three adducts were elevated in uremic plasma. Plasma CML (carboxymethyllysine) levels were mainly (>95%) albumin bound. Their levels were not correlated with fructoselysine levels and were similar in diabetic and non-diabetic patients on hemodialysis, indicating that their increase was not driven by glucose. Pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine were also increased in plasma to the same extent in diabetic and non-diabetic hemodialysis patients. Statistical analysis indicated that plasma levels of CML (carboxymethyllysine) correlated weakly (P<0.05) with those of pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine, but that pentosidine and MDA (malondialdehyde)-lysine varied independently (P>0.5).
results.reference: This is the first known report of concurrent plasma and ISF concentrations of a meropenem antibiotic during CVVHDF. We observed that the ISF concentrations of meropenem were significantly lower than the plasma concentrations, although the present dose was appropriate for infections caused by intermediately susceptible pathogens (MIC≤4 mg/L).

results.question: Does Sensation Return to the Nasal Tip After Microfat Grafting?
rewritten: Is Sensory Function Restored at the Nasal Tip Following Microfat Grafting Procedures?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that after microfat injections, patients initially experience numbness or decreased sensation in the nasal tip, but this sensation gradually recovers over time. Specifically, the touch threshold values improved progressively from week 1 to week 12, and the percentage of patients experiencing paresthesia diminished to none, suggesting that sensation does return after microfat grafting.

yes
contexts: Patients usually complain about numbness in the nasal tip after microfat injections. The present study evaluated the severity of the numbness in the nasal tip after the procedure.

To address the research question, a prospective study of young women was designed and performed at the Beijing Anzhen Hospital. Time was the primary predictor variable. The nasal tip sensation, which was evaluated using objective and subjective assessments, was used as the primary outcome variable. The McNemar-Bowker test (time vs nasal tip sensation) was used to detect statistical significance.

The sample was composed of 25 patients. Preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health were restored in most patients. Esthetic outcomes were deemed satisfactory by clinicians and patients. Neither permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed.

A total of 30 young women (age 20.04 ± 3.63 years) were recruited for the present study. The preoperative mean touch threshold value was 3.60 units. One week after the injection, the women experienced a decrease in the touch threshold value by 2.50 units. However, the sensation recovered gradually during the follow-up period (1.51 units at week 2, 2.39 units at week 4, 3.01 units at week 8, and 3.35 units at week 12). Significant differences were detected between multiple different measurement points (P<.05). The percentage of those experiencing paresthesia after the microfat injections also gradually diminished to none.

Only patients with isolated nasal fractures were included in the study. Patients with additional maxillofacial fractures and patients whose application time to our clinic was more than 10 days after the trauma were excluded. Patients were classified into 5 types according to their fracture. All patients underwent closed reduction and external fixation under local anesthesia. Patients were asked about their satisfaction in a survey at 28th day and sixth month after the surgery. Patients were divided into groups according to fracture type and intervention time, and the results of the survey were evaluated.
results.reference: Postoperative numbness occurs in most patients receiving nasal microfat injections. Partial to complete recovery of nasal tip sensation can be expected to occur over a 3-month period.

results.question: Do older men benefit from curative therapy of localized prostate cancer?
rewritten: Do older male patients with localized prostate cancer experience improved outcomes from curative treatment modalities such as radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that potentially curative therapy (radical prostatectomy or external beam radiotherapy) prolongs life expectancy and quality-adjusted life expectancy in men with localized prostate cancer up to age 75 for well- and moderately differentiated tumors, and up to age 80 for poorly differentiated disease. Benefits are limited to men with mild or no comorbidities, suggesting that older men beyond these ages may not benefit as much. Therefore, older men (beyond 75-80 years) do not generally benefit from curative therapy.

no
contexts: We evaluated three treatments, using a decision-analytic Markov model: radical prostatectomy (RP (radical prostatectomy)), external beam radiotherapy (EBRT (external beam radiotherapy)), and watchful waiting (WW (watchful waiting)). Rates of treatment complications and pretreatment incontinence and impotence were derived from published studies. We estimated treatment efficacy using three data sources: cancer registry cohort data, pooled case series, and modern radiotherapy studies. Utilities were obtained from 141 prostate cancer patients and from published studies.

For men with well-differentiated tumors and few comorbidities, potentially curative therapy (RP (radical prostatectomy) or EBRT (external beam radiotherapy)) prolonged LE (life expectancy) up to age 75 years but did not improve QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) at any age. For moderately differentiated cancers, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 75 years. For poorly differentiated disease, potentially curative therapy resulted in LE (life expectancy) and QALE (quality-adjusted life expectancy) gains up to age 80 years. Benefits of potentially curative therapy were restricted to men with no worse than mild comorbidity. When cohort and pooled case series data were used, RP (radical prostatectomy) was preferred over EBRT (external beam radiotherapy) in all groups but was comparable to modern radiotherapy.

The study evaluated 629 patients with clinically localized PC (prostate cancer) who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2010 and 2013. Exclusion criteria were signs of systemic infection, symptoms of an autoimmune disease or neoadjuvant androgen deprivation.

One hundred fifty patients with primary prostate cancer (T(1-3)N(0)M(0)) were informed by means of a decision aid of two treatment options: radiotherapy with 70 Gy versus 74 Gy. The latter treatment is associated with more cure and more toxicity. The patients were asked whether they wanted to choose, and if so which treatment they preferred. They also assigned importance weights to the probability of various outcomes, such as survival, cure and adverse effects. Patients who wanted to choose their own treatment (n = 119) are described here.

To analyze, retrospectively, the patterns and behavior of metastatic lesions in prostate cancer patients treated with external beam radiotherapy and to investigate whether patients with<or =5 lesions had an improved outcome relative to patients with>5 lesions.
results.reference: Potentially curative therapy results in significantly improved LE and QALE for older men with few comorbidities and moderately or poorly differentiated localized prostate cancer. Age should not be a barrier to treatment in this group.

results.question: Pituitary apoplexy: do histological features influence the clinical presentation and outcome?
rewritten: Does the histopathological profile of pituitary apoplexy influence its clinical presentation and patient outcomes?
results.answer:
The retrospective analysis described in the abstracts divided patients with pituitary apoplexy into groups based on histological features (infarction alone vs. hemorrhagic infarction/hemorrhage) and compared their clinical presentation and outcomes. This suggests that histological features were considered relevant to clinical presentation and outcome, supporting the idea that these features influence the disease course.

yes
contexts: A retrospective analysis of a contemporary series of patients with pituitary apoplexy was performed to ascertain whether the histopathological features influence the clinical presentation or the outcome.

A retrospective analysis was performed in 59 patients treated for pituitary apoplexy at the University of Virginia Health System, Charlottesville, Virginia, or Groote Schuur Hospital, University of Cape Town, South Africa. The patients were divided into two groups according to the histological features of their disease: one group with infarction alone, comprising 22 patients; and the other with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage, comprising 37 patients. The presenting symptoms, clinical features, endocrinological status, and outcome were compared between the two groups.
To assess the results of transsphenoidal pituitary surgery in patients with Cushing's disease over a period of 18 years, and to determine if there are factors which will predict the outcome.
The characteristics of both tumors, their association with tumors in other sites and the time of presentation are analyzed.

We describe the case of a 51-year-old woman who presented with a 4-day-history of intense pain in her left flank, hypertension, fever, microscopic hematuria, and acute renal failure. Contrast-enhanced renal ultrasound strongly suggested bilateral renal infarction. Medical history and an extensive workup allowed to exclude systemic embolism, recreational drug abuse, cardiac arrhythmias, and thrombophilia. A possible diagnosis of PAN (polyarteritis nodosa) was considered; however, within 2 weeks of admission, spontaneous remission of her clinical and biological symptoms occurred without the use of any immunosuppressive treatment. Finally, 3 months later, renal arteriography confirmed the diagnosis of PAN (polyarteritis nodosa). The patient remains free of symptoms 1 year after initial presentation.
results.reference: The patients who presented with histological features of pituitary tumor infarction alone had less severe clinical features on presentation, a longer course prior to presentation, and a better outcome than those presenting with hemorrhagic infarction or frank hemorrhage. The endocrine replacement requirements were similar in both groups.

results.question: Do African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight?
rewritten: Do African American women have lower basal metabolic rates and require fewer daily caloric intake to maintain body weight compared to women of other ethnicities?
results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that African American women had a higher baseline weight and BMI and consumed slightly more calories than non-African American women during controlled feeding. After adjusting for confounders, there was no significant difference in caloric intake required to maintain weight between African American and non-African American women. Therefore, the evidence does not support that African American women require fewer calories to maintain weight.

no
contexts: The high prevalence of obesity in African American (AA (american)) women may result, in part, from a lower resting metabolic rate (RMR (resting metabolic rate)) than non-AA (american) women. If true, AA (american) women should require fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight. Our objective was to determine in the setting of a controlled feeding study, if AA (american) women required fewer calories than non-AA (american) women to maintain weight.

AA (american) women had higher baseline weight and body mass index than non-AA (american) women (78.4 vs 72.4 kg, P<.01; 29.0 vs 27.6 kg/m(2), P<.05, respectively). During intervention feeding, mean (SD) kcal was 2168 (293) in AA (american) women and 2073 (284) in non-AA (american) women. Mean intake was 94.7 kcal higher in AA (american) women than in non-AA (american) women (P<.05). After adjustment for potential confounders, there was no difference in caloric intake between AA (american) and non-AA (american) women (Δ = -2.8 kcal, P = .95).

Subjects were 121 men and 111 women (age: 21-67 years, BMI (body mass index): 16-41 kg/m(2)). Height, weight, and BMR (basal metabolic rate) were measured. Continuous open-circuit indirect calorimetry using a ventilated hood system for 30 min was used to measure BMR (basal metabolic rate). A regression equation was derived using stepwise regression and accuracy was compared to 6 existing equations (Harris-Benedict, Henry, Liu, Yang, Owen and Mifflin). Additionally, the newly derived equation was cross-validated in a separate group of 70 Chinese subjects (26 men and 44 women, age: 21-69 years, BMI (body mass index): 17-39 kg/m(2)).

Measurement of basal metabolic rate (BMR (basal metabolic rate)) is suggested as a tool to estimate energy requirements. Therefore, BMR (basal metabolic rate) prediction equations have been developed in multiple populations because indirect calorimetry is not always feasible. However, there is a paucity of data on BMR (basal metabolic rate) measured in overweight and obese adults living in Asia and equations developed for this group of interest. The aim of this study was to develop a new BMR (basal metabolic rate) prediction equation for Chinese adults applicable for a large BMI (body mass index) range and compare it with commonly used prediction equations.

This analysis includes 206 women (73% AA (american)), aged 22-75 years, who participated in the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH (dietary approaches to stop hypertension)) trial-a multicenter, randomized, controlled, feeding study comparing the effects of 3 dietary patterns on blood pressure in individuals with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension. After a 3-week run-in, participants were randomized to 1 of 3 dietary patterns for 8 weeks. Calorie intake was adjusted during feeding to maintain stable weight. The primary outcome of this analysis was average daily calorie (kcal) intake during feeding.
results.reference: These results do not support the view that AA women are at greater risk for obesity because they require fewer calories to maintain weight.

results.question: Emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy: a feasible combined approach in acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding?
rewritten: Is emergency double-balloon enteroscopy combined with real-time visualization of capsule endoscopy a feasible and effective approach for managing acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) combined with real-time viewing of capsule endoscopy (CE) is feasible and useful in managing acute overt-obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB). Specifically, the combined approach correctly modified DBE management in 25% of patients, and emergency DBE had a significantly higher detection rate of lesions amenable to treatment. This supports the feasibility of the combined approach in this clinical setting.

yes
contexts: There are few data concerning emergency double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy)) and its usefulness in the management of severe acute obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding)). The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) and capsule endoscopy (CE (capsule endoscopy)) in patients with overt OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding), analyzing the feasibility of this combined approach.

Emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) in patients with overt OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding) was defined as performance within 24 h of symptom onset. We reported 27 patients (16 men, mean age: 64.6 ± 17.9 years) with overt severe bleeding who underwent 29 emergency DBE (22 anterograde, 7 retrograde). Of 27 patients, 16 (59.3%) underwent CE (capsule endoscopy) with real time (RT (real time)) viewing.

Patients were diagnosed with the following: Dieulafoy's lesion (DL; n = 11, 40.7%), angioectasia (n = 7, 25.9%), tumors (n = 4, 14.8%), diverticulum (n = 3, 11.1%), ulcers (n = 2, 7.4%). We diagnosed 23 lesions amenable to endoscopic hemostasis and successfully treated 21 of them (77.8%). DL detection rate was statistically higher in the emergency DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) group than in OGIB (obscure gastrointestinal bleeding) patients with DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) done 24 h after symptom onset (40.7% vs 0.9%, respectively, P < 0.001). Combined approach with RT (real time) viewing by CE (capsule endoscopy) correctly modified DBE (double-balloon enteroscopy) management in four patients (25%).

From March 2007 to January 2011, 88 DBE procedures were performed on 66 patients. Indications included evaluation anemia/gastrointestinal bleed, small bowel IBD (inflammatory bowel disease) and dilation of strictures. Video-capsule endoscopy (VCE (video-capsule endoscopy)) was used prior to DBE in 43 of the 66 patients prior to DBE evaluation.

The mean age was 62 years. Thirty-two patients were female, 15 were African-American; 44 antegrade and 44 retrograde DBEs were performed. The mean time per antegrade DBE was 107.4±30.0 minutes with a distance of 318.4±152.9 cm reached past the pylorus. The mean time per lower DBE was 100.7±27.3 minutes with 168.9±109.1 cm meters past the ileocecal valve reached. Endoscopic therapy in the form of electrocautery to ablate bleeding sources was performed in 20 patients (30.3%), biopsy in 17 patients (25.8%) and dilation of Crohn's-related small bowel strictures in 4 (6.1%). 43 VCEs with pathology noted were performed prior to DBE, with findings endoscopically confirmed in 32 cases (74.4%). In 3 cases the DBE showed findings not noted on VCE (video-capsule endoscopy).
results.reference: Emergency DBE is feasible, safe and effective in acute OGIB and may avoid major surgery, diagnosing and successfully treating most patients. Combined approach with RT viewing by CE is especially useful to identify recurrent bleeding vascular lesions such as DL that may be easily misdiagnosed by non-emergency DBE.

results.question: Cardiopulmonary bypass temperature does not affect postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome?
rewritten: Does the temperature management during cardiopulmonary bypass influence the incidence of postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome in cardiac surgery patients?
results.answer:
The studies show that both cold (hypothermic) and warm (normothermic) cardiopulmonary bypass result in similar changes in thyroid hormone levels indicative of euthyroid sick syndrome, such as reduced TT4, TT3, and free T3, and elevated rT3, with no significant difference between the temperature groups. Therefore, cardiopulmonary bypass temperature does not appear to affect the development of postoperative euthyroid sick syndrome.

yes
contexts: To determine if temperature during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass)) has an effect on perioperative and postoperative thyroid function.

Patients who underwent either cold (26 degrees +/- 5 degrees C) or warm (35 degrees +/- 1 degree C) CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) were comparable with regard to age, body weight, duration of CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass), cross-clamp time, use of inotropes, total heparin dose, and length of hospital stay. Incidence of postoperative myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, and death were similar. In both groups, TT4 and TT3 were reduced below baseline values beginning with CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) and persisting for up to 5 days after CPB (p<0.05), free T3 (triiodothyronine) was reduced for up to 3 days after CPB (p<0.05), mean serum rT3 was elevated on POD (postoperative days) 1 and POD (postoperative days) 3 (p<0.05), and TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone) remained unchanged.
Twelve patients scheduled to undergo cardiac operations with normothermic (n = 6) or hypothermic (n = 6) CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass).

Blood was analyzed for serum concentration of total thyroxine (TT4), total triiodothyronine (TT3), free T3 (fT3), reverse T3 (rT3), and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone)) preoperatively, 60 min after CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass) was initiated, 30 min after discontinuing CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass), and on postoperative days (POD (postoperative days)) 1, 3, and 5.
Prospective study comparing thyroid function during and after hypothermic and normothermic CPB (cardiopulmonary bypass).
results.reference: The results of this study suggest that normothermic CPB does not prevent the development of the "euthyroid sick syndrome" during and after CPB. Despite these changes in thyroid function, most patients in both groups had a normal postoperative recovery.

results.question: Body dysmorphic disorder: does it have a psychotic subtype?
rewritten: Body dysmorphic disorder: is there a recognized psychotic subtype characterized by delusional beliefs?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) can present with psychotic features, as there is a distinction made between nonpsychotic BDD (with some insight) and psychotic BDD (without insight and of delusional intensity). The study comparing these subtypes found differences in psychotic disorder diagnoses, supporting the existence of a psychotic subtype of BDD.

yes
contexts: Although body dysmorphic disorder (BDD (body dysmorphic disorder)) is classified in DSM-III-R as a nonpsychotic somatoform disorder, controversy exists as to whether BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) can present with psychotic features. If it can, this raises the possibility that its DSM-III-R psychotic counterpart-delusional disorder, somatic type--may not be a separate disorder. The purpose of this study was to determine whether patients with nonpsychotic BDD (defined according to DSM-III-R criteria, i.e., with maintenance of some insight) were different from patients with psychotic BDD (those whose preoccupation was without insight and of delusional intensity).

Patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) displayed a significantly higher rate of lifetime DSM-III-R psychotic disorder diagnoses than patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder). However, the two groups did not differ significantly on most other variables examined. For instance, both psychotic and nonpsychotic patients displayed significant morbidity; high comorbidity with mood, anxiety, and psychoactive substance use disorders; and apparent preferential response to serotonin reuptake inhibitors rather than to non-serotonin reuptake blocking antidepressants or antipsychotics.

Fifty consecutive patients meeting DSM-III-R criteria A and C for BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were assessed with a semistructured interview and the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R (SCID (structured clinical interview for dsm-iii-r)). Family histories of psychiatric disorders were blindly assessed. The 24 patients with nonpsychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) were compared with the 26 patients with psychotic BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) with respect to demographics, phenomenology, course of illness, associated features, comorbid psychiatric disorders, family history, and treatment response.

This was a retrospective study of 18 consecutive adults with a partial seizure disorder and PIPE (study group) and 36 patients with a partial seizure disorder but without PIPE (control group). These two groups were compared with respect to the likelihood of developing IPE (interictal psychotic episodes) over an 8-year follow-up period and the variables operant in the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Statistical analyses consisted of logistic regression models to identify the variables predictive of the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Predictors included: number and location of ictal foci, seizure type, etiology, age at seizure onset, duration of seizure disorder, MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) abnormalities, and psychiatric history prior to the index video/EEG (electroencephalogram) monitoring (other than PIPE (psychotic episodes)).

The point prevalence of pain was about 50%, the 6-month prevalence 75.5% and the 12-month prevalence 76.5%. The patients' most frequent complaints were low back pain, headache and shoulder and neck pain. Patients with affective disorders most frequently had pain complaints, followed by those with neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders and those with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia, schizotypic and delusional disorders. Almost 10% of all patients reported pain continuing at least 3 months in the past year. Impairment and unfitness for work were related to specific psychiatric diagnosis. Statistically significant risk factors for pain were depression (OR=6.05) and the number of past admissions to psychiatric hospitals (OR=3.609).
results.reference: Body dysmorphic disorder may have a closely related psychotic subtype that significantly overlaps with, or may even be the same disorder as, the BDD variant of delusional disorder, somatic type. Inclusion of a psychotic subtype for BDD should be considered for future editions of DSM.

results.question: Does receipt of hospice care in nursing homes improve the management of pain at the end of life?
rewritten: Does receipt of hospice care services in nursing home settings improve pain management outcomes in terminally ill patients during end-of-life care?
results.answer:
The data show that hospice residents in nursing homes were more likely to receive regular treatment for daily pain (51% vs. 33%) and were twice as likely to receive regular analgesic treatment compared to nonhospice residents. Additionally, hospice residents were less likely to receive analgesics not recommended by guidelines, indicating better adherence to pain management standards. Therefore, receipt of hospice care improves pain management at the end of life in nursing homes.

yes
contexts: To compare analgesic management of daily pain for dying nursing home residents enrolled and not enrolled in Medicare hospice.

A subset of residents with daily pain near the end of life taken from a matched cohort of hospice (2,644) and nonhospice (7,929) nursing home residents who had at least two resident assessments (Minimum Data Sets (MDSs)) completed, their last between 1992 and 1996, and who died before April 1997. The daily pain subset consisted of 709 hospice and 1,326 nonhospice residents.

Detailed drug use data contained on the last MDS before death were used to examine analgesic management of daily pain. Guidelines from the American Medical Directors Association (AMDA (american medical directors association)) were used to identify analgesics not recommended for use in managing chronic pain in long-term care settings. The study outcome, regular treatment of daily pain, examined whether patients received any analgesic, other than those not recommended by AMDA (american medical directors association), at least twice a day for each day of documented daily pain (i.e., 7 days before date of last MDS).

Fifteen percent of hospice residents and 23% of nonhospice residents in daily pain received no analgesics (odds ratio (OR) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)) = 0.45-0.74). A lower proportion of hospice residents (21%) than of nonhospice residents (29%) received analgesics not recommended by AMDA (OR = 0.65, 95% CI (confidence interval) =0.52-0.80). Overall, acetaminophen (not in combination with other drugs) was used most frequently for nonhospice residents (25% of 1,673 prescriptions), whereas morphine derivatives were used most frequently for hospice residents (30% of 1,058 prescriptions). Fifty-one percent of hospice residents and 33% of nonhospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain. Controlling for clinical confounders, hospice residents were twice as likely as nonhospice residents to receive regular treatment for daily pain (adjusted odds ratio = 2.08, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.68-2.56).

The services demonstrated that it was feasible to embed the Model into their organizational structures. Advance care planning conversations and involvement of family was an important outcome measure rather than completion rate of advance care planning documents in community settings. Services adapted and applied their own concept of community, which widened the impact of the model. Changes to quality audit processes were essential to consolidate the model into routine palliative care practice.
results.reference: Findings suggest that analgesic management of daily pain is better for nursing home residents enrolled in hospice than for those not enrolled in hospice.The prescribing practices portrayed by this study reveal that many dying nursing home residents in daily pain are receiving no analgesic treatment or are receiving analgesic treatment inconsistent with AMDA and other pain management guidelines. Improving the analgesic management of pain in nursing homes is essential if high-quality end-of-life care in nursing homes is to be achieved.

results.question: Fulfilling human resources development goal in West Africa: can the training of ophthalmologist diplomates be improved?
rewritten: Can the training programs for ophthalmologist diplomates in West Africa be enhanced to better achieve human resources development goals in eye care?
results.answer:
The survey of trainee ophthalmologist diplomates in West Africa revealed that while the majority found the program well-structured and felt fulfilled, there were perceived problems such as inadequate sponsorship, short course duration, and poor accommodation. Trainees suggested improvements including increased training posts, higher training allowances, and incentives for trainers, indicating that the training can indeed be improved to better fulfill human resource development goals.

yes
contexts: To ascertain the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats (TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats)) on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training (ODT (ophthalmic diploma training)) in West Africa with a view to improving the programme.
A survey of set 2005 TOD (trainee ophthalmologist diplomats) on ODT (ophthalmic diploma training) was carried out in Ghana, 2006.

Longitudinal cohort studies in sub-Saharan Africa are urgently needed to understand cardiovascular disease development. The trainees included 10 (83.35%) males and two (16.7%) females whose ages ranged between thirty-two and fifty-one years. The sponsors of the trainees included Sight Savers International, five (41.7%); Christian Blind Mission International, three (25.0%); Eye Foundation, Lagos, Nigeria two (16.7%); Ministry of Defence Nigeria, one (8.3%); and Health Authority Ghana, one (8.3%). All trainees were at least good in chalazion surgery and treatment of common medical eye conditions. Majority were at least good in eye surgery like cataract, eleven (91.7%); trabeculectomy nine (75.0%); pterygium 10 (83.3%); eyelid, eight (66.7%); destructive 11 (91.6%) and refraction 9 (75.0%). Some trainees' perceived problems included inadequate sponsorship (33.3%), short duration of the course four (33.3%) and poor accommodation facility two (16.7%). However, trainees' suggested increase in training posts, four (33.3); training allowance three (25.0%); and incentives for trainers/training hospitals two (16.7%).

As with some procedures, trauma fellowship training and greater surgeon experience may result in better outcomes following intramedullary nailing (IMN (intramedullary nailing)) of diaphyseal femur fractures. However, surgeons with such training and experience may not always be available to all patients. The purpose of this study is to determine whether trauma training affects the post-operative difference in femoral version (DFV (difference in femoral version)) following IMN (intramedullary nailing).

results.question: Does binge drinking during early pregnancy increase the risk of psychomotor deficits?
rewritten: Does maternal binge alcohol consumption during the first trimester of pregnancy increase the risk of psychomotor developmental deficits in offspring?
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts specifically examined the effects of binge drinking during early pregnancy on child motor function at age 5 and found no systematic or significant differences in motor function between children of mothers who reported isolated binge episodes and those with no binge episodes. Additionally, no association was found with the number or timing of binge episodes. Therefore, the evidence does not support an increased risk of psychomotor deficits due to binge drinking in early pregnancy.

no
contexts: The potential effects of binge drinking during pregnancy on child motor function have only been assessed in a few, small studies. We aimed to examine the effects of binge alcohol consumption during early pregnancy, including number of binge episodes and timing of binge drinking, on child motor function at age 5.

We performed a prospective follow-up study of 678 women and their children sampled from the Danish National Birth Cohort based on maternal alcohol consumption during pregnancy. At 5 years of age, the children were tested with the Movement Assessment Battery for Children. Parental education, maternal IQ, prenatal maternal smoking, the child's age at testing, sex of child, and tester were considered core confounders, while the full model also controlled for prenatal maternal average alcohol intake, maternal age and prepregnancy body mass index, parity, home environment, postnatal parental smoking, health status, participation in organized sport, and indicators for hearing and vision impairment.

There were no systematic or significant differences in motor function between children of mothers reporting isolated episodes of binge drinking and children of mothers with no binge episodes. No association was observed with respect to the number of binge episodes (maximum of 12) and timing of binge drinking.

It has been suggested that increasing obesity levels in young women lead to intrauterine environments that, in turn, stimulate increased obesity among their offspring, generating an intergenerational acceleration of obesity levels. If this mechanism is important, the association of maternal body mass index (BMI (body mass index)) with offspring BMI (body mass index) should be stronger than the association of paternal with offspring BMI (body mass index).

We compared strength of association for maternal-offspring and paternal-offspring BMI (body mass index) for 4654 complete parent-offspring trios in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC (avon longitudinal study of parents and children)), using unstandardised and standardised regression analysis. We carried out a sensitivity analysis to investigate the influence of non-paternity on these associations.
results.reference: In this study, we found no systematic association between isolated episodes of binge drinking during early pregnancy and child motor function at age 5.

results.question: Does tranexamic acid reduce desmopressin-induced hyperfibrinolysis?
rewritten: Does tranexamic acid reduce hyperfibrinolysis induced by desmopressin administration in patients?
results.answer:
The first abstract states that desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which increases hyperfibrinolysis and bleeding. It also suggests that combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and improve postoperative hemostasis. The second abstract describes a study where tranexamic acid was given before surgery along with desmopressin, implying a strategy to reduce fibrinolysis induced by desmopressin.

yes
contexts: Desmopressin releases tissue-type plasminogen activator, which augments cardiopulmonary bypass--associated hyperfibrinolysis, causing excessive bleeding. Combined use of desmopressin with prior administration of the antifibrinolytic drug tranexamic acid may decrease fibrinolytic activity and might improve postoperative hemostasis.

This prospective randomized study was carried out with 100 patients undergoing coronary artery bypass operations between April 1999 and November 2000 in Gülhane Military Medical Academy. Patients were divided into 2 groups. Desmopressin (0.3 microg/kg) was administrated just after cardiopulmonary bypass and after protamine infusion in group 1 (n = 50). Both desmopressin and tranexamic acid (before the skin incision at a loading dose of 10 mg/kg over 30 minutes and followed by 12 hours of 1 mg.kg(-1).h(-1)) were administrated in group 2 (n = 50).

To look at the effect of stopping FA (folic acid) supplementation in UK rheumatoid arthritis (RA (rheumatoid arthritis)) patients established on methotrexate<20 mg weekly and FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily, to report all toxicity (including absolute changes in haematological and liver enzyme indices) and to report changes in the efficacy of methotrexate.

25 suitable patients were enrolled, and 107 hypotensive events were documented. 40 ST events occurred in 14 patients, of which a quarter were symptomatic. Fourteen HII (hypotension induced ischaemic) events occurred in eight patients, with 13 of the 14 preceded by a fall in diastolic pressure (median diastolic pressure 57.5 mm Hg, interquartile range 11, maximum 72 mm Hg, minimum 45 mm Hg), and six preceded by a fall in systolic pressure (chi(2) = 11.9, p<0.001). ST events were significantly associated with preceding hypotensive events (chi(2) = 40.2, p<0.0001). Patients with HII (hypotension induced ischaemic) events were more frequently taking multiple hypotensive drug regimens (8/8 v 9/17, chi(2) = 5.54, p = 0.022).

In a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 75 patients who were established on methotrexate<20 mg weekly and FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily were asked to stop their FA (folic acid) and were randomized to one of two groups: placebo or FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily. Patients were evaluated for treatment toxicity and efficacy before entry and then at intervals of 3 months for 1 yr.
results.reference: Tranexamic acid administration significantly reduces desmopressin and bypass-induced hyperfibrinolysis. Combined use of tranexamic acid and desmopressin decreases both postoperative blood loss and transfusion requirement.

results.question: Does ultrasound-scored synovitis depend on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
rewritten: Is the severity of synovitis assessed by musculoskeletal ultrasound influenced by the pharmacokinetic profiles of subcutaneous tumor necrosis factor inhibitor therapies in patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1] and [2] specifically investigates the influence of the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents on ultrasound-detected synovitis in rheumatoid arthritis patients. Patients were assessed at peak and trough plasma drug concentrations, and ultrasound evaluations were performed blindly, indicating a direct examination of the relationship between drug pharmacokinetics and synovitis grade. This supports the idea that ultrasound-scored synovitis depends on the pharmacokinetics of subcutaneous anti-TNF agents.

yes
contexts: The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of the pharmacokinetics of s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents on the grade of US (ultrasound)-detected synovitis in RA patients.

Fifty RA patients were prospectively recruited from the Biologic Therapy Unit of our hospital. Inclusion criteria were being in treatment with s.c. anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agents and having had neither changes in therapy nor local corticosteroid injections in the previous 3 months. Patients underwent clinical, laboratory [28-joint DAS (DAS28) and Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI (simplified disease activity index))]and US (ultrasound) assessment at two time points, i.e. at peak plasma drug concentration and at trough plasma drug concentration. US (ultrasound) assessments were performed blindly to the anti-TNF (tumor necrosis factor) agent, the administration time and the clinical and laboratory data. Twenty-eight joints were investigated for the presence and grade (0-3) of B-mode synovitis and synovial power Doppler signal. Global indices for B-mode synovitis (BSI (b-mode synovitis)) and Doppler synovitis (DSI (doppler synovitis)) were calculated for 12 joints and for wrist-hand-ankle-foot joints. B-mode US (ultrasound) remission was defined as a BSI (b-mode synovitis)<1 and Doppler US (ultrasound) remission as a DSI (doppler synovitis)<1.

To look at the effect of stopping FA (folic acid) supplementation in UK rheumatoid arthritis (RA (rheumatoid arthritis)) patients established on methotrexate<20 mg weekly and FA (folic acid) 5 mg daily, to report all toxicity (including absolute changes in haematological and liver enzyme indices) and to report changes in the efficacy of methotrexate.

A severe systemic reaction to sulfasalazine developed in a 21-year old female with rheumatoid arthritis characterized by eosinophilia, granulomatous enteritis and myelotoxicity, cholestatic hepatitis, and seizures. The clinical course and management of this patient are presented as well as a review of the incidence and outcome of severe systemic reactions to sulfasalazine.

Tacrolimus is a potent immunosuppressive drug used in organ transplantation. Because of its substantial toxic effects, narrow therapeutic index, and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability, therapeutic drug monitoring of whole-blood tacrolimus concentrations has been recommended. We investigated the comparability of the results of 2 immunoassay systems, affinity column-mediated immunoassay (ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay)) and microparticle enzyme immunoassay (MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay)), comparing differences in the tacrolimus concentrations measured by the 2 methods in relation to the hematologic and biochemical values of hepatic and renal functions.
results.reference: Our results suggested that s.c. anti-TNF pharmacokinetics do not significantly influence US-scored synovitis in RA patients.

results.question: Counter sampling combined with medical provider education: do they alter prescribing behavior?
rewritten: Does the combination of counter sampling and healthcare provider education influence prescribing behavior in clinical practice?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that medical providers who received education combined with counter sampling significantly decreased their prescribing of COX-2 NSAIDs relative to total NSAID prescriptions, suggesting a change in prescribing behavior. Although total prescriptions for some other medications increased, the intervention clearly influenced prescribing patterns for at least one category of focus medications.

yes
contexts: The prescribing behavior of medical providers in the active intervention and control groups were significantly different at baseline in all three categories of focus medications. This suggested that the results should focus on changes across the two years of the study within the intervention and control groups rather than across the two groups. Medical providers in the intervention group significantly decreased the use of COX-2 NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions relative to total NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescriptions following active intervention (38.9% in year 1 versus 23.7% in year 2, P<0.05). Over the same two time periods, a nonstatistically significant decrease in COX-2 NSAID (non steroidal anti inflammatory drug) prescribing was seen at the control site (67.5% versus 62%, P>0.05). Education and counter sampling did not stop medical providers from significantly increasing the total yearly prescriptions for antihistamines and acid-relief medications that consisted of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (86.7% versus 93.1%, P<0.05) and PPIs (68.9% versus 86.2%, P<0.05). Statistically significant increases in the prescribing of focus-nonsedating antihistamines (77.9% versus 98.3%, P<0.05) and PPIs (77.5% versus 91.4%, P<0.05) were also observed in the control group.

To observe if medical providers alter their prescribing patterns of three relatively expensive categories of medications provided as samples by manufacturers (focus medications) when they receive additional education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower cost alternatives (counter samples) that are made available to dispense.

Medical providers in the active intervention group had: 1) education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower-cost alternatives compared with expensive focus medications 2) counter samples and patient sample handouts available to dispense to patients at their own discretion.

The aim of this study was to determine if educating residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure from computed tomographic (CT (computed tomographic)) imaging alters ordering patterns. This study also explored whether referring physicians are interested in radiation education and was an initial effort to address their CT (computed tomographic) ordering behavior.

Governments are urged to determine methods to control the use of medical resources and curb the rise of healthcare costs. The question is, do health behaviors have an impact on the use of medical resources? This study aims to identify and understand the difference in the number of outpatient visits and health examinations based on various health behaviors and to determine whether patients seek medical care for illness from the same physicians.
results.reference: Education by pharmacists, combined with access to counter samples, may or may not have an effect on medical provider prescribing, depending on the category of medication targeted for cost control.

results.question: Global Longitudinal Pathway: has medical education curriculum influenced medical students' skills and attitudes toward culturally diverse populations?
rewritten: Has the integration of the Global Longitudinal Pathway in medical education curricula influenced medical students' clinical skills and attitudes toward culturally diverse patient populations?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that the Pathway program involves longitudinal experiences with poor populations and aims to influence students' skills and attitudes toward culturally diverse populations. However, a previous study reported no significant attitudinal changes between Pathway and non-Pathway students toward the medically indigent, suggesting the curriculum did not significantly influence attitudes. Therefore, the evidence does not support that the curriculum influenced students' skills and attitudes in this regard.

no
contexts: The purpose of this study was to investigate and differentiate the skills and attitudes of Pathway and non-Pathway students in working with culturally diverse populations by conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses.

The Pathway represents a longitudinal program for medical students, consisting of both domestic and international experiences with poor populations. A previous study reported no significant attitudinal changes toward the medically indigent between Pathway and non-Pathway students.

Community-based medical education is growing to meet the increased demand for quality clinical education in expanded settings, and its sustainability relies on patient participation. This study investigated patients' views on being used as an educational resource for teaching medical students.

This study used a retrospective case-control, multiyear design, with contingency table analyses, to examine the performance of 412 students in the classes of 2005 to 2010 at a midwestern medical school. During their second year, these students took four CPEs that each used three standardized patient (SP (standardized patient)) cases, for a total of 12 cases. The authors correlated each student's average year 2 case score with the student's average case score on a senior (year 4) CPE (clinical performance examination). Contingency table analysis was carried out using performance on the year 2 CPEs and passing/failing the senior CPE (clinical performance examination). Similar analyses using each student's United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE (united states medical licensing examination)) Step 1 scores were also performed. Sensitivity, specificity, odds ratio, and relative risk were calculated for two year 2 performance standards.

Students followed 621 cases, representing a sampling of 14. 1% day surgery cases. Categories of problems highlighted by students included inappropriate patient and procedure selection, inadequate pain management, discharge, communication and resource issues. Students made a number of recommendations including the development of multilingual videotapes and patient information sheets for non-English speaking patients, avoidance of bilateral surgical procedures and improved links with local medical officers. They also developed new guidelines and protocols.
results.reference: Clear and distinct differences between the two studied groups were found indicating the root of this increased confidence may have developed due to exposure to the Pathway program.

results.question: Failed IUD insertions in community practice: an under-recognized problem?
rewritten: Are failed intrauterine device insertions in community healthcare settings an under-recognized clinical issue?
results.answer:
The data show a notable rate of unsuccessful copper T380A IUD insertions in community family planning clinics, with nearly 20% failure in nulliparous women and over 13% in parous women. This suggests that failed IUD insertions are a significant issue in community practice and may be under-recognized, especially since no adjuvant measures were used to facilitate difficult insertions.

yes
contexts: The data analysis was conducted to describe the rate of unsuccessful copper T380A intrauterine device (IUD (intrauterine device)) insertions among women using the IUD (intrauterine device) for emergency contraception (EC (emergency contraception)) at community family planning clinics in Utah.

Six providers performed 197 IUD (intrauterine device) insertion attempts. These providers had a mean of 14.1 years of experience (range 1-27, S.D. ±12.5). Among nulliparous women, 27 of 138 (19.6%) IUD (intrauterine device) insertions were unsuccessful. In parous women, 8 of 59 IUD (intrauterine device) insertions were unsuccessful (13.6%). The adjusted odds ratio (aOR (adjusted odds ratio)) showed that IUD (intrauterine device) insertion failure was more likely in nulliparous women compared to parous women (aOR (adjusted odds ratio)=2.31, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.90-6.52, p=.09).

These data were obtained from a prospective observational trial of women choosing the copper T380A IUD (intrauterine device) for EC (emergency contraception). Insertions were performed by nurse practitioners at two family planning clinics in order to generalize findings to the type of service setting most likely to employ this intervention. Adjuvant measures to facilitate difficult IUD (intrauterine device) insertions (cervical anesthesia, dilation, pain medication, and use of ultrasound guidance) were not utilized. The effect of parity on IUD (intrauterine device) insertion success was determined using exact logistic regression models adjusted for individual practitioner failure rates.

Although record linkage of routinely collected health datasets is a valuable research resource, most datasets are established for administrative purposes and not for health outcomes research. In order for meaningful results to be extrapolated to specific populations, the limitations of the data and linkage methodology need to be investigated and clarified. It is the objective of this study to investigate the differences in ascertainment which may arise between a hospital admission dataset and a dispensing claims dataset, using major depression in pregnancy as an example. The safe use of antidepressants in pregnancy is an ongoing issue for clinicians with around 10% of pregnant women suffer from depression. As the birth admission will be the first admission to hospital during their pregnancy for most women, their use of antidepressants, or their depressive condition, may not be revealed to the attending hospital clinicians. This may result in adverse outcomes for the mother and infant.

To assess the number of "missed opportunities" for influenza vaccination in office-based settings by race and ethnicity and the magnitude of potential vaccine uptake and reductions in racial and ethnic disparities in influenza vaccination if these "missed opportunities" were eliminated.
results.reference: The high rate of unsuccessful IUD insertions reported here, particularly for nulliparous women, suggests that the true insertion failure rate of providers who are not employing additional tools for difficult insertions may be much higher than reported in clinical trials. Further investigation is necessary to determine if this is a common problem and, if so, to assess if the use of adjuvant measures will reduce the number of unsuccessful IUD insertions.

results.question: Type II supracondylar humerus fractures: can some be treated nonoperatively?
rewritten: Type II supracondylar fractures of the humerus in pediatric patients: is nonoperative management a viable treatment option?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that some type II supracondylar humerus fractures can indeed be treated nonoperatively, as 57.9% of fractures in the study were successfully managed without surgery. Specific clinical and radiographic features, such as absence of rotational deformity or coronal angulation and a shaft-condylar angle >15 degrees, were associated with successful nonoperative treatment.

yes
contexts: The range of injury severity that can be seen within the category of type II supracondylar humerus fractures (SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures)) raises the question whether some could be treated nonoperatively. However, the clinical difficulty in using this approach lies in determining which type II SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures) can be managed successfully without a surgical intervention.

We reviewed clinical and radiographic information on 259 pediatric type II SCHFs (supracondylar humerus fractures) that were enrolled in a prospective registry of elbow fractures. The characteristics of the patients who were treated without surgery were compared with those of patients who were treated surgically. Treatment outcomes, as assessed by the final clinical and radiographic alignment, range of motion of the elbow, and complications, were compared between the groups to define clinical and radiographic features that related to success or failure of nonoperative management.

During the course of treatment, 39 fractures were found to have unsatisfactory alignment with nonoperative management and were taken for surgery. Ultimately, 150 fractures (57.9%) were treated nonoperatively, and 109 fractures (42.1%) were treated surgically. At final follow-up, outcome measures of change in carrying angle, range of motion, and complications did not show clinically significant differences between treatment groups. Fractures without rotational deformity or coronal angulation and with a shaft-condylar angle of>15 degrees were more likely to be associated with successful nonsurgical treatment. A scoring system was developed using these features to stratify the severity of the injury. Patients with isolated extension deformity, but none of the other features, were more likely to complete successful nonoperative management.

This study evaluated the outcomes and complications of the surgical treatment of condylar fractures by the retromandibular transparotid approach. The authors hypothesized that such an approach would be safe and reliable for the treatment of most condylar fractures.

A retrospective study was conducted on 23 talar neck fractures recorded over a a period of thirteen years. The following variables were analysed: displacement of the fracture, soft tissue injury, delay and type of treatment, complications, observation of the Hawkins sign, and functional outcome.
results.reference: This study suggests that some of the less severe pediatric type II SCHFs can be successfully treated without surgery if close follow-up is achieved. Fractures with initial rotational deformity, coronal malalignment, and significant extension of the distal fragment are likely to fail a nonoperative approach. An algorithm using the initial radiographic characteristics can aid in distinguishing groups.

results.question: The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: are they worth the price?
rewritten: Are specialty pharmaceuticals cost-effective and do their clinical benefits justify their high prices?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that specialty pharmaceuticals offer significant benefits such as increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, enhanced productivity, and reduced disease burden, which can justify their high costs. However, these benefits come with challenges including high expenses and the need for specialized management and pharmacoeconomic evaluation to control costs effectively. Overall, the evidence suggests that specialty pharmaceuticals are worth their price when managed properly.

yes
contexts: Specialty pharmaceuticals have evolved beyond their status as niche drugs designed to treat rare conditions and are now poised to become the standard of care in a wide variety of common chronic illnesses. Due in part to the cost of these therapies, payers are increasingly demanding evidence of their value. Determining the value of these medications is hampered by a lack of robust pharmacoeconomic data.
To outline emerging strategies and case study examples for the medical and pharmacy benefits management of specialty pharmaceuticals.

The promise of specialty pharmaceuticals: increased life expectancy, improved quality of life, enhanced workplace productivity, decreased burden of disease, and reduced health care spending comes at a significant cost. These agents require special handling, administration, patient education, clinical support, and risk mitigation. Additionally, specialty drugs require distribution systems that ensure appropriate patient selection and data collection. With the specialty pharmaceutical pipeline overflowing with new medicines and an aging population increasingly relying on these novel treatments to treat common diseases, the challenge of managing the costs associated with these agents can be daunting. Aided by sophisticated pharmacoeconomic models to assess value, the cost impacts of these specialty drugs can be appropriately controlled.

To observe if medical providers alter their prescribing patterns of three relatively expensive categories of medications provided as samples by manufacturers (focus medications) when they receive additional education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower cost alternatives (counter samples) that are made available to dispense.

Medical providers in the active intervention group had: 1) education from pharmacists concerning the appropriate use of lower-cost alternatives compared with expensive focus medications 2) counter samples and patient sample handouts available to dispense to patients at their own discretion.
results.reference: Current evidence suggests that when used in targeted patient populations, specialty pharmaceuticals may represent a good health care value.

results.question: Does invasive diagnosis of nosocomial pneumonia during off-hours delay treatment?
rewritten: Does invasive microbiological diagnosis of hospital-acquired pneumonia during off-hours delay initiation of antimicrobial therapy?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) episodes diagnosed during off-hours, there were no delays in treatment. In fact, the time from bronchoalveolar lavage to antibiotic administration was shorter during off-hours compared to day shifts, primarily due to shorter specimen collection-to-antibiotic prescription times, while the antibiotic prescription-to-administration times remained the same.

no
contexts: Of the 152 VAP (ventilator-associated pneumonia) episodes 66 were diagnosed during off-hours. Neither more bronchoscopy complications nor more inappropriate initial antimicrobial treatments for patients were observed between day and off-hour shifts. Indeed, the overall time from brochoalveolar lavage to antibiotic administration was shorter for off-hours than day-shifts due to shorter specimen collection-to-antibiotic prescription times, but antibiotic prescription-to-administration times were the same.

We examined whether invasive lung-specimen collection-to-treatment times for intensive care unit patients with suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP (ventilator-associated pneumonia)) differ with to the work shift during which specimens were collected. We compared weekday day shifts and off-hours (from 6:30 p.m. to 8:29 a.m. the next day for night shifts, from Saturday 1:00 p.m. to Monday 8:29 a.m. for weekends, and from 8:30 a.m. to 8:29 a.m. the following morning for public holidays).

Twenty-four doctors specialized in infectious diseases or clinical microbiology (16 specialists and 8 residents) from five hospitals were asked to assess the appropriateness of antimicrobial agents prescribed for a broad spectrum of indications in 56 paper cases. They were instructed how to handle guideline applicability and deviations. We created a reference standard of antimicrobial appropriateness using the modal assessment of 16 specialists. We calculated criterion validity and interrater and intrarater overall and specific agreement with an index expert (senior infectious disease physician) and analysed the influence of doctor characteristics on validity.

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.
101 patients who developed 152 episodes of bacteriologically confirmed VAP (ventilator-associated pneumonia).
results.reference: An invasive strategy based on bronchoscopy to diagnose VAP was not associated with a longer time to first appropriate antibiotic administration when clinical suspicion of VAP occurs during off-hours.

results.question: Undescended testes: does age at orchiopexy affect survival of the testis?
rewritten: Undescended testes (cryptorchidism): does the age at orchiopexy surgery influence testicular viability and long-term survival?
results.answer:
The study found that testicular atrophy rates varied with age at orchiopexy, being highest in the 13-24 month group compared to younger or older ages. However, after adjusting for testicular location, age was not statistically significant in predicting postsurgical atrophy, suggesting that age alone may not independently affect testicular survival.

yes
contexts: The optimal age at which to perform orchiopexy for cryptorchidism has long been debated. The aim of this study was to determine if age at orchiopexy affected testicular atrophy.

Mean follow up for the study was 25 months. There was postoperative atrophy in 27 testes (7.7%). Intraabdominal testicle was independently associated with increased postsurgical atrophy (p<0.0001). The odds of postsurgical atrophy were 15.66 times higher for an abdominal vs. inguinal location (95% CI (confidence interval): 5.5-44.6). Testicular atrophy was highest for orchiopexy at ages 13-24 months (n=16 of 133, 12%) vs. those less than 13 months (n=3 of 64, 5%), and those greater than 24 months (n=8 of 152, 5%) (p=0.0024). After adjusting for location, age was not statistically significant with postsurgical atrophy (p=0.055).

A retrospective review of patients undergoing orchiopexy from 2000 to 2010 was conducted. An individual testis, rather than patient, was used as the dependent variable. A total of 349 testicles from 1126 charts (ICD (implantable cardioverter defibrillator)-9=752.51) were identified. Primary study outcome was testicular survival without atrophy.

There is controversy surrounding the optimal management of the testicular remnant associated with the vanishing testes syndrome. Some urologists advocate the need for surgical exploration, whereas others believe this is unnecessary. These differing opinions are based on the variable reports of viable germ cell elements found within the testicular remnants. To better understand the pathology associated with this syndrome and the need for surgical management, we reviewed our experience regarding the incidence of viable germ cell elements within the testicular remnant.

We reviewed all cases of neonatal testicular torsion occurring at our institution between the years 1999 and 2006. Age at presentation, physical examination, ultrasonographic and intraoperative findings were recorded. Patients were followed after initial surgical intervention to determine the likelihood of developing a subsequent hydrocele or hernia.
results.reference: From this study we conclude that there is no increase in testicular atrophy in patients less than 13 months.

results.question: Do lipids, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking confer equal risk of myocardial infarction in women as in men?
rewritten: Do lipid levels, arterial blood pressure, diabetes mellitus, and cigarette smoking confer equivalent risk of myocardial infarction in female patients compared to male patients?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts do not specifically compare the risk conferred by lipids, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking on myocardial infarction between women and men. While abstract [5] mentions the number of women and men who suffered myocardial infarction or coronary death, it does not provide information on whether these risk factors confer equal risk across sexes. Therefore, there is no direct evidence to answer the question.

maybe
contexts: We measured hsCRP (high-sensitivity crp) levels, the carotid IMT (intima-media thickness), and conventional cardiovascular risk factors including obesity parameters, blood pressure, lipid profiles, insulin resistance, and smoking habits in 820 volunteers (35-79 years old) in a cross-sectional study.

It has recently been shown that non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C) may be a better predictor of cardiovascular risk than low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C). Based on known ethic differences in lipid parameters and cardiovascular risk prediction, we sought to study the predictability of attaining non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C target and long-term major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event)) in Thai patients after acute myocardial infarction (AMI (acute myocardial infarction)) compared to attaining LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C target.

Within a prospective, population-based cohort study individuals without history of myocardial infarction were identified and the relative risk of baseline variables was assessed in relation to verified myocardial infarction or coronary death during follow-up.

Of study participants, 36% were male. Prevalence of casual high BP (blood pressure) was 19%. In the population, 10% were current cigarette smokers and habitual alcohol use was high at 56%. As measured by body mass index, 2% were obese and 14% had abdominal obesity. RHR (resting heart rate) was elevated (>90 bpm) in 19%. Overall, 79% of study participants were found to have at least one CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factor. RHR (resting heart rate) was significantly associated with age, waist circumference, and BP (blood pressure). Individuals with an elevated RHR (resting heart rate) had a higher risk (OR 1.94, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.15-3.26%, p = 0.013) of casual high BP (blood pressure) compared with participants with normal RHR (resting heart rate) independently of several established CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factors. The regression dilution ratio of RHR (resting heart rate) was 0.75 (95% CI (confidence interval) 0.62-0.89).

Of the 9681 women and 8888 men who attended risk assessment from 1967-1991, with follow-up period of up to 28 years, 706 women and 1700 men suffered a non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary death.
results.reference: This large study of the major risk factors compared between the sexes demonstrates similar relative risk of myocardial infarction associated with cholesterol for both sexes, however, the relative risk is higher in women for many other risk factors such as smoking, diabetes, elevated triglycerides and left ventricular hypertrophy.

results.question: Does family practice at residency teaching sites reflect community practice?
rewritten: Does clinical practice in family medicine residency teaching sites accurately represent the scope and characteristics of community-based family medicine practice?
results.answer:
The data from residency training sites show patient demographics and reasons for visits that are largely similar to those seen in community practice, with many overlapping diagnoses and reasons for visits. Although there are some differences, such as more preventive and therapeutic services and fewer diagnostic services, the overall patient characteristics and visit patterns closely resemble those in community family practice settings.

yes
contexts: Family medicine has aspired to train residents and conduct research in settings that closely resemble community practice. The purpose of this study was to compare the patient characteristics of the ambulatory teaching centers of a consortium of seven community-based university-affiliated family practice residency programs in northeast Ohio with the National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NAMCS (national ambulatory medical care survey)) results for family physicians (FPs (family physicians)) and general practitioners (GPs (general practitioners)).

The medical files of all medicine and surgery residents in their first year of specialization between the years 2005 and 2008 were reviewed. These residents were required to go through a preventive medical visit at the University Center of Family and Community Health.

Ninety-eight faculty and resident physicians at the residency training site of the Northeastern Ohio Universities College of Medicine collected data on all ambulatory patient visits (N = 1498) for one randomly chosen week between July 1, 1991, and June 30, 1992. We compared these data with patient visits reported in the 1990 NAMCS (national ambulatory medical care survey) for FPs (family physicians) and GPs (general practitioners).

Community-based medical education is growing to meet the increased demand for quality clinical education in expanded settings, and its sustainability relies on patient participation. This study investigated patients' views on being used as an educational resource for teaching medical students.

The residency training sites saw slightly more children, women, blacks, and Medicare and Medicaid patients. The most common reason for an office visit in both populations was an undifferentiated symptom. Fifteen of the top 20 "reason for visit" codes were identical, as were 14 of the top 20 diagnoses. More preventive and therapeutic services were offered or performed at our residency training sites but fewer diagnostic services were performed. There were fewer consultations requested at our residency training sites but similar hospitalization rates for patients. The mean duration of visit differed by only 1 minute.
results.reference: The residency training sites of the Northeastern Ohio Universities College of Medicine provide patient care opportunities similar to those found in a national survey of family and general practitioners.

results.question: Midwives' competence: is it affected by working in a rural location?
rewritten: Does working in rural healthcare settings affect the clinical competence and professional performance of midwives?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that midwives in rural and urban settings report similar overall competence, but differ in specific skills, with rural midwives more competent in breech delivery and urban midwives more competent in intravenous fluid replacement and newborn examinations. This suggests that working in a rural location influences the type of competencies midwives develop, though not necessarily their overall competence.

yes
contexts: The response rate from midwives in rural settings was considerably higher (85%) than from midwives in the urban areas (60%). Although the proportion of midwives who reported that they were competent was broadly similar in the two groups, there were some significant differences regarding specific competencies. Midwives in the rural group were more likely to report competence for breech delivery (p = 0.001), while more urban midwives reported competence in skills such as intravenous fluid replacement (p<0.001) and initial and discharge examination of the newborn (p<0.001). Both groups reported facing barriers to continuing professional development; however, more of the rural group had attended an educational event within the last month (p<0.001). Lack of time was a greater barrier for urban midwives (p = 0.02), whereas distance to training was greater for rural midwives (p = 0.009). Lack of motivation or interest was significantly higher in urban units (p = 0.006).

Rising health care costs and the need to consolidate expertise in tertiary services have led to the centralisation of services. In the UK, the result has been that many rural maternity units have become midwife-led. A key consideration is that midwives have the skills to competently and confidently provide maternity services in rural areas, which may be geographically isolated and where the midwife may only see a small number of pregnant women each year. Our objective was to compare the views of midwives in rural and urban settings, regarding their competence and confidence with respect to 'competencies' identified as being those which all professionals should have in order to provide effective and safe care for low-risk women.

This was a comparative questionnaire survey involving a stratified sample of remote and rural maternity units and an ad hoc comparison group of three urban maternity units in Scotland. Questionnaires were sent to 82 midwives working in remote and rural areas and 107 midwives working in urban hospitals with midwife-led units.

Patients living in rural areas may be at a disadvantage in accessing tertiary health care.AIM: To test the hypothesis that very premature infants born to mothers residing in rural areas have poorer outcomes than those residing in urban areas in the state of New South Wales (NSW (new south wales)) and the Australian Capital Territory (ACT (australian capital territory)) despite a coordinated referral and transport system.
To explore the impact of delivery mode on women's postpartum quality of life in rural China and probe factors influencing postnatal quality of life.
results.reference: It is often assumed that midwives in rural areas where there are fewer deliveries, will be less competent and confident in their practice. Our exploratory study suggests that the issue of competence is far more complex and deserves further attention.

results.question: The effective orifice area/patient aortic annulus area ratio: a better way to compare different bioprostheses?
rewritten: Is the effective orifice area to patient aortic annulus area ratio a superior metric for comparing hemodynamic performance of different bioprosthetic aortic valve prostheses?
results.answer:
The study compared the hemodynamic performance of two bioprostheses and used the ratio of effective orifice area (EOA) to patient aortic annulus area to adjust for patient anatomy and valve dimensions. It found no significant difference between the two bioprostheses when using this indexed ratio, suggesting that this ratio is a useful method for comparing different bioprostheses by normalizing for anatomical differences.

yes
contexts: Between August 2000 and September 2002, 139 patients underwent isolated aortic valve replacement (AVR (aortic valve replacement)) with the Mosaic (n = 67) or Perimount (n = 72) bioprosthesis. Intraoperatively, the internal aortic annulus diameter was measured by insertion of a gauge (Hegar dilator), while prosthesis size was determined by using the original sizers. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed to determine hemodynamic and dimensional data. As the aim of AVR (aortic valve replacement) is to achieve a maximal effective orifice area (EOA (effective orifice area)) within a given aortic annulus, the ratio of EOA (effective orifice area) to patient aortic annulus area was calculated, the latter being based on annulus diameter measured intraoperatively.

Operative mortality was 2.2% (Mosaic 3.0%; Perimount 1.4%; p = NS). Upsizing (using a prosthesis larger in labeled valve size than the patient's measured internal aortic annulus diameter) was possible in 28.4% of Mosaic patients and 8.3% of Perimount patients. The postoperative mean systolic pressure gradient ranged from 10.5 to 22.2 mmHg in the Mosaic group, and from 9.4 to 12.6 mmHg in the Perimount group; it was significantly lower for 21 and 23 Perimount valves than for 21 and 23 Mosaic valves. The EOA (effective orifice area) ranged from 0.78 to 2.37 cm2 in Mosaic patients, and from 0.95 to 2.12 cm2 in Perimount patients. When indexing EOA (effective orifice area) by calculating the ratio of EOA (effective orifice area) to patient aortic annulus area to adjust for variables such as patient anatomy and valve dimensions, there was no significant difference between the two bioprostheses.

The aim of this prospective, randomized study was to compare the hemodynamic performance of the Medtronic Mosaic and Edwards Perimount bioprostheses in the aortic position, and to evaluate prosthesis-specific differences in valve sizing and valve-size labeling.

The progression rate of aortic valve obstruction was found to be dependent on the degree of valvar calcification ([VC] scoring 0 to III) and to be exponentially correlated with the aortic valve opening area (AVA (aortic valve opening area)) at initial catheterization. Neither age nor sex of the patient nor etiology of the valvar obstruction significantly influence the progression of aortic stenosis. If AVA (aortic valve opening area) decreases below 0.75 cm(2) with a present degree of VC = 0, or AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 0.8 with VC of I, AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 0.9 with VC of II, or AVA (aortic valve opening area) of 1.0 with VC of III, it is probable that aortic stenosis will have to be operated upon in the following years.
