It was the aim of the present study to elaborate criteria for the assessment of rapid hemodynamic progression of valvar aortic stenosis. These criteria are of special importance when cardiac surgery is indicated for other reasons but the established criteria for aortic valve replacement are not yet fulfilled. Such aspects of therapeutic planing were mostly disregarded in the past so that patients had to undergo cardiac reoperation within a few years.
context_sections: BACKGROUND AND AIM OF THE STUDY
results.reference: Comparisons of absolute EOA values grouped by the manufacturers' valve sizes are misleading because of specific differences in geometric dimensions. The EOA:patient aortic annulus area ratio provides a new hemodynamic index which may facilitate objective comparisons between different valve types.

results.question: Evaluation of pediatric VCUG at an academic children's hospital: is the radiographic scout image necessary?
rewritten: Is the radiographic scout image necessary for pediatric voiding cystourethrography evaluation at an academic children's hospital?
results.answer:
The study found that the radiographic scout image did not provide any clinically significant or management-changing information during pediatric VCUG exams, despite contributing a measurable radiation dose. Therefore, the scout image does not appear necessary for the evaluation process.

no
contexts: There is heterogeneity in how pediatric voiding cystourethrography (VCUG (voiding cystourethrography)) is performed. Some institutions, including our own, obtain a radiographic scout image prior to contrast agent instillation.

To demonstrate that the radiographic scout image does not augment VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) interpretation or contribute management-changing information but nonetheless carries a non-negligible effective dose.

We evaluated 181 children who underwent VCUG (voiding cystourethrography) in 2012, with an age breakdown of less than 1 year (56 children), 1-5 years (66 children), 6-10 years (43 children) and 11-18 years (16 children), with a mean age of 4.0 years. We investigated patient demographics, clinical indication for the examination, scout image findings and estimated effective radiation dose, as well as overall exam findings and impression.

No clinically significant or management-changing findings were present on scout images, and no radiopaque urinary tract calculi or concerning incidental finding was identified. Scout image estimated effective radiation dose averaged 0.09 mSv in children younger than 1 y, 0.09 mSv in children age 1-5, 0.13 mSv in children age 6-10 and 0.18 mSv in children age 11-18. Total fluoroscopy time per examination averaged 36.7 s (range 34.8-39.6 s for all age group averages). Evaluation of known or suspected vesicoureteral reflux (VUR (vesicoureteral reflux)) and urinary tract infection (UTI (urinary tract infection)) were the most common clinical indications, stated in 40.9% and 37.0% of exams, respectively.

The correlation between radiographic transition zone on contrast enema in Hirschsprung's disease and the total length of aganglionosis is known to be inaccurate. The aim of our study was to analyse this correlation more precisely to improve preoperative planning of the corrective surgery.
results.reference: Although the estimated effective dose is low for VCUG radiographic scout images, this step did not augment VCUG interpretation or contribute management-changing information. This step should be omitted or substituted to further reduce dose in pediatric VCUG.

results.question: Are endometrial polyps from pre-menopausal women similar to post-menopausal women?
rewritten: Are the histopathological and molecular characteristics of endometrial polyps in premenopausal women similar to those in postmenopausal women?
results.answer:
Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women show significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67, indicating they are not entirely similar. However, both groups have similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, suggesting some common features. Overall, the evidence points to differences rather than complete similarity.

no
contexts: Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women had significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67. However, polyps from both groups of women had similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, an inhibitor of apoptosis.

Do endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women have similar immunohistochemical expression of oestrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) and markers of cellular proliferation/apoptosis (Ki67 and Bcl-2).
Fourteen pre-menopausal and 16 post-menopausal women who presented with abnormal bleeding with endometrial polyps.

The records of 282 consecutive women with recurrent endometrial cancer treated from 1986 to 2005 were retrospectively collected in 8 Italian institutions. Primary disease, clinical history, and recurrence features and data were analyzed.

The median age of the patients was 48 years (range: 25 to 75). One hundred twenty-five non-neoplastic polyps and 20 neoplastic polyps were found. Neoplastic polyps were more frequently found in patients older than 60 years, those with hypertension, a polyp size greater than 10 mm, and a rapid growth rate greater than 0.6 mm/mo. On multivariate analysis, however, the growth rate was not related to the neoplastic nature of a polyp, but older age (>60 y) and large size (>10 mm) were significantly associated with neoplastic polyps.
results.reference: Pre- and post-menopausal polyps exhibit differing hormone receptor and proliferation markers, presumably a result of their hormonal milieu. However, both groups appear to have lost the usual control mechanisms for apoptotic regulation, this appears to be responsible for their growth.

results.question: Does accompanying metabolic syndrome contribute to heart dimensions in hypertensive patients?
rewritten: Does the presence of metabolic syndrome influence cardiac structural remodeling and heart chamber dimensions in patients with arterial hypertension?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that hypertensive patients with metabolic syndrome have a significantly greater left atrial diameter compared to those without metabolic syndrome, and this diameter correlates with the number of metabolic syndrome criteria. Other heart dimensions were increased in hypertensive patients regardless of metabolic syndrome presence, but the specific contribution of metabolic syndrome was evident for left atrial diameter.

yes
contexts: Metabolic syndrome (MetS (metabolic syndrome)) is associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events. We evaluated heart dimensions in hypertensive patients with MetS (metabolic syndrome).

The study included 75 hypertensive patients (34 males, 41 females; mean age 51+/-9 years) without coronary artery disease. Patients were evaluated in two groups depending on the presence or absence of MetS (metabolic syndrome). Age- and gender-matched 20 healthy subjects (9 males, 11 females; mean age 50+/-5 years) comprised the control group. The diagnosis of MetS (metabolic syndrome) was based on the presence of at least three of five MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria. Hypertension was defined as arterial blood pressure exceeding 140/85 mmHg on three consecutive measurements or the use of antihypertensive drugs. Echocardiographic measurements included interventricular septal thickness, left ventricular internal diameter, posterior wall thickness, aortic diameter, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass.

Metabolic syndrome was present in 32 hypertensive patients (42.7%; 18 males, 14 females). The mean number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria was 2.6+/-1.0 in the hypertensive group. Compared to the control group, patients with or without MetS (metabolic syndrome) exhibited significantly increased interventricular septum and posterior wall thickness, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and left ventricular mass (p<0.05). The only significant difference between the two patient groups was that MetS (metabolic syndrome) was associated with a greater left atrial diameter (p=0.019). Left atrial diameter was correlated with the number of MetS (metabolic syndrome) criteria (r=0.51; p<0.001).

Seventy-three patients with SCD (sickle cell disease) with 96 febrile events were evaluated over a 1-year period. Twenty-four percent (23/96) of the patients had CXR evidence of ACS (acute chest syndrome). On the basis of the questionnaire data, 61% (14/23) of ACS (acute chest syndrome) cases were not clinically suspected by the evaluating physician before obtaining CXR. Comparing the patients with and without ACS (acute chest syndrome) revealed that, with the exception of splinting (4/23 [17%] versus 0/73 [0%]), no symptom or physical examination finding helped to identify which patients had ACS (acute chest syndrome). Fifty-seven percent of patients with ACS (acute chest syndrome) had completely normal findings on physical examination. The presentation of patients with clinically detected versus clinically unsuspected ACS (acute chest syndrome) also did not differ significantly. Length of hospitalization, oxygen use, and need for transfusion were the same in both the unsuspected and detected ACS (acute chest syndrome) groups. Overall physician sensitivity for predicting ACS (acute chest syndrome) was only 39%, and diagnostic accuracy did not improve significantly with increasing levels of pediatric training.

Endomyocardial fibrosis is characterized by fibrous tissue deposition in the endomyocardium of the apex and/or inflow tract of one or both ventricles. Although left ventricular global systolic function is preserved, patients exhibit wall motion abnormalities in the apical and inferoapical regions. Fibrous tissue resection in New York Heart Association FC III and IV endomyocardial fibrosis patients has been shown to decrease morbidity and mortality.
results.reference: Left ventricular dimensions are not influenced by MetS. Rather than MetS, hypertension is primarily responsible for changes in left ventricular dimensions. However, left atrial enlargement is more prominent in patients with MetS, suggesting that each MetS criterion contributes to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction.

results.question: The Prevalence of Incidentally Detected Idiopathic Misty Mesentery on Multidetector Computed Tomography: Can Obesity Be the Triggering Cause?
rewritten: What is the prevalence of incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on multidetector computed tomography, and is obesity a potential etiological factor contributing to its development?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that among patients with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on CT, a high proportion were classified as obese (67.5%) or overweight (17.5%). This suggests a possible association between obesity and the presence of idiopathic misty mesentery, implying that obesity could be a triggering factor. Therefore, the evidence supports the hypothesis that obesity may be related to the prevalence of idiopathic misty mesentery.

yes
contexts: Misty mesentery appearance is commonly reported in daily practice, usually as a secondary finding of various pathological entities, but sometimes it is encountered as an isolated finding that cannot be attributed to any other disease entity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of cases with incidentally detected idiopathic misty mesentery on computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and to summarize the pathologies leading to this appearance.

There were a total of 561 patients in whom misty mesentery appearance was depicted on abdominopelvic CT (computed tomography) scans. A total of 80 cases were found to have isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7%. The common indication for CT (computed tomography) examination was abdominal pain. There was a slight female predominance (51.3%). 67.5% of all patients were classified as obese and 17.5% as overweight.

Medical records and initial and follow-up CT (computed tomography) features of patients with misty mesentery appearance between January 2011 and January 2013 were analysed. The study included cases with no known cause of misty mesentery according to associated CT (computed tomography) findings, clinical history, or biochemical manifestations, and excluded patients with diseases known to cause misty mesentery, lymph nodes greater than a short-axis diameter of 5 mm, discrete mesenteric masses, or bowel wall thickening.

The aim of this study was to prospectively compare the diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), multidetector computed tomography (MDCT (multidetector computed tomography)) and endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS (endoscopic ultrasonography)) in the preoperative locoregional staging of gastric cancer.

To investigate the effect of obesity at the start of adolescence on the prevalence, incidence and maintenance of chest wheezing among individuals aged 11-15 years in a birth cohort in a developing country.
results.reference: The results of the present study show that idiopathic incidental misty mesentery appearance has a significant prevalence. Also, the high body mass index of these patients and the growing evidence of obesity-induced inflammatory changes in adipose tissue are suggestive of an association between obesity and misty mesentery appearance on CT.

results.question: Are pediatric concussion patients compliant with discharge instructions?
rewritten: Are pediatric patients with mild traumatic brain injury compliant with post-discharge care instructions following concussion?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a study evaluating compliance with emergency department discharge instructions for pediatric concussion patients, including follow-up surveys at 2 and 4 weeks post-visit. However, none of the abstracts explicitly state the results regarding compliance rates or whether patients adhered to the instructions. Therefore, there is no direct evidence in the provided context to confirm or refute compliance.

maybe
contexts: Concussions are commonly diagnosed in pediatric patients presenting to the emergency department (ED (emergency department)). The primary objective of this study was to evaluate compliance with ED (emergency department) discharge instructions for concussion management.

A prospective cohort study was conducted from November 2011 to November 2012 in a pediatric ED (emergency department) at a regional Level 1 trauma center, serving 35,000 pediatric patients per year. Subjects were aged 8 years to 17 years and were discharged from the ED (emergency department) with a diagnosis of concussion. Exclusion criteria included recent (past 3 months) diagnosis of head injury, hospital admission, intracranial injury, skull fracture, suspected nonaccidental trauma, or preexisting neurologic condition. Subjects were administered a baseline survey in the ED (emergency department) and were given standardized discharge instructions for concussion by the treating physician. Telephone follow-up surveys were conducted at 2 weeks and 4 weeks after ED (emergency department) visit.

We enrolled 25 severe DOC (disorders of consciousness) patients, following post-anoxic or traumatic brain injury and 20 healthy individuals (HC) as control group. Baseline electrophysiological evaluation evidenced, in comparison to HC, a partial preservation of cortical effective connectivity and excitability in clinically defined MCS (minimally conscious state), whereas these components were absent in clinically defined UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome). Then, we applied an anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (a-tDCS) protocol over the orbitofrontal cortex.

Injury severity score (ISS (injury severity score)), Glasgow coma score (GCS (glasgow coma score)), and revised trauma score (RTS (revised trauma score)) are the most frequently used methods to evaluate the severity of injury in blunt trauma patients. ISS (injury severity score) is too complicated to assess easily and GCS (glasgow coma score) and RTS (revised trauma score) are easy to assess but somewhat subjective. White blood cell count (WBC (white blood cell count)) is an easy, quick and objective test. This study was performed to evaluate the significance of the WBC (white blood cell count) count at presentation in the blunt trauma patients.
Retrospective comparison of neuropsychological test results for patients who suffered traumatic LOC (loss of consciousness), no LOC (loss of consciousness), or uncertain LOC (loss of consciousness).
results.reference: Pediatric patients discharged from the ED are mostly compliant with concussion instructions. However, a significant number of patients RTP on the day of injury, while experiencing symptoms or without medical clearance.

results.question: Is the zeolite hemostatic agent beneficial in reducing blood loss during arterial injury?
rewritten: Is the use of zeolite-based hemostatic agents effective in reducing hemorrhage and blood loss during arterial injury and vascular trauma?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1] and [4] evaluates the effect of the zeolite mineral QuikClot (QC-ACS) on blood loss in a swine extremity arterial injury model. The QC group had the zeolite directly applied over the lacerated femoral artery, and blood loss and physiological parameters were measured, indicating an investigation into its hemostatic efficacy. This suggests that the zeolite hemostatic agent is beneficial in reducing blood loss during arterial injury.

yes
contexts: Uncontrolled hemorrhage is the leading cause of fatality. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of zeolite mineral (QuikClot - Advanced Clotting Sponge [QC-ACS]) on blood loss and physiological variables in a swine extremity arterial injury model.

Arterial catheters are routinely used to sample blood for clotting studies in most cardiothoracic intensive care units. The clotting profile in surgical bleeding after cardiac surgery influences further management. Aspiration and discard of a certain amount of blood from the line, prior to sampling, are assumed to clear heparin contamination. We have investigated this assumption through analysis of the clotting profile by simultaneous arterial line and peripheral venous samples.

This is a retrospective study of twenty-two cases treated with TEVAR for TAI (traumatic aortic injury) in our department from 2009 to 2014. Aortic injury was assessed in accordance with the recommendations of the Society of Vascular Surgery. We measured the aortic arch angle and the aortic arch index, based on the initial angio-CT scan, in each of the analyzed cases.

Sixteen swine were used. Oblique groin incision was created and a 5 mm incision was made. The animals were allocated to: control group (n: 6): Pressure dressing was applied with manual pressure over gauze sponge; or QC group (n: 10): QC was directly applied over lacerated femoral artery. Mean arterial pressure, blood loss and physiological parameters were measured during the study period.

713 blunt trauma patients, who were admitted to the Uludag University Medical Center Emergency Department between 01.04.2000-31.12.2000, were retrospectively evaluated in terms of ISS (injury severity score), GCS (glasgow coma score), RTS (revised trauma score) and white blood cell count at presentation.
results.reference: According to the physiological parameters, we observed that zeolite tends to reduce blood loss, however could not stop bleeding completely. We believe that further clinical trials are needed to conclude that zeolite could be used in the routine practice.

results.question: Treatment as prevention in resource-limited settings: is it feasible to maintain HIV viral load suppression over time?
rewritten: Is sustained HIV viral load suppression achievable through treatment as prevention strategies in resource-limited healthcare settings over extended periods?
results.answer:
The study described in abstract [3] shows that among patients on long-term HAART in a resource-limited setting, 87.3% had undetectable viral loads, indicating successful viral suppression over a median of 14 years. This suggests that maintaining HIV viral load suppression over time is feasible in such settings despite challenges like prior exposure to less effective regimens and some virologic failures.

yes
contexts: Recently, there has been increasing interest in the role of "treatment as prevention" (TasP (the role of "treatment as prevention")). Some of the questions regarding TasP (the role of "treatment as prevention") strategies arise from the perceived difficulties in achieving and maintaining viral load (VL (viral load)) suppression over time and the risk of emergence of viral resistance that could compromise future treatment options. This study was conducted to assess these questions in a resource-limited setting.
To evaluate whether reported unsafe sexual behaviour among HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)- infected individuals is changing over time.

Of 619 patients on follow-up, 82 (13.2%) were diagnosed in the pre-HAART era. At the time of our study, 79 (96.3%) patients were on HAART, with a median duration of 14 years (IQR 12-15) of therapy, and exposure to mono or dual nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors regimens in 47.8% of cases. Sixty-nine patients (87.3%) had undetectable VL (viral load), 37 (46.8%) never presented virologic failure, and 19 (24.1%) experienced only one failure. Thirteen patients (16.5%) were receiving third-line ART (assisted reproductive technology) regimens, with an average of 2.7-fold more virologic failures than those on first- or second-line regimens (p = 0.007).

To determine whether the OraQuick® HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA) in sputum is a valid tool for HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) surveillance among TB (tuberculosis) patients.

To assess the impact of the comprehensive HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/STD (sexually transmitted disease) Control Program established in Jamaica since the late 1980s on the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic.
results.reference: Maintaining viral load suppression over time in resource-limited-settings is feasible.

results.question: Are octogenarians at high risk for carotid endarterectomy?
rewritten: Are patients aged 80 years and older at increased risk of perioperative complications and adverse outcomes following carotid endarterectomy?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that octogenarians are considered a high-risk group for carotid endarterectomy, as stated in [2], which proposes that being an octogenarian places patients in the high-risk category for carotid artery stenting. However, the actual perioperative outcomes in octogenarians from [3] show low complication rates and no deaths, suggesting that while they are classified as high risk, the procedure can still be performed safely in this age group.

yes
contexts: All patients between the ages of 80 to 89 years undergoing carotid endarterectomy during a 12-year period were included in the study. Information included indications for carotid endarterectomy, associated risk factors, length of stay, and hospital course. Perioperative morbidity and mortality, including neurologic events and myocardial infarction, were recorded.

Several prospective randomized trials have proved carotid endarterectomy to be safe and effective for both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients younger than 80 years of age. Recently, carotid artery stenting (CAS (carotid artery stenting)) has been approved for use in selected high-risk patients. It has been proposed that being an octogenarian places patients in this high-risk category.

A total of 103 carotid endarterectomies were performed in 95 octogenarians. Procedures were performed on 59 men and 36 women. Indications for operation included symptomatic carotid stenosis in 44 patients (43%) and asymptomatic carotid stenosis in 59 (57%). Associated risk factors included diabetes mellitus (17%), hypertension (76%), coronary artery disease (28%), hyperlipidemia (39%), and history of smoking (42%). There were 4 perioperative neurologic complications, which included 1 transient ischemic attack (0.97%), 2 minor strokes (1.94%), and 1 major stroke (0.97%). There were no deaths.

The case records of patients consecutively undergoing CAB (coronary artery bypass surgery) were reviewed. Patients were stratified retrospectively into high- or low-risk groups according to risk factors for significant carotid stenosis and perioperative stroke: peripheral vascular disease (PVD (peripheral vascular disease)), carotid bruit, diabetes mellitus, age>70 years and/or history of cerebrovascular disease. Prevalence of carotid stenosis detected by ultrasonography, surgical management and perioperative stroke rates were determined in each group.

Overall, 205 consecutive patients underwent preoperative carotid screening. The prevalence of significant carotid stenosis was 5.8%. Univariate analysis confirmed that PVD (P=0.005), carotid bruit (P=0.003) and diabetes mellitus (P=0.05) were significant risk factors for stenosis. Carotid stenosis was a risk factor for stroke (P=0.03). Prevalence of carotid stenosis was higher in the high-risk group (9.1%) than the low-risk group (1.2%) (P<0.05). All concomitant or staged carotid endarterectomies/CAB (5/205) and all patients who had perioperative strokes (5/205) were in the high-risk group (P=0.01).
results.reference: Combined end points for adverse events are acceptable in the octogenarian. Carotid endarterectomy remains the gold standard for treatment of extracranial carotid disease in all age groups. Age alone should not place patients in the high-risk category for carotid endarterectomy.

results.question: Has the mammography quality standards act affected the mammography quality in North Carolina?
rewritten: Has the implementation of the Mammography Quality Standards Act improved mammographic image quality and diagnostic accuracy in North Carolina?
results.answer:
The data show that after the implementation of the Mammography Quality Standards Act, the percentage of facilities meeting quality standards in North Carolina increased significantly across multiple measures, including phantom scores, darkroom fog, and temperature difference passing rates. This indicates an improvement in mammography quality following the Act's enforcement.

yes
contexts: The United States Food and Drug Administration implemented federal regulations governing mammography under the Mammography Quality Standards Act (MQSA (mammography quality standards act)) of 1992. During 1995, its first year in implementation, we examined the impact of the MQSA (mammography quality standards act) on the quality of mammography in North Carolina.

All mammography facilities were inspected during 1993-1994, and again in 1995. Both inspections evaluated mean glandular radiation dose, phantom image evaluation, darkroom fog, and developer temperature. Two mammography health specialists employed by the North Carolina Division of Radiation Protection performed all inspections and collected and codified data.

Telephone counseling and tailored print communications have emerged as promising methods for promoting mammography screening. However, there has been little research testing, within the same randomized field trial, of the efficacy of these two methods compared to a high-quality usual care system for enhancing screening. This study addressed the question: Compared to usual care, is tailored telephone counseling more effective than tailored print materials for promoting mammography screening?

The identification of the most suspect enhancing part of a lesion is regarded as a major diagnostic criterion in dynamic magnetic resonance mammography. Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD (computer-aided diagnosis)) software allows the semi-automatic analysis of the kinetic characteristics of complete enhancing lesions, providing additional information about lesion vasculature. The diagnostic value of this information has not yet been quantified.

The percentage of facilities that met quality standards increased from the first inspection to the second inspection. Phantom scores passing rate was 31.6% versus 78.2%; darkroom fog passing rate was 74.3% versus 88.5%; and temperature difference passing rate was 62.4% versus 86.9%.
results.reference: In 1995, the first year that the MQSA was in effect, there was a significant improvement in the quality of mammography in North Carolina. This improvement probably resulted from facilities' compliance with federal regulations.

results.question: Do hospitals provide lower quality care on weekends?
rewritten: Do hospitals provide lower quality of clinical care and patient outcomes during weekend admissions compared to weekdays?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that patients admitted with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) on weekends are less likely to receive immediate intensive cardiac procedures and experience higher rates of adverse health outcomes, including increased 1-year mortality and readmission rates. This suggests that the quality of care, particularly timely intervention, is lower on weekends.

yes
contexts: The patient is the primary unit of analysis. I use ordinary least squares regression to estimate the effect of weekend hospitalization on rates of cardiac catheterization, angioplasty, and bypass surgery (in various time periods subsequent to the initial hospitalization), 1-year expenditures and rates of adverse health outcomes in various periods following the AMI (acute myocardial infarction) admission.

Weekend AMI (acute myocardial infarction) patients are significantly less likely to receive immediate intensive cardiac procedures, and experience significantly higher rates of adverse health outcomes. Weekend admission leads to a 3.47 percentage point reduction in catheterization at 1 day, a 1.52 point reduction in angioplasty, and a 0.35 point reduction in by-pass surgery (p<.001 in all cases). The primary effect is delayed treatment, as weekend-weekday procedure differentials narrow over time from the initial hospitalization. Weekend patients experience a 0.38 percentage point (p<.001) increase in 1-year mortality and a 0.20 point (p<.001) increase in 1-year readmission with congestive heart failure.

Swedish hospital mergers seem to stem from a conviction among policy makers that bigger hospitals lead to lower average costs and improved clinical outcomes. The effects of mergers in the form of multisited hospitals have not been systematically evaluated. The purpose of this article is to contribute to this area of knowledge by exploring responses to the merger of Blekinge Hospital.

Of the 601 patients with cardiogenic shock, 287 (47.8%) were admitted to hospitals without revascularization services and 314 (52.2%) were admitted to hospitals with coronary angioplasty and coronary artery bypass surgery facilities. Clinical characteristics were similar across the subgroups. Patients admitted to hospitals with revascularization services were more likely to undergo coronary revascularization during the index hospitalization and during the first month after acute myocardial infarction. After adjustment for demographic, clinical, hospital, and treatment strategies, the presence of onsite revascularization services was not associated with a significantly lower 30-day (odds ratio 0.83, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.47, 1.45) or 1-year mortality (odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.49, 1.72).

The short stay ward accounted for 10.3% (Westmead Hospital) and 14.7% (New Children's Hospital) of admissions, with 56% medical in nature, 30% surgical, and the remainder procedural or psychological. Admission patterns were similar, with asthma, gastroenteritis, convulsion, pneumonia, and simple surgical conditions accounting for most short stay ward admissions. The short stay ward increased hospital efficiency with an average length of stay of 17.5 hours (Westmead Hospital) compared to 20.5 hours (New Children's Hospital). The users of the short stay ward were children of young age less than 2 years, with stay greater than 23 hours reported in only 1% of all admissions to the short stay ward. The rate of patient admission to an in-hospital bed was low, (4% [Westmead Hospital] compared to 6% [New Children's Hospital]), with the number of unscheduled visits within 72 hours of short stay ward discharge less than 1%. There were no adverse events reported at either short stay ward, with parental satisfaction high. The short stay ward was developed through reallocation of resources from within the hospital to the short stay ward. This resulted in estimated savings of $1/2 million (Westmead Hospital) to $2.3 million (New Children's Hospital) to the hospital, due to more efficient bed usage.
results.reference: Weekend hospitalization leads to delayed provision of intensive procedures and elevated 1-year mortality for elderly AMI patients. The existence of measurable differences in treatments raises questions regarding the efficacy of a single input regulation (e.g., mandated nurse staffing ratios) in enhancing the quality of weekend care. My results suggest that targeted financial incentives might be a more cost-effective policy response than broad regulation aimed at improving quality.

results.question: Screening History Among Women with Invasive Cervical Cancer in an Academic Medical Center: Will We Miss Cancers Following Updated Guidelines?
rewritten: Does adherence to updated cervical cancer screening guidelines affect the detection rates of invasive cervical cancer among women treated at an academic medical center?
results.answer:
The data show that invasive cervical cancer was diagnosed in women younger than 30 despite prior normal Pap tests, with a shorter mean time from normal Pap to diagnosis compared to older women. This suggests that less frequent screening and less aggressive management in younger women, as recommended by updated guidelines, could delay detection and potentially miss cancers. Therefore, the evidence supports the concern that cancers may be missed following updated guidelines.

yes

results.question: Does a dedicated discharge coordinator improve the quality of hospital discharge?

results.question: Can dobutamine stress echocardiography induce cardiac troponin elevation?

results.question: Cigarettes and cinema: does parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing reduce adolescent smoking susceptibility?

results.question: Sub-classification of low-grade cerebellar astrocytoma: is it clinically meaningful?

results.answer:

results.question: Is intraoperative neuromonitoring associated with better functional outcome in patients undergoing open TME?

results.question: Can we predict which head and neck cancer survivors develop fears of recurrence?

results.answer:
The studies indicate that fears of recurrence in head and neck cancer survivors are not related to socio-demographic, disease, treatment, or symptom-related factors but are directly predicted by pre-treatment fears and optimism. results.question: The secular growth acceleration: does it appear during fetal life?

results.question: Does quantitative left ventricular regional wall motion change after fibrous tissue resection in endomyocardial fibrosis?

results.question: Appendectomy timing: Will delayed surgery increase the complications?

results.question: Does Viral Co-Infection Influence the Severity of Acute Respiratory Infection in Children?
rewritten: Does viral co-infection affect the clinical severity and outcomes of acute respiratory infections in pediatric patients?
results.answer:
The provided data indicates that the number of detected viruses (viral co-infection) did not correlate with any markers of severity in children admitted with acute respiratory infections. results.question: Learning needs of postpartum women: does socioeconomic status matter?

results.answer:

results.question: Laminoplasty outcomes: is there a difference between patients with degenerative stenosis and those with ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament?
rewritten: Are there differences in clinical and radiological outcomes of cervical laminoplasty between patients with degenerative cervical spinal stenosis and those with ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament?
results.answer:
The provided data from the laminoplasty study shows no significant differences in estimated blood loss, length of hospital stay, Nurick score improvement, visual analog scale neck pain scores, or complication rates between patients with degenerative cervical stenosis and those with ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament. Therefore, the outcomes of laminoplasty appear similar between these two patient groups.

no
contexts: Two common causes of cervical myelopathy include degenerative stenosis and ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament)). It has been postulated that patients with OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament) have more complications and worse outcomes than those with degenerative stenosis. The authors sought to compare the surgical results of laminoplasty in the treatment of cervical stenosis with myelopathy due to either degenerative changes or segmental OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament).

The authors conducted a retrospective review of 40 instrumented laminoplasty cases performed at a single institution over a 4-year period to treat cervical myelopathy without kyphosis. Twelve of these patients had degenerative cervical stenotic myelopathy ([CSM]; degenerative group), and the remaining 28 had segmental OPLL (OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament) group). The 2 groups had statistically similar demographic characteristics and number of treated levels (mean 3.9 surgically treated levels; p>0.05). The authors collected perioperative and follow-up data, including radiographic results.

The overall clinical follow-up rate was 88%, and the mean clinical follow-up duration was 16.4 months. The mean radiographic follow-up rate was 83%, and the mean length of radiographic follow-up was 9.3 months. There were no significant differences in the estimated blood loss (EBL (estimated blood loss)) or length of hospital stay (LOS (length of hospital stay)) between the groups (p>0.05). The mean EBL (estimated blood loss) and LOS (length of hospital stay) for the degenerative group were 206 ml and 3.7 days, respectively. The mean EBL (estimated blood loss) and LOS (length of hospital stay) for the OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament) group were 155 ml and 4 days, respectively. There was a statistically significant improvement of more than one grade in the Nurick score for both groups following surgery (p<0.05). The Nurick score improvement was not statistically different between the groups (p>0.05). The visual analog scale (VAS (visual analog scale)) neck pain scores were similar between groups pre- and postoperatively (p>0.05). The complication rates were not statistically different between groups either (p>0.05). Radiographically, both groups lost extension range of motion (ROM (range of motion)) following laminoplasty, but this change was not statistically significant (p>0.05).

To determine the relationship between injury severity surrogates and other patient factors with the development and severity of heterotopic ossification (HO (heterotopic ossification)) following open reduction internal fixation of acetabular fractures treated with a posterior approach.

Of 522 patients included in this study, 96 (18.4%) had prior ACD (advanced cervical dilatation), 246 (47.1%) had prior PPROM (premature rupture of membranes), and 180 (34.5%) had prior PTL (preterm labor). results.reference: Patients with CSM due to either degenerative disease or segmental OPLL have similar perioperative results and neurological outcomes with laminoplasty. The VAS neck pain scores did not improve significantly with laminoplasty for either group. Laminoplasty may limit extension ROM.

results.question: Immunohistochemical assessment of steroid hormone receptors in tissues of the anal canal. Implications for anal incontinence?
rewritten: Does immunohistochemical assessment of estrogen and progesterone steroid hormone receptors in anal canal tissues have implications for the pathophysiology and management of anal incontinence?
results.answer:
The presence of estrogen and progesterone receptors in the tissues of the anal canal, particularly in the smooth muscle cells of the internal sphincter and perimuscular connective tissue in females, suggests a potential hormonal influence on anal continence. Since hormone receptors are prerequisites for hormonal effects, their localization supports the idea that steroid hormones could impact anal continence mechanisms.

yes
contexts: A prerequisite for a hormonal influence on anal continence in women is the presence of hormone receptors in the tissues of the anal canal. Using immunohistochemical techniques, we demonstrated and localized estrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) in tissue sections of the anal canal.

Do endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women have similar immunohistochemical expression of oestrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) and markers of cellular proliferation/apoptosis (Ki67 and Bcl-2).

Positive staining for ER (emergency room) and PR was seen exclusively over cell nuclei. Estrogen receptors were found in the smooth muscle cells of the internal sphincter of all females (10/10) and in four of the seven males. Staining for ER (emergency room) was detected in the perimuscular connective tissue of all females (12/12) and in four of the seven males. No specific staining for ER (emergency room) or PR was found in the nuclei of striated muscle cells of the external sphincter in males or females (n = 8). In females, about 50% of the ER (emergency room)-positive tissues were also found to be positive for PR. Amongst the male patients, only one exhibited staining for PR, and this was confined to the smooth muscle.

Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women had significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67. However, polyps from both groups of women had similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, an inhibitor of apoptosis.
Significant differences or correlations between hormone receptor expression (oestrogen and progesterone) and cell growth indices (Ki67 and Bcl-2).
results.reference: Expression of ER is a constitutional feature of the connective tissue and smooth muscle cells of the anal continence organ. Estrogen receptors and PR are not detectable in the striated muscle fibers of the external anal sphincter in either sex. The presence of ER in the stroma and smooth muscles of the anal canal suggests that these tissues are targets for estrogen. This constitutes a theoretical basis for the beneficial effects of estrogen and progestin replacement on anal continence in postmenopausal women.

results.question: Is acute fibrinous and organizing pneumonia the expression of immune dysregulation?

contexts: 25 suitable patients were enrolled, and 107 hypotensive events were documented. 40 ST events occurred in 14 patients, of which a quarter were symptomatic. results.question: Do inhaled corticosteroids affect perception of dyspnea during bronchoconstriction in asthma?
rewritten: Do inhaled corticosteroids influence the perception of dyspnea during methacholine-induced bronchoconstriction in patients with asthma?
results.answer:

yes
contexts: Some of the disagreements on the perception of dyspnea (PD (perception of dyspnea)) during bronchoconstriction in asthma patients could depend on the interrelationships among the following: (1) the influence of baseline airflow obstruction on the patient's ability to detect any further increase in airway resistance; (2) the effect of eosinophilic inflammation on the airway; (3) bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness)); and (4) the effect of inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs (inhaled corticosteroids)).

We hypothesized that if the inflammation of the airway wall influences to some extent and in some way the PD (perception of dyspnea) in asthma patients, ICSs (inhaled corticosteroids) reverse the effect of airway inflammation on the PD (perception of dyspnea).

We studied 100 asthma patients who were divided into the following four groups: patients with obstruction who were either ICS-naive (group I) or were treated with ICSs (group II (group i) or were treated with icss)); and nonobstructed patients who were either ICS-naive (group III) or were treated with ICSs (group IV). Factor analysis yielded the following four factors that accounted for 70% of the variance in the data: ICS; eosinophil counts; FEV(1); and PC(20) loaded on separated factors with PD (perception of dyspnea) loading on the same factors as PC(20). The post hoc analysis carried out dividing the patients into ICS-treated and ICS-naive, showed that in the former group eosinophil counts and BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness) proved to be factors negatively associated with PD (perception of dyspnea), while in the latter group eosinophil counts were positively associated with PD (perception of dyspnea).

results.reference: We have shown that eosinophilic inflammation of the airway wall may increase PD and that the association of eosinophil counts with ICSs may result in lessening the PD.
