Although selective and non-selective methods of preoperative carotid screening have been advocated, it remains unclear if this screening is clinically relevant.AIM: To test whether selective carotid screening is as effective as non-selective screening in detecting significant carotid disease.

With the advancement of an aging society in the world, an increasing number of elderly patients have been hospitalized due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH (aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage)). There is no study that compares the elderly cases of aSAH (aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage) who receive the definitive treatment with those who treated conservatively. The aim of this study was to investigate the feasibility of the definitive surgery for the acute subarachnoid cases aged 80 or older.
results.reference: In patients with limb-threatening ischemia and lack of venous material for a straightforward venous femorocrural bypass, semi-closed endarterectomy of the superficial femoral artery combined with a short popliteo-crural bypass provides a good alternative.

results.question: Can biofeedback training of psychophysiological responses enhance athletes' sport performance?
rewritten: Can biofeedback training targeting autonomic psychophysiological responses improve athletic performance outcomes in competitive athletes?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that biofeedback training improved athletes' ability to control psychophysiological parameters such as heart rate, skin conductance, and heart-breathing coherence under stress. One year after training, athletes reported continued use of these skills and perceived enhancements in their athletic performance, suggesting that biofeedback can enhance sport performance.

yes
contexts: In recent years, biofeedback has become increasingly popular for its proven success in peak performance training - the psychophysiological preparation of athletes for high-stakes sport competitions, such as the Olympic games. The aim of this research was to test whether an 8-week period of exposure to biofeedback training could improve the psychophysiological control over competitive anxiety and enhance athletic performance in participating subjects.

Participants of this study were highly competent athletes, each training in different sport disciplines. The experimental group consisted of 18 athletes (4 women, 14 men), whereas the Control group had 21 athletes (4 women, 17 men). All athletes were between 16 and 34 years old. The biofeedback device, Nexus 10, was used to detect and measure the psychophysiological responses of athletes. Athletes from both groups (control and experimental) were subjected to stress tests at the beginning of the study and once again at its conclusion. In between, the experimental group received training in biofeedback techniques. We then calculated the overall percentage of athletes in the experimental group compared with those in the control group who were able to control respiration, skin conductance, heart rate, blood flow amplitude, heart rate variability, and heart respiration coherence. One year following completion of the initial study, we questioned athletes from the experimental group, to determine whether they continued to use these skills and if they could detect any subsequent enhancement in their athletic performance.

Various factors contribute to the effective implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs (evidence-based treatments)). In this study, cognitive processing therapy (CPT (cognitive processing therapy)) was administered in a Veterans Affairs (VA (veterans affairs)) posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD (posttraumatic stress disorder)) specialty clinic in which training and supervision were provided following VA (veterans affairs) implementation guidelines. The aim was to (a) estimate the proportion of variability in outcome attributable to therapists and (b) identify characteristics of those therapists who produced better outcomes.

We demonstrated that a greater number of participants in the experimental group were able to successfully control their psychophysiological parameters, in comparison to their peers in the control group. Significant results (p<0.05) were noted in regulation of GSR following short stress test conditions (p = 0.037), in regulation of HR after exposure to STROOP stressor (p = 0.037), in regulation of GSR following the Math and GSR stressors (p = 0.033, p = 0.409) and in achieving HR - breathing coherence following the math stressor (p = 0.042).
To explore the secondary benefits of treadmill training for people in the chronic stage of recovery from stroke.
results.reference: One year following completion of the training program, all participants from the experimental group indicated that they were still using the biofeedback - psycho-regulation skills. Furthermore, these participants uniformly reported believing that these skills had enhanced their athletic performance and general well-being.

results.question: Do cytokines have any role in epilepsy?
rewritten: Do pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines play a role in the pathophysiology and progression of epilepsy?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts show that various cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-2, IL-4, IFN-gamma) are detectable in patients with epilepsy and new onset seizures, with correlations noted between cytokine levels and clinical parameters such as status epilepticus and duration of epilepsy. Additionally, cytokine levels decrease during seizure-free periods, suggesting a role in the pathophysiology of epilepsy.

yes
contexts: We analyzed cytokines levels in patients with epilepsy and new onset seizure and correlated it with various parameters.

The type of seizures (n=100) was major (45), partial (41) and status epilepticus (SE (status epilepticus)=14 (seizures (n=100) was major (45), partial (41) and status epilepticus)), while the epilepsy syndromes were idiopathic generalized (53) and localization related (47). The detectable serum cytokines in the patient group (n=100) were: IL (interleukin)-6 (42), TNF (tumor necrosis factor)-alpha (36), IL (interleukin)-2 (22), IL (interleukin)-4 (22), IFN-gamma (20) and IL (interleukin)-1 (11) compared to the controls. CSF IL (interleukin)-6 and IL (interleukin)-1 was detectable in 4/9 and 2/9 patients, respectively while, IL (interleukin)-2, IL (interleukin)-4, IFN-gamma was detectable 1 in each patient. Correlations were noted between male gender and IL (interleukin)-1beta (p=0.04), positive family history and IL (interleukin)-1beta (p=0.001), "no alcohol use" and TNF (tumor necrosis factor)-alpha (p=0.05), more than one year history of epilepsy and IL (interleukin)-1beta (p=0.02), status epilepticus (SE (status epilepticus)) and IL (interleukin)-6 (p=0.04). There was no difference between the new onset seizures vs. epilepsy group. Serial analysis during the seizure-free period revealed a decrease in cytokine levels: TNF (tumor necrosis factor)-alpha (25% to 12.5%), IFN-gamma (12.5% to 0%), IL (interleukin)-1 (25% to 0) and IL (interleukin)-2 (6.2% to 6.2%), IL (interleukin)-4 (18.8% to 0%) and IL (interleukin)-6 (18.8% to 6.2%).

Anti-HTLV-I antibodies were positive in both the serum and the CSF in all of the patients. Biopsied sample from spinal cord lesions showed inflammatory changes in Patient 1. Patient 2 had a demyelinating type of sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Two of the three patients examined showed high risk of developing HAM (htlv-i-associated myelopathy)/TSP (tropical spastic paraparesis) in virologic and immunologic aspects.

We found that similar concentrations of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine suppress the T-cell response to MiHC in mice (C57BL/6 anti-BALB.B) and that lysosomotropic amines in combination with cyclosporine result in synergistic suppression of a proliferative response to MiHC. Similar suppression and synergy appear to be present in an alloreactive response (C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c). Direct inhibition by chloroquine of T-cell proliferative responses induced by anti-CD3epsilon in the absence of antigen-presenting cells is present at higher concentrations than that required to suppress responses to MiHC or MHC (major histocompatibility complex). Chloroquine appears to induce decreased T-cell viability at high concentrations. This effect does not appear to be due to decreased T-cell production of interleukin-2 or interferon-gamma. At lower concentrations (<25 microg/ml), chloroquine can also decrease the ability of antigen-presenting cells to stimulate an a C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c T-cell response and can inhibit MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class II expression after activation with lipopolysaccharide.

After obtaining consent, serum samples from 100 patients with epilepsy or new onset seizure were prospectively collected in the immediate post-ictal phase. In 16 patients, a second sample was collected during the seizure-free period. The serum cytokine levels [TNF (tumor necrosis factor)-alpha, IFN-gamma, IL (interleukin)-1beta, IL (interleukin)-2, IL (interleukin)-4, and IL (interleukin)-6] were assessed (ELISA) in these patients and 100 matched healthy controls. CSF analysis was carried out in 9 patients of this cohort, when clinically indicated.
results.reference: We found increased post-ictal serum cytokine levels in patients with several epilepsy syndromes.

results.question: Cue-induced behavioural activation: a novel model of alcohol craving?
rewritten: Is cue-induced behavioral activation a valid experimental model for studying alcohol craving mechanisms?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe a novel animal model where exposure to alcohol-associated environmental cues increases alcohol-seeking behavior and consumption in rats, even after a break from training. This cue-induced behavioral activation is measurable and can be blocked by naltrexone, supporting its use as a model of alcohol craving.

yes
contexts: Alcohol-associated cues elicit craving in human addicts but little is known about craving mechanisms. Current animal models focus on relapse and this may confound the effect of environmental cues. OBJECTIVES. To develop a model to study the effects of environmental cues on alcohol consumption in animals not experiencing withdrawal or relapse.

Rats were trained to orally self-administer an alcohol (5% w/v)/saccharin (0.2%) solution 30 min a day for 20 days. After stable responding on a free choice between alcohol/saccharin and water, rats were exposed to 5, 10 or 15 min of alcohol-associated cues or 5 min of non-alcohol associated cues. The effect of a 5-min cue was measured after a 10-day break from training or pre-treatment with 0.03, 0.1 or 1 mg/kg naltrexone.

Rats given 5 min of alcohol-associated cues responded significantly more on the active lever (26% increase) and consumed more alcohol as verified by increased blood alcohol levels (8.9 mM versus control 7.5 mM). Ten or 15 min of cues did not change alcohol consumption and 5 min in a novel environment decreased response by 66%. After a 10-day break in training, 5 min of alcohol-associated cues still increased alcohol consumption (29% increase) and the cue effect could be dose-dependently blocked by naltrexone (143% decrease at 0.03 mg/kg).

With a 2 (confederate's drinking condition: alcohol vs. soda) × 2 (participant's stress condition: stress vs. no stress) experimental design, we tested whether the tendency to imitate other people's drinking was related to participants' induced stress levels. The young male adults (N = 106) were randomly assigned to each of the conditions. In each session, directly after the stress or no-stress period, confederates and participants entered a bar laboratory where we observed their drinking behavior. Prior to entering the session, confederates were instructed to drink alcohol or soda.

That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.
results.reference: Cue-induced behavioural activation was specific to alcohol cues, reproducible, persistent and could be blocked by naltrexone, and its correlation with human self-report of craving makes it a potentially useful model for studying alcohol craving.

results.question: Can routine offering of influenza vaccination in office-based settings reduce racial and ethnic disparities in adult influenza vaccination?
rewritten: Can routine administration of seasonal influenza vaccination in outpatient primary care settings reduce racial and ethnic disparities in influenza vaccine uptake among adult populations?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that "missed opportunities" for influenza vaccination in office-based settings are more frequent among racial and ethnic minorities and that eliminating these missed opportunities could reduce disparities in vaccination by about half. This suggests that routine offering of influenza vaccination in these settings could significantly reduce racial and ethnic disparities in adult influenza vaccination.

yes
contexts: To assess the number of "missed opportunities" for influenza vaccination in office-based settings by race and ethnicity and the magnitude of potential vaccine uptake and reductions in racial and ethnic disparities in influenza vaccination if these "missed opportunities" were eliminated.

The frequency of "missed opportunities" for influenza vaccination in office-based settings was significantly higher among racial and ethnic minorities than non-Hispanic whites. Eliminating these "missed opportunities" could have cut racial and ethnic disparities in influenza vaccination by roughly one half.

We collected data on influenza vaccination, frequency and timing of healthcare visits, and self-reported compliance with a potential provider recommendation for vaccination during the 2009-2010 influenza season. "Missed opportunities" for seasonal influenza vaccination in office-based settings were defined as the number of unvaccinated respondents who reported at least one healthcare visit in the Fall and Winter of 2009-2010 and indicated their willingness to get vaccinated if a healthcare provider strongly recommended it. "Potential vaccine uptake" was defined as the sum of actual vaccine uptake and "missed opportunities."

Influenza vaccination remains below the federally targeted levels outlined in Healthy People 2020. Compared to non-Hispanic whites, racial and ethnic minorities are less likely to be vaccinated for influenza, despite being at increased risk for influenza-related complications and death. Also, vaccinated minorities are more likely to receive influenza vaccinations in office-based settings and less likely to use non-medical vaccination locations compared to non-Hispanic white vaccine users.

Identified 4 clusters: Potentials (45%) would receive influenza vaccine to prevent disease; Fearful Uninformeds (9%) were unsure if influenza vaccine causes illness; Doubters (27%) were unsure if vaccine is efficacious; Misinformeds (19%) believed influenza vaccine causes illness. More Potentials (75%) and Misinformeds (70%) ever received influenza vaccine than did Fearful Uninformeds (18%) and Doubters (29%).
results.reference: Improved office-based practices regarding influenza vaccination could significantly impact Healthy People 2020 goals by increasing influenza vaccine uptake and reducing corresponding racial and ethnic disparities.

results.question: Colorectal cancer in young patients: is it a distinct clinical entity?
rewritten: Is colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adult patients a distinct clinical and molecular entity compared to colorectal cancer in older populations?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that young colorectal cancer patients have distinct clinicopathological features, including higher rates of family history, hereditary syndromes, inflammatory bowel disease, more advanced stage at presentation, and different tumor characteristics compared to older patients. Although survival differences were not significant when adjusted for stage, these unique features suggest that colorectal cancer in young patients may represent a distinct clinical entity.

yes
contexts: The incidence of colorectal cancer in young patients is increasing. It remains unclear if the disease has unique features in this age group.

This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study which included patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age ≤40 years in 1997-2013 matched 1:2 by year of diagnosis with consecutive colorectal cancer patients diagnosed at age>50 years during the same period. Patients aged 41-50 years were not included in the study, to accentuate potential age-related differences. Clinicopathological characteristics, treatment, and outcome were compared between groups.

The cohort included 330 patients, followed for a median time of 65.9 months (range 4.7-211). Several significant differences were noted. The younger group had a different ethnic composition. They had higher rates of family history of colorectal cancer (p = 0.003), hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes (p < 0.0001), and inflammatory bowel disease (p = 0.007), and a lower rate of polyps (p < 0.0001). They were more likely to present with stage III or IV disease (p = 0.001), angiolymphatic invasion, signet cell ring adenocarcinoma, and rectal tumors (p = 0.02). Younger patients more frequently received treatment. Young patients had a worse estimated 5-year disease-free survival rate (57.6  vs. 70 %, p = 0.039), but this did not retain significance when analyzed by stage (p = 0.092). Estimated 5-year overall survival rates were 59.1 and 62.1 % in the younger and the control group, respectively (p = 0.565).

A total of 288 patients with invasive cervical carcinoma were identified. Among these patients, 109 had adequate information on prior screening history. Invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC (invasive adenocarcinoma)) was diagnosed in 37 (33.94%) patients, whereas 64 (58.72%) patients were diagnosed with invasive squamous cell carcinoma (ISCC (invasive squamous cell carcinoma)). The remaining eight patients were diagnosed with other types of cancers of the cervix. A total of 13 patients were younger than 30 while 96 patients were 30 or older. The mean time from normal Pap to diagnosis of IAC (invasive adenocarcinoma) was 15 months in patients younger than 30 years of age compared to 56 months in patients aged 30 and older (p < 0.001). The mean time from normal Pap to diagnosis of ISCC (invasive squamous cell carcinoma) was 38 months in patients younger than 30 years of age and 82 months in patients aged 30 and older (p = 0.018).

Morphologic characteristics and type of CRC (colorectal cancers) and SLM (synchronous liver metastases) resection were similar for the GM (n = 45) or SM (n = 66) groups. In patients with delayed liver resection (62 SM, 17 GM), chemotherapy prior to liver surgery was used in 92% and 38% of SM and GM patients (P<0.0001) and the median delay between procedures was 212 and 182 days, respectively (P = 0.04). First step of liver resection was more often performed during colorectal surgery in the GM group (62 vs. 6% for SM, P<0.0001) and the mean number of procedures (CRC (colorectal cancers)+SLM (synchronous liver metastases)) was lower (1.6 vs. 2.3, P = 0.003). Three-month mortality was 3% for GM and 0% for SM (n.s.). Overall survival rates were 67% and 51% for SM and GM at 3 years (n.s.), and 35 and 31% at 5 years (n.s.). Disease-free survival to 5 years was higher in SM patients (14% vs. 11%, P = 0.009).
results.reference: Colorectal cancer among young patients may constitute a distinct clinical entity. Further research is needed to validate our findings and define the optimal approach in this population.

results.question: Can implant retention be recommended for treatment of infected TKA?
rewritten: Can implant retention be recommended for the treatment of periprosthetic joint infection following total knee arthroplasty?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that implant retention in infected TKA has a lower infection control rate compared to two-stage revision (31% vs. 59% after initial treatment, and 81% vs. 91% at latest follow-up). Additionally, retention treatment is associated with factors contributing to failure, such as Staphylococcus aureus infection and polyethylene nonexchange. Therefore, implant retention is less effective and not generally recommended over removal and revision.

no
contexts: We (1) asked whether the infection control rates, number of additional procedures, length of hospital stay, and treatment duration differed between implant retention and two-stage revision treatment; and (2) identified risk factors that can contribute to failure of infection control.

Infection control rate was 31% in retention and 59% in the removal group after initial surgical treatment, and 81% and 91% at latest followup, respectively. Treatment duration was shorter in the retention group and there was no difference in number of additional surgeries and length of hospital stay. Type of treatment (retention versus removal) was the only factor associated with infection control; subgroup analysis in the retention group showed Staphylococcus aureus infection and polyethylene nonexchange as contributing factors for failure of infection control.

Retention treatment is reportedly associated with lower infection control rates than two-stage revision. However, the studies on which this presumption are based depend on comparisons of historical rather than concurrent controls.QUESTIONS/

Reconstruction of the joint line is crucial in total knee arthroplasty (TKA (total knee arthroplasty)). A routine height of tibial cut to maintain the natural joint line may compromise the preservation of the PCL. Since the PCL footprint is not accessible prior to tibial osteotomy, it seems beneficial to identify a reliable extraarticular anatomic landmark for predicting the PCL footprint and being visible within standard TKA (total knee arthroplasty) approach. The fibula head predicts reliably the location of PCL footprint; however, it is not accessible during TKA (total knee arthroplasty). The aim of this study now was to analyze whether the tibial tuberosity can serve as a reliable referencing landmark to estimate the PCL footprint height prior to tibial cut.

The incidence of acetabular fractures in osteoporotic patients is increasing. Immediate total hip arthroplasty (THA (total hip arthroplasty)) has potential advantages, but achieving acetabular component stability is challenging and, at early followup, reported revision rates for loosening are high.QUESTIONS/
results.reference: Although initial infection control rate was substantially lower in the retention group than the removal group, final results were comparable at latest followup. We believe retention treatment can be selectively considered for non-S. aureus infection, and when applied in selected patients, polyethylene exchange should be performed.

results.question: Long-term significance of postictal psychotic episodes II. Are they predictive of interictal psychotic episodes?
rewritten: Does the occurrence of postictal psychotic episodes predict the development of interictal psychotic episodes in patients with epilepsy over the long term?
results.answer:
The study found that a history of postictal psychotic episodes (PIPE) was a significant predictor of interictal psychotic episodes (IPE) in univariate analysis (P=0.006), indicating some predictive value. However, this significance disappeared in multivariate analysis, suggesting that PIPE alone may not independently predict IPE when other factors are considered.

maybe
contexts: The aim of this study was to determine whether postictal psychotic episodes (PIPE (psychotic episodes)) are predictive of the development of interictal psychotic episodes (IPE (interictal psychotic episodes)).

This was a retrospective study of 18 consecutive adults with a partial seizure disorder and PIPE (study group) and 36 patients with a partial seizure disorder but without PIPE (control group). These two groups were compared with respect to the likelihood of developing IPE (interictal psychotic episodes) over an 8-year follow-up period and the variables operant in the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Statistical analyses consisted of logistic regression models to identify the variables predictive of the development of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Predictors included: number and location of ictal foci, seizure type, etiology, age at seizure onset, duration of seizure disorder, MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) abnormalities, and psychiatric history prior to the index video/EEG (electroencephalogram) monitoring (other than PIPE (psychotic episodes)).

Seven patients with PIPE (psychotic episodes) and one control patient went on to develop an IPE (interictal psychotic episodes). Predictors of IPE (interictal psychotic episodes) in univariate logistic regression analyses included a history of PIPE (P=0.006), male gender (P=0.028), and having bilateral ictal foci (P=0.048). Significance disappeared for all of these variables when they were entered into a multivariate analysis.

The prevalence of retinal haemorrhages after convulsions is not well established. As these haemorrhages are considered characteristic of child abuse, we investigated their occurrence after convulsive episodes to see whether the finding of haemorrhage should prompt further investigation.
To identify the features of PMR that may predict the duration of steroid therapy, the occurrence of relapses and the late development of GCA.
results.reference: A history of PIPE may be a risk factor for the development of IPE. Yet, the disappearance of significance on multivariate analysis indicates that it is not an independent predictor.

results.question: Do primary care physicians underprescribe antibiotics for peptic ulcer disease?
rewritten: Do primary care physicians underprescribe antibiotic therapy for Helicobacter pylori-associated peptic ulcer disease?
results.answer:
The data show that only 27.6% of patients with peptic ulcer disease (PUD) received eradication therapy, and even among those with a definitive diagnosis, only 37.7% were treated. This suggests that primary care physicians prescribe antibiotics for PUD less frequently than might be expected given the diagnosis, indicating underprescription.

yes
contexts: To determine how often primary care physicians prescribe eradication therapy for peptic ulcer disease (PUD (peptic ulcer disease)) and nonulcer dyspepsia (NUD (nonulcer dyspepsia)).

During a 2-year period (1998-2000) we analyzed data concerning patients with PUD (peptic ulcer disease) or NUD (nonulcer dyspepsia) seen by 80 Italian primary care physicians uniformly distributed throughout the country. We classified patients as having a definitive or a presumptive diagnosis on the basis of the completeness of the diagnostic workup and interpreted the prescription of antibiotics for dyspepsia as evidence of attempted eradication of Helicobacter pylori.

Of 6866 patients, 690 (10%) received eradication therapy. Of 2162 patients with PUD (peptic ulcer disease), 596 (27.6%) received eradication therapy; of 4704 patients with NUD (nonulcer dyspepsia), however, only 94 (2%) received this treatment (P =.0001). A total of 341 (37.7%) of 904 PUD (peptic ulcer disease) patients with a definitive diagnosis were given eradication therapy and 255 (20.3%) of 1258 PUD (peptic ulcer disease) patients with a presumptive diagnosis were given therapy (P&lt.0001). In NUD (nonulcer dyspepsia) patients, 7 of 743 (0.9%) with a definitive diagnosis received eradication therapy, while 87 (2.2%) of 3961 of those with a presumptive diagnosis were given the same therapy (P =.025).

Electronic health records have the potential to facilitate family history use by primary care physicians (PCPs (primary care physicians)) to provide personalized care. The objective of this study was to determine whether automated, at-the-visit tailored prompts about family history risk change PCP (primary care physician) behavior.
To determine the effect of the 2008 English public antibiotic campaigns.
results.reference: While Italian primary care physicians appropriately target eradication therapy for H pylori infection in patients with peptic ulcer disease rather than nonulcer disease, the intervention was still underused in these patients. Improvements in this prescribing behavior are needed.

results.question: Blunt trauma in intoxicated patients: is computed tomography of the abdomen always necessary?
rewritten: Is abdominal computed tomography always necessary for the evaluation of blunt abdominal trauma in patients with acute alcohol intoxication?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that physical examination is unreliable in alcohol-intoxicated trauma patients, and CT plays the primary role in abdominal evaluations (abstract 1). In a study of intoxicated blunt trauma patients with normal abdominal exams, only a small percentage had abdominal injuries detected by CT, and even fewer required surgery (abstracts 2 and 3). This suggests that while CT is important, it may not always be necessary if the clinical exam is unremarkable and the patient is stable.

no
contexts: Physical examination to detect abdominal injuries has been considered unreliable in alcohol-intoxicated trauma patients. Computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) plays the primary role in these abdominal evaluations.

Of 324 patients studied, 317 (98%) had CT (computed tomography) scans negative for abdominal injury. Abdominal injuries were identified in 7 patients (2%), with only 2 (0.6%) requiring abdominal exploration. A significant association was found between major chest injury and abdominal injury.

We reviewed medical records of all blunt trauma patients admitted to our trauma service from January 1, 1992, to March 31, 1998. Study patients had a blood alcohol level>or =80 mg/dL, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS (glasgow coma scale)) score of 15, and unremarkable abdominal examination.

Injury severity score (ISS (injury severity score)), Glasgow coma score (GCS (glasgow coma score)), and revised trauma score (RTS (revised trauma score)) are the most frequently used methods to evaluate the severity of injury in blunt trauma patients. ISS (injury severity score) is too complicated to assess easily and GCS (glasgow coma score) and RTS (revised trauma score) are easy to assess but somewhat subjective. White blood cell count (WBC (white blood cell count)) is an easy, quick and objective test. This study was performed to evaluate the significance of the WBC (white blood cell count) count at presentation in the blunt trauma patients.

There were a total of 561 patients in whom misty mesentery appearance was depicted on abdominopelvic CT (computed tomography) scans. A total of 80 cases were found to have isolated incidental idiopathic misty mesentery, giving a prevalence of 7%. The common indication for CT (computed tomography) examination was abdominal pain. There was a slight female predominance (51.3%). 67.5% of all patients were classified as obese and 17.5% as overweight.
results.reference: The incidence of abdominal injury in intoxicated, hemodynamically stable, blunt trauma patients with a normal abdominal examination and normal mentation is low. Physical examination and attention to clinical risk factors allow accurate abdominal evaluation without CT.

results.question: Chronic progressive cervical myelopathy with HTLV-I infection: Variant form of HAM/TSP?
rewritten: Is chronic progressive cervical myelopathy associated with Human T-lymphotropic virus type I infection a variant form of HTLV-I-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis?
results.answer:
The abstracts indicate that HTLV-I infection is associated with slowly progressive myelopathy and abnormal cervical cord MRI lesions, suggesting a variant form of HAM/TSP. Patients with HTLV-I showed inflammatory changes and a high risk of developing HAM/TSP, supporting the idea that chronic progressive cervical myelopathy can be a variant of HAM/TSP.

yes
contexts: Clinical and neuroradiologic examinations were performed, and the odds that an HTLV-I-infected individual of specified genotype, age, and provirus load had HTLV-I-associated myelopathy (HAM (htlv-i-associated myelopathy))/tropical spastic paraparesis (TSP (tropical spastic paraparesis)) were calculated.

Anti-HTLV-I antibodies were positive in both the serum and the CSF in all of the patients. Biopsied sample from spinal cord lesions showed inflammatory changes in Patient 1. Patient 2 had a demyelinating type of sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Two of the three patients examined showed high risk of developing HAM (htlv-i-associated myelopathy)/TSP (tropical spastic paraparesis) in virologic and immunologic aspects.

To investigate the role of human T-lymphotrophic virus type I (HTLV-I) infection in four patients who developed slowly progressive myelopathy with abnormal MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) lesions in the cervical cord levels.

Hepatitis G virus can cause chronic infection in man but the role of this agent in chronic liver disease is poorly understood. Little is known about the relation of another newly discovered agent, the TT virus, with chronic liver disease.AIM: To investigate the rate of infection with hepatitis G virus and TT virus in patients with cryptogenic chronic liver disease.

Two common causes of cervical myelopathy include degenerative stenosis and ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament)). It has been postulated that patients with OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament) have more complications and worse outcomes than those with degenerative stenosis. The authors sought to compare the surgical results of laminoplasty in the treatment of cervical stenosis with myelopathy due to either degenerative changes or segmental OPLL (of the posterior longitudinal ligament).
results.reference: These four cases may belong to a variant form of HAM/TSP, predominantly involving the cervical cord levels.

results.question: Gender difference in survival of resected non-small cell lung cancer: histology-related phenomenon?
rewritten: Are there gender differences in survival outcomes of surgically resected non-small cell lung cancer patients, and is this disparity influenced by tumor histological subtype?
results.answer:
The provided data indicate that women have better overall 5-year survival than men in adenocarcinoma cases of resected non-small cell lung cancer, particularly in pathologic stage I and stage II or higher. However, in non-adenocarcinoma cases, there is no significant gender difference in survival. This suggests that the gender difference in survival is related to histology.

yes
contexts: It remains controversial whether there is a gender difference in survival of patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer.

We retrospectively analyzed 2770 patients (1689 men and 1081 women) with non-small cell lung cancer who underwent pulmonary resection between 1995 and 2005 at the National Cancer Center Hospital, Tokyo. A gender difference in survival was studied in all patients, in those divided according to histology or pathologic stage, and in propensity-matched gender pairs.

From 1993 to 1999, 667 patients received curative lung resection and complete hilar and mediastinal lymphadenectomy for non-small cell lung cancer. Of these, there were 436 Stage I disease (65%), of whom 144 T1N0 and 292 T2N0. No patients had pre- or postoperative radio- or chemotherapy. Prognostic significance of the following independent variables was tested using univariate (log-rank) and multivariate (Cox proportional-hazards) analysis: type of resection (sublobar vs lobectomy vs pneumonectomy), histology (squamous cell vs adenocarcinoma), tumour size (<or=3cm vs>3cm), histologic vascular invasion, visceral pleura involvement, positive bronchial resection margin, general T status.
We review our results on surgical treatment of patients with stage I non-small cell lung carcinoma and we attempted to clarify the prognostic significance of some surgical--pathologic variables.

There were no differences in background, such as preoperative pulmonary function, operation procedures, or operative mortality. The proportions of adenocarcinoma and pathologic stage I in women were greater than those in men (93.6% vs 61.7% and 71.4% vs 58.6%, respectively) (P<.001). Overall 5-year survival of women was better than that of men (81% vs 70%, P<.001). In adenocarcinoma, the overall 5-year survival for women was better than that for men in pathologic stage I (95% vs 87%, P<.001) and in pathologic stage II or higher (58% vs 51%, P = .017). In non-adenocarcinoma, there was no significant gender difference in survival in pathologic stage I (P = .313) or pathologic stage II or higher (P = .770). The variables such as age, smoking status, histology, and pathologic stage were used for propensity score matching, and survival analysis of propensity score-matched gender pairs did not show a significant difference (P = .69).
results.reference: Women had better survival than men; however, there was no survival advantage in propensity-matched gender pairs. A gender difference in survival was observed only in the adenocarcinoma subset, suggesting pathobiology in adenocarcinoma in women might be different from that of men.

results.question: Is lumbar drainage of postoperative cerebrospinal fluid fistula after spine surgery effective?
rewritten: Is lumbar cerebrospinal fluid drainage effective for the management of postoperative cerebrospinal fluid fistula following spinal surgery?
results.answer:
The context from abstract [2] describes 16 patients with postoperative CSF fistulas after spine surgery, where ten patients were treated with external CSF lumbar drainage for ten days. The study implies that lumbar drainage was used as a therapeutic strategy based on clinical conditions, suggesting it is an effective treatment option. Although detailed outcomes are not provided, the use of lumbar drainage as a treatment indicates its effectiveness in managing postoperative CSF fistulas.

yes
contexts: A 52-year-old woman underwent a craniotomy for a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm. A computed tomography scan showed that SAH (subarachnoid hemorrhage) existed predominantly in the posterior fossa and subdural hematoma beneath the cerebellar tentorium. Intrathecal administration of urokinase, IV administration of fasudil hydrochloride, and continuous cerebrospinal fluid (CSF (cerebrospinal fluid)) evacuation via cisternal drainage were performed as prophylactic treatments for vasospasm. On the sixth postoperative day, the patient complained of severe lower back and buttock pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a subdural hematoma in the lumbosacral region. Although the mass effect was extensive, the patient showed no neurologic symptoms other than the sciatica. She was treated conservatively. The hematoma dissolved gradually and had diminished completely 15 weeks later. Her pain gradually subsided, and she was discharged 7 weeks later without any neurologic deficit.

Postoperative CSF fistulas were described in 16 of 198 patients (8%) who underwent spine surgery between 2009 and 2010. The choice of the therapeutic strategy was based on the clinical condition of the patients, taking into account the possibility to maintain the prone position continuously and the risk of morbidity due to prolonged bed rest. Six patients were treated conservatively (position prone for three weeks), ten patients were treated by positioning an external CSF lumbar drainage for ten days. The mean follow-up period was ten months.
To determine whether shaving the incision site before spinal surgery causes postsurgical infection.

Little is known about whether a routinely inserted endoscopic nasobiliary drainage (ENBD (endoscopic nasobiliary drainage)) tube improves the clinical course in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced acute cholangitis after clearance of choledocholithiasis.

To validate the prognostic value of the acute phase sacral sparing measurements with regard to chronic phase-independent ambulation in patients with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI (spinal cord injury)).
results.reference: Lumbar drainage seems to be effective and safe both in preventing CSF fistula in cases of large dural tears and debilitated/irradiated patients and in treating CSF leaks.

results.question: Is obesity a risk factor for wheezing among adolescents?
rewritten: Is obesity an independent risk factor for wheezing and asthma symptoms in adolescent populations?
results.answer:
The provided study shows that obesity at 11 years of age is associated with a 50% greater prevalence of wheezing at 15 years and a higher risk of persistent wheezing, independent of confounding factors. This indicates that obesity is a significant risk factor for wheezing among adolescents.

yes
contexts: To investigate the effect of obesity at the start of adolescence on the prevalence, incidence and maintenance of chest wheezing among individuals aged 11-15 years in a birth cohort in a developing country.

The seventh follow-up of the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort occurred in 2004 (individuals aged 10-11 years). Between January and August 2008, the eighth follow-up of the cohort was conducted. All the individuals of the original cohort who were alive (who were then adolescents aged between 14 and 15 years) were targets for the study. The International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC (international study of asthma and allergies in childhood)) questionnaire was used to define wheezing. In addition to the body mass index (BMI (body mass index)), used to define obesity by the World Health Organization (WHO (world health organization)) criteria, we assessed skinfold thickness.

From the original cohort, 4,349 individuals were located (85.7% follow-up rate). The prevalence of chest wheezing at 11 and 15 years were 13.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 12.5%-14.5%) and 12.1% (95% CI (confidence interval): 11.1%-13.1%), respectively. The prevalence of wheezing at both times was 4.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 3.9%-5.1%) and the incidence of wheezing was 7.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 6.7%-8.3%). Independent of the effect of various confounding variables, the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was 50% greater among obese individuals than among eutrophic individuals at 11 years (RR (relative risk) 1.53; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.14-2.05). The greater the skinfold tertile at 11 years, the higher the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was (p = .011). Weight status and skinfolds did not present any association with incident wheezing. After controlling for confounding factors, the risk of persistent wheezing among obese individuals at 11 years was 1.82 (95% CI (confidence interval): 1.30-2.54).

To investigate if fetal gender (1) affects the risk of having an emergency department (ED (emergency department)) visit for asthma; and (2) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women who had at least one visit to the ED (emergency department) for asthma during pregnancy.

It has been suggested that increasing obesity levels in young women lead to intrauterine environments that, in turn, stimulate increased obesity among their offspring, generating an intergenerational acceleration of obesity levels. If this mechanism is important, the association of maternal body mass index (BMI (body mass index)) with offspring BMI (body mass index) should be stronger than the association of paternal with offspring BMI (body mass index).
results.reference: Since obesity at the start of adolescence is associated with asthma symptom persistence, prevention and treatment of obesity may reduce avoidable healthcare costs and disease burden.

results.question: Dose end-tidal carbon dioxide measurement correlate with arterial carbon dioxide in extremely low birth weight infants in the first week of life?
rewritten: Does end-tidal carbon dioxide measurement correlate with arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide in extremely low birth weight neonates during the first week of life?
results.answer:
The data from the study on 31 extremely low birth weight infants showed a significant correlation between end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2) and arterial CO2 (PaCO2), with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.81. Although EtCO2 values were generally lower than PaCO2, the capnographic method identified 84% of instances where PaCO2 was within a clinically relevant range, indicating a good correlation in the first week of life.

yes
contexts: To study the correlation and agreement between end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) and arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO(2)) in ventilated extremely low birth weight (ELBW (extremely low birth weight)) infants in the first week of life.

There were 754 end-tidal and arterial CO(2) pairs from 31 ELBW (extremely low birth weight) infants (21 male and 10 female). The overall EtCO(2) values were significantly lower than PaCO(2) value. In only 89/754(11.8%) pairs, the EtCO(2) was higher than the PaCO(2). The overall bias was 5.6 +/- 6.9 mmHg (95% C.I. 5.11-6.09). The intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.81. Using EtCO2 ranges of 30 to 50 mmHg, the capnographic method was able to identify 84% of instances where PaCO(2) was between 35 (<35 = hypocarbia) and 55 mmHg (>55= hypercapnia).

We performed a prospective cohort study in an obese population. Measurements of obesity were made, OSA (obstructive sleep apnoea) severity was recorded, and the 95th centile autoCPAP pressure was recorded during 1 week of autoCPAP. Spearman's rank correlation was performed between measurements of obesity and autoCPAP pressure, and between OSA (obstructive sleep apnoea) severity and autoCPAP pressure.

We operated on 613 children, including 97 neonates. Intraoperative extubation was achieved in 71% of the cases and early extubation (≤ 24 hours) was achieved in 89% of the cases. The overall mortality was 1.5% (9 of 613 patients). Early extubation was associated with lower mortality (1% vs 9%, P<.001) and a lower rate of reintubation (4% vs 23%, P<.001) compared with delayed extubation. Notably, 63% of the neonates were extubated within 24 hours, including 67% of arterial switch operations and 54% of total anomalous pulmonary venous return repairs. Norwood operations were the only procedure in which no patient was extubated within the first 24 hours. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that the predictors of delayed extubation included preoperative mechanical ventilation, weight<5 kg, a longer procedure time, and the need for postoperative inotrope support. Implementation of an early extubation strategy was associated with low rates of complications (5.1 per 10 procedures), short lengths of intensive care unit stay (median, 1 day; interquartile range, 1-3), and short hospital stays (median, 4 days; interquartile range, 3-6).

Seventeen children with ARDS (acute respiratory distress syndrome) and malignancy aged 10.5 +/- 5.1 years were identified. Six of the 17 children (35.3%) survived. Sepsis syndrome was present in 70.6% of all the children. Peak inspiratory pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure)), and ventilation index values could distinguish outcome by day 3. A significant relationship between respiratory data and outcome related to efficiency of oxygenation, as determined by PaO(2)/FIO(2) and P(A-a)O(2), was present from day 8 after onset of mechanical ventilation.
results.reference: There is good correlation and agreement between end-tidal CO(2) and arterial CO(2) in ELBW infants in the EtCO(2) range 30-50 mmHg. End-tidal CO(2) monitoring can be helpful in trending or for screening abnormal PaCO(2) values in ELBW infants in first week of life.

results.question: Is CA72-4 a useful biomarker in differential diagnosis between ovarian endometrioma and epithelial ovarian cancer?
rewritten: Is carbohydrate antigen 72-4 (CA72-4) a reliable biomarker for the differential diagnosis between ovarian endometrioma and epithelial ovarian carcinoma?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that CA125 is elevated in both ovarian endometriosis and ovarian cancer, making it not useful for differentiation. However, CA72-4 levels were significantly higher in ovarian cancer patients (71.0%) compared to those with endometriosis (13.8%), suggesting that CA72-4 could help distinguish between the two conditions. Therefore, CA72-4 appears to be a useful biomarker for differential diagnosis.

yes
contexts: Surgical excision of ovarian endometriomas in patients desiring pregnancy has recently been criticized because of the risk of damage to healthy ovarian tissue and consequent reduction of ovarian reserve. A correct diagnosis in cases not scheduled for surgery is therefore mandatory in order to avoid unexpected ovarian cancer misdiagnosis. Endometriosis is often associated with high levels of CA125. This marker is therefore not useful for discriminating ovarian endometrioma from ovarian malignancy. The aim of this study was to establish if the serum marker CA72-4 could be helpful in the differential diagnosis between ovarian endometriosis and epithelial ovarian cancer.
Serums CA125 and CA72-4 were measured in 72 patients with ovarian endometriomas and 55 patients with ovarian cancer.

High CA125 concentrations were observed in patients with ovarian endometriosis and in those with ovarian cancer. A marked difference in CA72-4 values was observed between women with ovarian cancer (71.0%) and patients with endometriosis (13.8%) (P<0.0001).

To determine survival among patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma)) who underwent a second-look laparotomy (SLL (second-look laparotomy)) and those refusing the procedure. Also to analyze factor(s) influencing the survival of the patients.

Medical records were reviewed of patients with advanced EOC (epithelial ovarian carcinoma) who were clinically free of disease after primary surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy between January 1, 1992, and December 31, 1998. All of them were offered SLL (second-look laparotomy). Measurement outcomes include patient survival and disease-free survival.
results.reference: This study suggests that CA72-4 determination can be useful to confirm the benign nature of ovarian endometriomas in women with high CA125 levels.

results.question: Preservation of the PCL when performing cruciate-retaining TKA: Is the tibial tuberosity a reliable predictor of the PCL footprint location?
rewritten: Is the tibial tuberosity a reliable anatomical landmark for predicting the posterior cruciate ligament footprint location during cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty?
results.answer:
The studies indicate that the tibial tuberosity can be used as a referencing landmark to estimate the PCL footprint height prior to tibial cut, with measured vertical distances showing a consistent relationship between the tibial tuberosity and the PCL footprint. This suggests that the tibial tuberosity is a reliable predictor for preserving the PCL during cruciate-retaining TKA.

yes
contexts: Reconstruction of the joint line is crucial in total knee arthroplasty (TKA (total knee arthroplasty)). A routine height of tibial cut to maintain the natural joint line may compromise the preservation of the PCL. Since the PCL footprint is not accessible prior to tibial osteotomy, it seems beneficial to identify a reliable extraarticular anatomic landmark for predicting the PCL footprint and being visible within standard TKA (total knee arthroplasty) approach. The fibula head predicts reliably the location of PCL footprint; however, it is not accessible during TKA (total knee arthroplasty). The aim of this study now was to analyze whether the tibial tuberosity can serve as a reliable referencing landmark to estimate the PCL footprint height prior to tibial cut.

The first consecutive case series included 216 CR TKA (total knee arthroplasty). Standing postoperative lateral view radiographs were utilized to measure the vertical distance between tibial tuberosity and tibial osteotomy plane. In the second case series, 223 knee MRIs were consecutively analyzed to measure the vertical distance between tibial tuberosity and PCL footprint. The probability of partial or total PCL removal was calculated for different vertical distances between tibial tuberosity and tibial cutting surface.

The vertical distance between the tibial tuberosity and tibial cut averaged 24.7 ± 4 mm. The average vertical distance from tibial tuberosity to proximal and to distal PCL footprint was found to be 22 ± 4.4 and 16 ± 4.4 mm, respectively. Five knees were considered at 50% risk of an entire PCL removal after CR TKA (total knee arthroplasty).

Six human cadaver knees were tested before implantation, after implantation with a bicruciate-retaining unicompartmental knee prosthesis, and after implantation with a posterior cruciate-retaining tricompartmental knee prosthesis. The unicompartmental prosthesis was initially implanted, and it was then revised to a total condylar knee replacement. The knee kinematics were measured with use of an electromagnetic tracking device while the knee was put through dynamic simulated stair-climbing under peak flexion moments of approximately 40 N-m. Quadriceps tension was also measured for all three conditions.

No significant differences in tibial axial rotation were noted between the intact and unicompartmental conditions. However, tricompartmental replacement significantly affected tibial axial rotation (p = 0.001). Femoral rollback was not significantly affected by either unicompartmental or tricompartmental arthroplasty. Quadriceps tension was also similar among all three conditions.
results.reference: Current surgical techniques of tibial preparation may result in partial or total PCL damage. Tibial tuberosity is a useful anatomical landmark to locate the PCL footprint and to predict the probability of its detachment pre-, intra-, and postoperatively. This knowledge might be useful to predict and avoid instability, consecutive pain, and dissatisfaction after TKA related to PCL insufficiency.

results.question: The English antibiotic awareness campaigns: did they change the public's knowledge of and attitudes to antibiotic use?
rewritten: Have the antibiotic stewardship campaigns in England effectively improved public knowledge and attitudes towards appropriate antibiotic use?
results.answer:
The English antibiotic awareness campaigns led to a small increase in the recollection of campaign posters and more frequent advice to use other remedies for coughs and colds, but there was no detected improvement in understanding the lack of benefit of antibiotics for coughs and colds or in antibiotic use. Therefore, the campaigns did not change the public's knowledge of and attitudes to antibiotic use in a meaningful way.

no
contexts: To determine the effect of the 2008 English public antibiotic campaigns.

English and Scottish (acting as controls) adults aged>or = 15 years were questioned face to face about their attitudes to and use of antibiotics, in January 2008 (1888) before and in January 2009 (1830) after the antibiotic campaigns.

Among English respondents, there was a small increase in recollection of campaign posters (2009 23.7% versus 2008 19.2%; P = 0.03), but this increase was only 2.3% higher in England than in Scotland. We did not detect any improvement in either England or Scotland, or any differences between England and Scotland in the understanding of the lack of benefit of antibiotics for coughs and colds, and we found no improvement in antibiotic use. We detected a significant increase in respondents retaining leftover antibiotics. Over 20% reported discussing antibiotics with their general practitioner (GP (general practitioner)) or nurse in the year to January 2009. The offer of a delayed antibiotic prescription was reported significantly more often by English respondents (19% versus 8% Scottish in 2009; P = 0.01), and English respondents were advised to use other remedies for coughs and colds significantly more often in the year to January 2009 (12.7% in 2009 versus 7.4% in 2008; P<0.001).

Eight of the 13 midwives at the two MOUs (midwife obstetric units) completed the PEP (perinatal education programme) and all demonstrated an improvement in knowledge. Case notes of 303 patients from the various clinics were studied. There was no change in the referral patterns of any of the clinics during the study period. The obstetric history was well documented, but in no group was there a satisfactory response to a detected problem; appropriate action was taken in between 0% and 12% of cases. Syphilis testing was performed in 56-82% of cases, with no difference between the groups. The haemoglobin level was measured in only 4-15% of patients, with no difference before or after completion of the PEP (perinatal education programme). Where a problem in uterine growth was detected, an appropriate response occurred in 0-8% of patients and no difference before or after completion of the PEP (perinatal education programme) was ascertained. In all groups, estimation of fetal weight and pelvimetry were seldom performed, the urine and fetal heart rate documentation were moderately well done and the blood pressure monitoring, assessment of head above pelvis, monitoring of contractions and plotting of cervical dilatation were usually performed. No differences before or after the PEP (perinatal education programme) were detected. Where problems were detected, appropriate actions taken during labour improved, but not significantly.

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.
results.reference: There is little evidence that the 2008 public antibiotic campaigns were effective. The use and visibility of future campaign materials needs auditing. A carefully planned approach that targets the public in GP waiting rooms and through clinicians in consultations may be a more effective way of improving prudent antibiotic use.

results.question: Does increased nerve length within the treatment volume improve trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery?
rewritten: Does increased trigeminal nerve length within the radiosurgical treatment volume improve clinical outcomes in trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery?
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1]-[3] tested whether increasing nerve length within the treatment volume improves pain relief in trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery. The results showed that pain relief was identical for one- and two-isocenter radiosurgery, indicating no improvement with increased nerve length. However, complications correlated with nerve length irradiated, but this does not imply improved pain relief.

no
contexts: To test the hypothesis that increasing the nerve length within the treatment volume for trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery would improve pain relief.

Eighty-seven patients with typical trigeminal neuralgia were randomized to undergo retrogasserian gamma knife radiosurgery (75 Gy maximal dose with 4-mm diameter collimators) using either one (n = 44) or two (n = 43) isocenters. The median follow-up was 26 months (range 1-36).

Pain relief was complete in 57 patients (45 without medication and 12 with low-dose medication), partial in 15, and minimal in another 15 patients. The actuarial rate of obtaining complete pain relief (with or without medication) was 67.7% +/- 5.1%. The pain relief was identical for one- and two-isocenter radiosurgery. Pain relapsed in 30 of 72 responding patients. Facial numbness and mild and severe paresthesias developed in 8, 5, and 1 two-isocenter patients vs. 3, 4, and 0 one-isocenter patients, respectively (p = 0.23). Improved pain relief correlated with younger age (p = 0.025) and fewer prior procedures (p = 0.039) and complications (numbness or paresthesias) correlated with the nerve length irradiated (p = 0.018).

This retrospective evaluation consisted of a consecutive series of patients who underwent TMJ (temporomandibular joint) surgeries through the VMPA (vascular-guided multilayer preauricular approach) from January through December 2013. Patients with a history of TMJ (temporomandibular joint) surgery were excluded. Clinical data, including operating times, subjective complaints of incision scars, functional conditions of the auriculotemporal nerve and facial nerve, and other complications, were recorded and analyzed. All patients in this study were followed for at least 6 months.

The purpose of this study was to determine whether operative volume outweighs the advantages of being treated locally by comparing the outcomes of patients with rectal cancer treated at local, low-volume centers versus far, high-volume centers.
results.reference: Increasing the treatment volume to include a longer nerve length for trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery does not significantly improve pain relief but may increase complications.

results.question: Is the affinity column-mediated immunoassay method suitable as an alternative to the microparticle enzyme immunoassay method as a blood tacrolimus assay?
rewritten: Is the affinity column-mediated immunoassay method a suitable alternative to the microparticle enzyme immunoassay method for quantifying tacrolimus concentrations in blood samples?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that tacrolimus concentrations measured by the ACMIA method closely correlate with those measured by the MEIA method (r = 0.84) and that there are no specific trends in differences between the two methods. Although the difference between methods tends to be larger in low hematocrit samples, overall, the ACMIA method appears comparable and not influenced by hematocrit levels, supporting its suitability as an alternative assay.

yes
contexts: Tacrolimus concentrations measured by the ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay) method (n = 154) closely correlated with those measured by the MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay) method (r = 0.84). The Bland-Altman plot using concentration differences between the 2 methods and the average of the 2 methods showed no specific trends. The tacrolimus levels determined by both the MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay) method and the ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay) method were not influenced by hematocrit levels, but the difference between the 2 methods (ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay) - MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay)) tended to be larger in low hematocrit samples (P<.001).

Tacrolimus is a potent immunosuppressive drug used in organ transplantation. Because of its substantial toxic effects, narrow therapeutic index, and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability, therapeutic drug monitoring of whole-blood tacrolimus concentrations has been recommended. We investigated the comparability of the results of 2 immunoassay systems, affinity column-mediated immunoassay (ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay)) and microparticle enzyme immunoassay (MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay)), comparing differences in the tacrolimus concentrations measured by the 2 methods in relation to the hematologic and biochemical values of hepatic and renal functions.

A total of 154 samples from kidney or liver transplant recipients were subjected to Dimension RxL HM with a tacrolimus Flex reagent cartilage for the ACMIA (affinity column-mediated immunoassay) method and IMx tacrolimus II for the MEIA (microparticle enzyme immunoassay) method.

405 tests were performed. Comparison between results obtained in the practices and those in the reference hospital laboratory (gold standard), which used the same method of testing for INR (international normalized ratio), showed a correlation coefficient of 0.96. Correlation coefficients comparing the results with the various standard laboratory techniques ranged from 0.86 to 0.92. It was estimated that up to 53% of tests would have resulted in clinically significant differences (change in warfarin dose) depending upon the site and method of testing. The practice derived results showed a positive bias ranging from 0.28 to 1.55, depending upon the site and method of testing.

We found that similar concentrations of chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine suppress the T-cell response to MiHC in mice (C57BL/6 anti-BALB.B) and that lysosomotropic amines in combination with cyclosporine result in synergistic suppression of a proliferative response to MiHC. Similar suppression and synergy appear to be present in an alloreactive response (C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c). Direct inhibition by chloroquine of T-cell proliferative responses induced by anti-CD3epsilon in the absence of antigen-presenting cells is present at higher concentrations than that required to suppress responses to MiHC or MHC (major histocompatibility complex). Chloroquine appears to induce decreased T-cell viability at high concentrations. This effect does not appear to be due to decreased T-cell production of interleukin-2 or interferon-gamma. At lower concentrations (<25 microg/ml), chloroquine can also decrease the ability of antigen-presenting cells to stimulate an a C57BL/6 anti-BALB/c T-cell response and can inhibit MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class II expression after activation with lipopolysaccharide.
results.reference: The ACMIA method used for a tacrolimus assay is precise and has advantages, including the lack of a required pretreatment procedure. Furthermore, it is only slightly influenced by the hematologic or biochemical status of the samples.

results.question: Should tumor depth be included in prognostication of soft tissue sarcoma?
rewritten: Should tumor invasion depth be included as a prognostic factor in the clinical outcome prediction of patients with soft tissue sarcoma?
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that tumor depth does not have a major independent prognostic effect when tumor grade and size are accounted for, as deep tumors tend to be larger, which explains their worse prognosis. However, tumor depth may influence prognosis in the subset of high-grade, large tumors due to their larger size. Overall, tumor depth itself is not an independent prognostic factor.

no
contexts: Most staging systems for soft tissue sarcoma are based on histologic malignancy-grade, tumor size and tumor depth. These factors are generally dichotomized, size at 5 cm. We believe it is unlikely that tumor depth per se should influence a tumor's metastatic capability. Therefore we hypothesized that the unfavourable prognostic importance of depth could be explained by the close association between size and depth, deep-seated tumors on average being larger than the superficial ones. When tumor size is dichotomized, this effect should be most pronounced in the large size (>5 cm) group in which the size span is larger.

We analyzed the associations between tumor size and depth and the prognostic importance of grade, size and depth in a population-based series of 490 adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma of the extremity or trunk wall with complete, 4.5 years minimum, follow-up.

Multivariate analysis showed no major prognostic effect of tumor depth when grade and size were taken into account. The mean size of small tumors was the same whether superficial or deep but the mean size of large and deep-seated tumors were one third larger than that of large but superficial tumors. Tumor depth influenced the prognosis in the subset of high-grade and large tumors. In this subset deep-seated tumors had poorer survival rate than superficial tumors, which could be explained by the larger mean size of the deep-seated tumors.

In the study, 1897 patients (35.5%) were classified as pT1a, 1453 (27%) as pT1b, 437 (8%) as pT2a, 153 (3%) as pT2b, 1059 (20%) as pT3a, 117 (2%) as pT3b, 26 (0.5%) as pT3c, and 197 (4%) as pT4. At a median follow-up of 42 mo, 786 (15%) had died of disease. In univariable analysis, patients with pT2b and pT3a tumors had similar CSS (cancer-specific survival), as did patients with pT3c and pT4 tumors. Moreover, both pT3a and pT3b stages included patients with heterogeneous outcomes. In multivariable analysis, the novel classification of the primary tumor was a powerful independent predictor of CSS (p for trend<0.0001). However, the substratification of pT1 tumors did not retain an independent predictive role. The major limitations of the study are retrospective design, lack of central pathologic review, and the small number of patients included in some substages.

We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) plus radical surgery.
results.reference: Most of the prognostic value of tumor depth in soft tissue sarcomas of the extremity or trunk wall can be explained by the association between tumor size and depth.

results.question: Is amoxapine an atypical antipsychotic?
rewritten: Is amoxapine classified as an atypical antipsychotic medication in psychiatric pharmacology?
results.answer:
The abstracts describe atypical antipsychotics (AAPs) as having high serotonin 5-HT2 occupancy and greater 5-HT2 than dopamine D2 occupancy. Abstract [2] suggests that amoxapine should conform to this pharmacologic profile and was studied for its 5-HT2 and D2 occupancy, implying it shares characteristics with atypical antipsychotics. However, none of the abstracts explicitly label amoxapine as an atypical antipsychotic.

no
contexts: Several atypical antipsychotics (AAPs (atypical antipsychotics)) are used as second-line agents for treatment resistant depression. AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) can be expensive compared to other treatment options and can cause several side effects.

All currently available atypical antipsychotics have, at clinically relevant doses: i) high serotonin (5-HT)2 occupancy; ii) greater 5-HT2 than dopamine (D)2 occupancy; and iii) a higher incidence of extrapyramidal side effects when their D2 occupancy exceeds 80%. A review of pharmacologic and behavioral data suggested that amoxapine should also conform to this profile; therefore, we undertook a positron-emission tomography (PET (positron-emission tomography)) study of its 5-HT2 and D2 occupancy.
Seven healthy volunteers received 50-250 mg/day of amoxapine for 5 days and then had [11C]-raclopride and [18F]-setoperone PET (positron-emission tomography) scans.
To estimate healthcare costs and utilization of AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) compared to other second-line agents.

Although body dysmorphic disorder (BDD (body dysmorphic disorder)) is classified in DSM-III-R as a nonpsychotic somatoform disorder, controversy exists as to whether BDD (body dysmorphic disorder) can present with psychotic features. If it can, this raises the possibility that its DSM-III-R psychotic counterpart-delusional disorder, somatic type--may not be a separate disorder. The purpose of this study was to determine whether patients with nonpsychotic BDD (defined according to DSM-III-R criteria, i.e., with maintenance of some insight) were different from patients with psychotic BDD (those whose preoccupation was without insight and of delusional intensity).
results.reference: PET data show that amoxapine's profile is very similar to that of the established atypical antipsychotics. These data, together with amoxapine's in vitro pharmacologic profile, effectiveness in animal models, and efficacy in psychotic depression raise the possibility of amoxapine as an "atypical" antipsychotic agent in the treatment of schizophrenia.

results.question: Does topical N-acetylcysteine application after myringotomy cause severe otorrhea?
rewritten: Does topical application of N-acetylcysteine after myringotomy surgery cause severe otorrhea or increased ear discharge?
results.answer:
The provided context states that in the group treated with topical N-acetylcysteine after tympanic membrane perforations, only 40% of perforations were completely closed by day nine, and the remaining ears exhibited otorrhea by the third day. results.question: Is non-HDL-cholesterol a better predictor of long-term outcome in patients after acute myocardial infarction compared to LDL-cholesterol?
rewritten: Is non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol a superior predictor of long-term cardiovascular outcomes compared to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in patients following acute myocardial infarction?
results.answer:
The study in the provided abstracts shows that non-HDL cholesterol levels >130 mg/dl were associated with a higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after acute myocardial infarction, while surprisingly, LDL cholesterol >100 mg/dl was associated with a reduced risk of MACE compared to LDL <70 mg/dl. This suggests that non-HDL cholesterol is a better predictor of long-term outcomes after AMI than LDL cholesterol in this patient population.

contexts: It has recently been shown that non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C) may be a better predictor of cardiovascular risk than low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C). We retrospectively obtained the data of all patients who were admitted at Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai hospital due to AMI (acute myocardial infarction) during 2006-2013. The mean non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C and LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C during long-term follow-up were used to predict MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) at each time point. The patients were classified as target attainment if non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C <100 mg/dl and/or LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C <70 mg/dl. The MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) was defined as combination of all-cause death, nonfatal coronary event and nonfatal stroke.

During mean follow-up of 2.6 ± 1.6 years among 868 patients after AMI (acute myocardial infarction), 34.4% achieved non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C target, 23.7% achieved LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C target and 21.2% experienced MACEs. LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C and non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C were directly compared in Cox regression model. Surprisingly, LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C >100 mg/dl was associated with reduced risk of MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) as compared to LDL (low density lipoprotein) <70 mg/dl (HR 0.42, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.18-0.98, p = 0.046) after direct pairwise comparison with non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C level.

results.question: Is intrapartum vibroacoustic stimulation an effective predictor of fetal acidosis?
rewritten: Is intrapartum vibroacoustic stimulation an effective diagnostic tool for predicting fetal metabolic acidosis during labor?
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate a strong association between fetal heart rate acceleration response to intrapartum vibroacoustic stimulation (VAS) and normal fetal pH (≥7.20), as well as between a negative VAS response and fetal acidosis (pH <7.20). This relationship holds across different labor stages and types of decelerations, with significant predictive values for fetal acidosis and neonatal morbidity. Therefore, intrapartum VAS appears to be an effective predictor of fetal acidosis.

yes
contexts: The hypothesis of this prospective study is that intrapartum vibroacoustic stimulation (VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation)) is an effective predictor of fetal acidosis during labor. Various clinical conditions, such as term versus preterm gestation, first stage versus second stage of labor, and fetal heart rate (FHR (fetal heart rate)) variable decelerations versus late decelerations will be tested.

Excellent association between acceleration response to VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) and pH>or = 7.20, and between a negative response to VAS (no acceleration or decelerations) and pH<7.20 were found in the first stage of labor, the second stage of labor, and the combination of both stages together (p = 0.0001, OR = 10.6 [3.3-34.0]). It was observed that negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) responses for predicting fetal acidosis (pH<7.20) were comparable between term (>or = 37 weeks) and preterm (<37 weeks,>or = 34 weeks) fetuses. Since the preterm fetuses enrolled in the study were limited in number, it is difficult to draw adequate conclusions. The positive predictive value (PPV (positive predictive value)) of fetal acidosis was 67% in both groups of FHR (fetal heart rate) variable decelerations and late decelerations, but the false negative rate of acceleration VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response for predicting no acidosis was significantly higher in the group of late decelerations (29% vs 8%, p = 0.034). Finally, both a negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response and fetal acidosis (pH<7.20) have equal predictability for neonatal morbidity. The PPV (positive predictive value) of NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) admission by a negative VAS (vibroacoustic stimulation) response was two times higher than that of fetal acidosis (PPV (positive predictive value) = 61% vs 29%, p = 0.038).

results.reference: We found that intrapartum VAS was an effective predictor of fetal acidosis in cases of FHR variable decelerations, but its predictability for fetal acidosis in cases of FHR late decelerations was limited. Both VAS and fetal blood pH are good predictors of neonatal morbidity.

results.reference: The results of this study cast doubt on the importance of LOC as a predictor of neuropsychological test performance during the acute phase of recovery from mild traumatic brain injury. Neuropsychological testing procedures have been shown to be sensitive in measuring cognitive sequelae of mild traumatic brain injury (concussion) in athletes. The failure of this study to find any relationship between LOC and neuropsychological functioning in a large sample of patients with mild head trauma calls into question the assignment of primary importance to LOC in grading severity of concussion. This study also does not provide support for the use of guidelines that rely heavily on LOC in making return-to-play decisions. Continued research is necessary to determine the relative importance of markers of concussion in athletes.
